scenes.synopsis: Laurent, the eve — the Frenchman; the promise, tonight. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(He found her in the gallery, between the ancestors, an hour before the guests were due down. The Hartwells on the walls looked at him with the particular skepticism of oil paint, and he looked back at them like a man facing a tribunal he had chosen.)*
> *(The gallery at that hour held the day's last light in its tall windows, and the dust moved in it, slow, unbothered. Somewhere below, a door closed, and a footman's footsteps crossed the hall and faded. The house was holding its breath before the evening.)*
> "Tonight," Laurent said, without preamble.
> "Tonight," Rose agreed. "The old world's last night. You have said so four times today. The ancestors are beginning to take it personally."
> *(He smiled, but it was the thin one, the polish worn through at the edges.)* "I practiced my English on the drive up. Your steward corrected my pronunciation of 'extinguisher.'"
> "Harrow corrects everyone's pronunciation. It is his love language."
> "Then I am much loved." *(He took her hands. His were cold.)* "Rose. I have been the Frenchman in England for —" He counted, frowning. "It does not matter how long. It feels like a life. The accent, the shrug, the —" He made a small gesture that was somehow entirely Parisian and entirely tired. "Tonight it ends. Not the man. The performance."
> "You will still shrug," Rose said. "I have seen you shrug in your sleep."
> "In my sleep I am French. It is allowed." *(He lifted her hands and held them against his chest, over his heart, which was beating fast enough that she could feel it through his coat.)* "At midnight the mask comes off. Permanently. I will stand in your hall, unmasked, and choose England, and your émigré guests will write home about it, and Paris will be furious or relieved, and none of it will matter." He looked at her directly, the unpolished look, the true one. "What matters is that you believe me."
> "I believe you," Rose said.
> "Good." He breathed out. "Then I can survive the ancestors."
> *(He bowed to the nearest Hartwell, a small ironic bow, and went down to dress, and Rose stood among the painted Hartwells and listened to his footsteps go, and to her own heart, which was beating nearly as fast as his. The dust went on moving in the light, unbothered, and she thought that was the trick of it: to be unbothered, and to go on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the guests — Paris, arrived; the émigré houses, the old world. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The guests came at eight, and Rose watched them come from the long gallery's window, unobserved, still in her day dress, her hair not yet done. It was the hostess's privilege, this one hour of invisibility: to see the arrivals as a stranger would see them, before she became the evening's center.)*
> *(The carriages came up the drive in procession, lamps lit against the early dark. The émigré houses descended in their Parisian silks, the women with their jewel cases handed down like infants, the men straightening their orders on the steps. Harrow received them at the great doors with his ledger-calm, checking names against his list, directing footmen with small economical gestures. He had the evening's arithmetic entirely in hand, and Rose, watching, felt the particular peace of a household in competent hands.)*
> *(An old marquise paused on the steps and looked up at the house, and Rose saw her say something to her companion, and the companion nodded, and they went in together. A young French officer laughed at something, the sound carrying clear across the gravel. The English guests came among the French: neighbors, the ton, the curious, their carriages plainer, their jewels English. She watched a neighbor's wife descend carefully, holding her skirts clear of the wheel, and thought that arrivals were the most honest part of any evening: everyone still hoping, no one yet disappointed.)*
> *(She counted without meaning to: the carriages, the couples, the masks already tied on in the carriages, paint and silk flashing in the lamp light. Forty-one, forty-two. The old world, assembling for its farewell, and she the only soul in the house not yet dressed for it.)*
> *(Below, the great doors opened and closed, opened and closed. The hall filled with French. The night's first music — not the musicians yet, but the sound of arrival, talk and laughter rising like a tide — came up through the floorboards to where she stood.)*
> *(Her maid knocked, and came in, and laid out the ivory gown on the bed, and Rose turned from the window. The hour of invisibility was ending. The evening wanted its hostess, and the hostess had a mask to choose.)*

scenes.synopsis: the hall — the masquerade's stage; the old world's theater. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The hall at half past eight, before the company came down: the masquerade's stage, set. Rose walked its length alone, in the ivory gown now, her hair done, the mask not yet chosen — that waited in the morning room, on its white cloths — and the hall received her the way a theater receives its actress before the audience is admitted.)*
> *(Six hundred candles, lit. The stands by the east windows, the musicians' chairs empty, the instruments waiting. The masks on the gallery wall, all claimed now, the tags removed. The supper room beyond, under cloths. The chandelier's crystals threw small rainbows onto the empty floor, and her footsteps sounded loud and then not loud, the way footsteps do in a room built for music.)*
> *(She stood at its center and turned slowly, taking the stage's measure. This was the old world's theater, and tonight it would hold the old world's farewell. The French airs would come from the alcove. The dancers would turn where she stood. At midnight the masks would come off, and the faces underneath would blink in the candlelight, and Laurent's face among them, unmasked permanently.)*
> *(She thought of the S1 ball, ten seasons past: this hall, this chandelier, herself terrified at the stair's foot. The girl had not known the hall was a stage. The woman knew, and knew too that the stage was hers to set. The candles, the music, the supper, the guest list — the arithmetic of the night, all balanced, all hers.)*
> *(A footman crossed with a final branch of candles, and Harrow followed, checking, and Harrow saw her and bowed, and did not ask why the hostess was alone in her hall. Harrow understood the hour before the evening. Everyone who has ever run a house understands it: the stillness before the doors open. Above, the ancestors looked down from the gallery, oil-paint eyes on the empty floor, and Rose nodded to them, hostess to hosts, and they approved, or she chose to think so.)*
> *(She went up the stair then, to the morning room, where the three masks waited on their white cloths. The stage was set. The choosing remained.)*

scenes.synopsis: the music — the old world's; the masquerade's sound. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The music was warming up. Rose paused by the east alcove's doorway, unobserved, and listened to the musicians tune: the first violin's A, the cello's answering C, a flute trying a run and catching it. The thin man with the wart on his chin — the first violin — tapped his bow against his stand and they began a French air, quietly, for themselves, not yet for the hall.)*
> *(It was a gavotte, the one her dancing master had despaired of, and hearing it played soft, as a rehearsal, undid something in her. The old world's music, practicing its farewell. The émigré ladies would close their eyes when they heard it, she knew. A tune could do what words could not: carry a country across the water.)*
> *(The cellist smiled at something the flutist did, and they tried the passage again, and got it, and the first violin nodded, satisfied. They were good, these musicians. Harrow had chosen them, or the choice had been made by someone who understood that a farewell needs a tune you can hum.)*
> *(She thought of all the music of ten seasons: the S1 ball's nervous strings, the Vauxhall gala's brass, the Bath assembly's thin piano. This was different. This was the sound of the old world tuning itself for the last time, and she stood in the doorway and let it wash over her, the hostess not yet the hostess, the night not yet the night.)*
> *(The gavotte ended. The first violin tapped his bow. They began a musette air, sweet and a little sad, and Rose thought of Laurent upstairs, dressing, his letters to Paris written, his English practiced, and of how a tune could hold what he was leaving, and she let it hold her, there in the doorway, until Harrow's footsteps in the hall told her the company was coming down. The flutist caught her eye as she turned to go, and smiled, quick and shy, and she smiled back, and the musette air followed her up the stair like a hand waving.)*
> *(She slipped away before they saw her. The musicians played on, unaware, and the hall filled behind her with talk and silk, and the masquerade's sound became the night's.)*

scenes.synopsis: the unmasking's eve — the anticipation; midnight, approaching. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The ball began below without her, which was the hostess's prerogative and also her favorite part. Rose stood in the morning room with the three masks on their white cloths and listened to it assemble through the floorboards: the first proper French air, the dancers finding their places, the murmur rising like water coming to a boil.)*
> *(Midnight was two hours off. Two hours of silk and paint, and then the ribbons untied, and then whatever was underneath, blinking in the candlelight. Laurent's underneath first among them. She had believed him in the gallery with his heart hammering under her palm, and she believed him still, but belief, she was discovering, was not a door you walked through once. It was a lamp you trimmed every evening.)*
> *(Forty-two masks hung along the gallery wall for forty-two guests, Harrow's clerkly tags on every one. Hers were the only three laid out for choosing, which struck her as either an honor or a symptom. The old world's ritual: pick the face you wear to the farewell. The Frenchwomen would have opinions. Letitia would have several. Octavia would look at the three and say something precise about Rose that Rose had not yet said to herself, and be right, and Rose was in no hurry to hear it.)*
> *(On the dresser behind her lay the bouquet Élise had sent up at six: white lilies, blush roses, the ribbon long and loose. For midnight, Élise had said, tying the knot with chalk still on her fingers. You will want something to hold.)*
> *(She looked at the three silk faces. The triumph, quoted from the Season she had been twenty and terrified: ivory silk, the gold embroidery gone soft at the edges. The rose, blush silk massed with fabric roses at the temple, the Hartwell flower. The domino, black and unadorned, which told nothing and promised nothing and therefore told the truth.)*
> *(Below, somebody laughed — a real laugh, surprised out of someone — and Harrow's voice announced a late arrival, and the night turned on its heel without her, patient as a well-trained horse. It could wait. The entrance was hers to time, and the mask was hers to choose, and she intended to make the night wait a little longer for both.)*
> *(She touched the domino's cool silk, then the triumph's gold brow. Two hours. The candle flames stood straight in their sconces, not a draft in the room, as if the house itself were holding still to watch her decide.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE MASK (which mask Rose wears: the triumph quoted, the rose, or the domino plain). The night deepens; decide the mask. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The night deepened, and the masks waited on their white cloths in the morning room, and Rose stood before them the way a general regards three roads. The triumph, quoted: ivory silk, gold embroidery, the beginning's face. The rose: blush silk, the little fabric roses, the Hartwell legacy blooming at the temple. The domino, plain: black silk, unadorned, the woman's face with nothing on it.)*
> *(She had handled them at noon and set them aside, and the setting aside had been its own kind of choosing, a postponement dressed as deliberation. Now the ball was below her, the French airs coming up through the floor, and the night wanted its first statement.)*
> *(The triumph mask would say: I remember who I was. The beginning, quoted, the S1 girl become the woman, the past worn as proof. It would match the gown, ivory and gold, the quoted triumph head to foot. The old world would understand it at once. Everyone who remembered would understand.)*
> *(The rose mask would say: I am the Hartwell. The legacy, the house, the name, blooming. It would be the bolder choice, the blush against the ivory gown, the flower the house had bred across ten seasons. Letitia would approve. Augusta would approve. It would be a statement, and the night wanted a statement.)*
> *(The domino would say nothing, which was its own statement. Plain black silk. No quotation, no legacy. The woman, unadorned, at the old world's farewell. It would be the quietest face in the hall, and the truest, and nobody would understand it but her.)*
> *(She thought of Élise's hands, chalk-stained, tying the bouquet. She thought of Laurent's cold hands, his heart beating through his coat. She thought of midnight, two hours off, when all the masks would come off anyway, and the choosing would be revealed as what it was: a few hours' loan of a face.)*
> *(The French airs rose through the floor, sweet and insistent. The masks waited. The night held its breath, politely, the way the old world did everything.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The mask:*
- **The triumph, quoted** — *the beginning's mask.* Rose wears the S1 triumph's mask — the beginning, quoted. (Consequence: the quoting is the thesis — but beginnings are past, and the night wants the becoming.)
- **The rose** — *the legacy's mask.* Rose wears the Hartwell rose's mask — the legacy, blooming. (Consequence: the blooming is the statement — but legacies are weighty, and the masquerade wants lightness.)
- **The domino, plain** — *the woman's mask.* Rose wears the plain domino — unadorned, the woman's. (Consequence: the plainness is the truth — but plain is retiring, and the night wants the statement.)
> *(She reached out, and her hand hovered, and the candlelight moved over the three silk faces, and she chose.)*
> *(The mask settled over her own face, the ribbons tied behind, the silk cool and then warm. She looked in the glass over the mantel. The woman in the glass wore the night's first statement, and the statement was hers.)*
> *(Below, the ball turned on. She went down the stair to meet it, masked, and the old world's last night began in earnest.)*

scenes.synopsis: the entrance — masked; the old world, entering. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Her entrance was announced at half past ten, and the hall turned to watch, and for a moment the French airs seemed to play only for her. She came down the great stair in the ivory gown, quoted and transformed, the mask she had chosen tied neat behind her head, the quoted bouquet in her gloved hands.)*
> *(The old world entered with her. That was the trick of a great entrance: the room rearranges itself around the person descending, and the person descending pretends not to notice. Rose noticed everything. The marquise who had patted her cheek at eight now stared openly. A young English officer missed a step in the dance. Letitia, scarlet domino, applauded with her fan.)*
> *(She reached the hall's floor and the dancing resumed around her, and the night was begun, the farewell's. The candlelight found the gold embroidery of her gown and lit it from within. The white lilies of her bouquet were cool against her gloves, the blush roses among them the Hartwell's own.)*
> *(Laurent was across the hall, masked himself now, and even masked she knew him: the stance, the stillness at the center of the turning room. He bowed to her, the Frenchman's bow, and she inclined her head, and the hall saw the exchange and understood nothing and everything.)*
> *(Harrow materialized at her elbow, as Harrow did, from nowhere and exactly on time.)* "The entrance is complete, Miss Hartwell. The company is —" He searched for the word. "Moved."
> "The company is masked, Harrow. The company cannot be seen to be moved."
> "The company is moved behind its masks, miss." *(The dry smile, there and gone.)* "The supper room is ready. The champagne is cold. The night —" He glanced at the turning hall. "The night is yours, miss."
> *(She took a glass of champagne from a passing footman. It was properly cold. Somebody had seen to it. In a house running a masquerade for the old world's farewell, somebody always saw to the champagne, and Rose made a note to find out who and thank them, because the small things were the whole thing, and she had learned that the long way.)*
> *(The dancers turned, masked, the old world's, and she stood at the hall's center, masked as she had chosen, and let the night come to her.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dancing — masked; the old world's last dance. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(She danced. The mask she had chosen moved with her face, the ribbons holding, the silk breathing. Her partners were a succession of silk and paint: a French vicomte who danced as if the floor owed him money, an English squire's son who apologized to her slippers, Laurent twice, masked, his hand sure at her waist.)*
> *(The old world's last dance went on around her, the hall turning, the French airs. The women's skirts swung, the men's coats flared, the candlelight moved over it all. Somebody's mask slipped and was straightened with laughter. Somebody guessed somebody else wrongly and there was a shriek of delight.)*
> *(Rose thought, dancing, of the S1 ball: the terror, the newness, the feeling of being looked at by a hundred eyes and found wanting or not. Ten seasons later the hundred eyes were still there, and she was still being looked at, and the difference was that she had stopped minding. The mask helped. The ten seasons helped more.)*
> *(Between dances she stood by the pillar and drank champagne and watched. The émigré ladies danced with a particular grace, as if each dance were a small act of remembrance. The English danced with a particular energy, as if each dance were a small act of defiance. The hall held both, and the music held the hall.)*
> *(The vicomte, between dances, told her in rapid French about his estate in Normandy, lost, and his dancing, retained, and she gathered that the dancing was the greater consolation. The squire's son asked after the Park's roses and blushed when she answered. Laurent, the second time, said nothing at all, and the nothing was the best conversation of the evening.)*
> *(Octavia danced past with a French gentleman of a certain age, and caught Rose's eye over his shoulder, and mouthed, "The light," and Rose nodded, because the light was indeed perfect, the candles at their height, the faces true behind the paint.)*
> *(The clock in the hall said eleven. One hour to midnight. The dancing went on, masked, the old world's, and Rose danced in the middle of it, and the night was sweet, and the sweetness had an edge, like champagne.)*

scenes.synopsis: Laurent, masked — the Frenchman, the night's; the truth, underneath. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(He claimed her for the dance before midnight, and the hall made way for them the way halls do for couples it has decided to watch. Masked, the Frenchman, the night's, his hand at her waist sure and warm through the ivory silk.)*
> "The hall," he said as they turned, surveying it over her shoulder. "Full. The émigré —" A glance at the French contingent, laughing by the windows. "Paris, here. The old world —" Another glance, at the English. "One more night."
> "You have been counting," Rose said.
> "I count when I am nervous. It is a habit I learned from an Englishwoman." *(The mask's eyes smiled, or the eyes behind the mask did.)* "Midnight, Rose. The unmasking."
> "I know. You have mentioned it."
> "I will mention it again. It is the only subject I have." *(He spun her, neatly, and caught her, neatly, and the hall approved with a small sound.)* "The mask off. Permanently. England."
> "England," Rose said. "The Park. The future. Here. You practiced this."
> "I practiced it on the drive. Harrow corrected my pronunciation." *(A beat.)* "Of 'permanently.' He was right. I had the emphasis on the wrong syllable for a decade."
> *(She laughed, and the laugh was real, and the masked couple turning in the candlelight looked, to the watching hall, like the night's own emblem: the Frenchman and the Englishwoman, the old world and the new, dancing the last dance before the truth.)*
> *(The music slowed for the turn, and his hand tightened at her waist, barely, the only sign.)* "After midnight," he said quietly, "whatever the hall thinks, whatever Paris writes home —" He stopped. "You believe me. That is the whole of it."
> "I believe you," Rose said, for the second time that night, and meant it for the second time, which was easier and harder both.
> *(The music ended. He bowed over her hand, the Frenchman's bow, and held it a moment longer than the dance required.)*
> "Midnight," he said quietly.
> "Midnight," Rose said.
> *(He went back into the turning hall, masked, the night's, and the truth waited underneath, patient as a held breath.)*

scenes.synopsis: the intrigue — the masquerade's play; the old world's game. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The masquerade played its old game, and the hall played along. Masked flirtations bloomed and withered in the space of a dance. Guessed identities were traded like currency: "You are the Devonshires' cousin," "You are nobody's cousin," shrieks of laughter when the masks slipped just enough.)*
> *(Rose watched a young Frenchwoman spend an entire country dance trying to determine whether her partner was the man she had quarreled with in Paris in the spring, and fail, and decide she preferred not knowing. It seemed to Rose the wisest decision of the evening.)*
> *(Letitia held court by the windows in the scarlet domino, collecting guesses like tributes and denying everything. "I am the Duchess of Somewhere," she told a masked guardsman. "I am incognito. You may kiss my hand." The guardsman kissed her hand. Letitia looked over his shoulder at Rose and winked, the mask's eyeholes crinkling.)*
> *(It was the old world's game, the harmless one: who knows what, behind which mask. Nobody's fortune turned on it tonight. Nobody's heart broke. The stakes were champagne and laughter, and the hall paid them gladly.)*
> *(A masked lady addressed Rose as "ma chère" and told her, confidentially, that the Hartwell girl had done very well for herself, and Rose thanked her gravely, and the lady moved on, never knowing. Rose treasured the moment the way one treasures a good joke heard at one's own expense: completely. She caught Octavia's eye across the hall and mouthed, "The Hartwell girl," and Octavia's precise smile said she had heard, and was storing it.)*
> *(A young officer spent ten minutes trying to guess Harrow, who was unmasked and carrying his list, and Harrow endured it with the patience of a man who has been guessed at by better officers. "The butler," Harrow said at last, dryly, and the officer laughed until his mask slipped.)*
> *(The clock said a quarter to twelve. The intrigue went on, the guessed and the guessing, the masks, the play, and beneath it the anticipation sat quiet and certain: midnight, the unmasking, the game's end. The old world played its last hand with flair, and the hall loved it for it.)*

scenes.synopsis: the supper — masked; the old world's feast. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Supper was served at eleven, masked, in the long gallery, and it was the old world's feast: the French dishes, the champagne, the last night's table. The cooks had outdone themselves. There was a ham in champagne sauce that made a French marquise close her eyes. There were jellies that trembled in the candlelight like small captured skies. There was champagne, properly cold, in quantities that suggested the cellar had been given its head.)*
> *(Rose sat between a masked émigré and an unmasked English neighbor who had given up on his domino as a bad job, and ate, and listened. The talk was the old world's talk: Paris, London, who had married whom, who had lost what at cards, the price of everything and the value of nothing, all of it fond.)*
> *(The marquise who had patted Rose's cheek leaned across and said, in French too rapid to follow, something about the ham, and Rose nodded and smiled, and the marquise patted her hand, satisfied, and Rose decided that patting was this woman's entire conversational range, and that it was enough.)*
> *(Across the table Laurent was telling a story, masked, his hands moving, and his end of the table was laughing. He caught Rose's eye and raised his glass, and she raised hers, and the champagne was cold and sharp and perfect.)*
> *(The neighbor, unmasked and cheerful, told her the ham was the finest he had tasted since his wedding breakfast, and asked after the Park's roses, and confessed he had lost his domino in the cloakroom and felt liberated. "Under a hat, they tell me," he said. "My mask was under a hat. There is a moral there, Miss Hartwell, though I cannot find it.")*
> "The moral is that hats are deeper than they look," Rose said, and he laughed, and the marquise patted his hand too, impartial in her patting.
> *(The clocks in the gallery said half past eleven. The feast went on, masked, the farewell's, the French dishes, the champagne, and Rose thought that if the old world had to end, it was ending the way it had lived: at table, laughing, with the candles lit.)*
> *(She set down her glass. Half an hour to midnight. The masks' last half hour. She could feel the night gathering itself, the way the hall gathered before a toast.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night's thesis — dress the becoming; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief — The last great masquerade:** "The old world's last night. The mask comes off at midnight — permanently. Dress for the becoming — the triumph, quoted, transformed. **Editorial criterion: becoming.**"
>
> **A. The Becoming** — ivory, the triumph's memory; the woman, becoming. Motif: the S1 triumph, quoted in embroidery — the becoming, stated. Thread: **gold** (the landed, stated) / **ivory silk** (the triumph, matched) / **pearl** (the becoming, lit). Colorway: ivory + gold + pearl. Accessories: the grandmother's pearls; the mask, as chosen; ivory kid gloves.
> **B. The Quoted** — blush, the rose's echo; the legacy, the night's. Motif: the Hartwell rose, massed — the quoted, embroidered. Thread: **rose silk** (the living, matched) / **gold** (the landed, stated) / **pearl** (the quoted, lit). Colorway: blush + gold + pearl. Accessories: a gold circlet; the rose mask; blush kid gloves.
> **C. The Plain** — black, the domino's; the woman, the unadorned. Motif: the unbroken line, architectural — the plain, embroidered. Thread: **silver** (the exact, edged) / **black silk** (the domino, matched) / **pearl** (the plain, lit). Colorway: black + silver + pearl. Accessories: a silver chain; the plain domino; black kid gloves.
>
> *(The dressing room, the masquerade's afternoon: the triumph, quoted, transformed. She dresses the way the becoming asks: the beginning, become.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the becoming, the quoted, or the plain — the night's thesis, remembered. The hair, dressed for the mask. The accessories, exact. The mirror, to be faced masked. **Direction.** The mask comes off at midnight — dress for the becoming. **Editorial criterion.** Becoming — every choice must answer the transformation, not the disguise.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the night. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** the night's face — the ivory becoming, or the blush quoted, or the black plain — whichever the becoming chose, the masquerade worn. *5 coins.*

scenes.synopsis: midnight approaches — the unmasking's hour; the hall, holding its breath. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Midnight approached, and the hall knew it. The dancing slowed the way a top slows before it stops, the couples turning wider, the talk dropping to something quieter. The musicians played a last air before the hour, something slow, and the candlelight seemed to lean in.)*
> *(Rose stood by the pillar and watched the masks' last minutes. Forty-one masks, one lost and found under a hat, all of them living their final hour. The silk, the paint, the night's faces. In a quarter of an hour they would be untied, set down, become relics. She thought of the morning room's white cloths, the choosing, her hand hovering, and of how long ago the choosing felt, though it was hours.)*
> *(She thought of her own mask, the ribbons at the back of her head, the silk warm now from her skin. She had worn it half the night. It had become familiar, almost comfortable, which was the danger of masks: they fit. The domino would have fit differently. The rose would have fit differently. But the choosing was done, and the mask was hers, and the fit was the night's.)*
> *(Laurent was across the hall, unmoving in the turning room, watching the clock. She could see the tension in his shoulders even at the distance. Ten seasons of the Frenchman, and in fifteen minutes the performance ended. She wanted to go to him. She stayed where she was. Some minutes had to be waited out alone.)*
> *(A French lady near the pillar was crying quietly behind her mask, not from sorrow, Rose thought, but from the particular fullness of a farewell done beautifully. Her companion pretended not to notice, and refilled her champagne, which was the correct response.)*
> *(The clock's minute hand moved. The hall held its breath. The old world, masked, waited for the hour, and the candles burned lower and warmer, and Octavia was right, the light was perfect, the faces about to be true. Rose found she was holding her bouquet too tightly, the stems creaking in her gloves, and loosened her grip, and breathed.)*

scenes.synopsis: the terrace — masked, the night air; the old world's edge, quiet. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(A quarter hour before midnight she slipped out to the terrace, because the hall had begun to feel like the inside of a jewel box and she wanted air that had not been breathed by forty people.)*
> *(The Park lay below in full moonlight, the lake a flat sheet of silver, the gardens gone to dark shapes with silver edges. Her slippers were thin evening things, useless against November, and the cold came up through the terrace stones at once. She did not mind. The cold was at least honest, which was more than could be said for the perfume in the hall.)*
> *(Her breath showed. The bouquet was still in her hand — the lilies ghostly, the roses gone almost black in the moonlight, the stems a little crushed from the dancing, the ribbon loosened. For midnight, Élise had said. You will want something to hold. Élise was always right about practical things, which was why Rose forgave her being right about everything else.)*
> *(She thought about the unmasking the way one thinks about cold water before the plunge: the ribbons, the silk coming away, her own face underneath, blinking. And Laurent's, ten seasons in the coming off. The thought landed in her like a stone in the lake below — England, the Park, the future, here — and the ripples went out across the silver water and did not come back.)*
> *(Behind the glass doors the hall glowed and the music came through muffled, as if the night were talking about her in the next room. Ahead, the Park: moonlit, English, entirely uninterested in masquerades. She stood between the two with her cold feet and her crushed lilies, and thought of Julian's terrace — the free life, the walk continuing — and of Henry at the hall's edge, who had watched the whole evening the way a man watches a coastline.)*
> *(The moon went behind a cloud and came out again, and the lake flared silver, and somewhere beyond the lime walk an owl called once, with the tone of a creature that had seen far grander follies than this one.)*
> *(A footman came out to check the terrace lanterns, saw her standing there masked in the moonlight with her ruined bouquet, and withdrew without a word, closing the door soft as a secret. She was grateful. Some minutes want no witness but the moon, and this — the last quarter hour of the masked world — was one of them.)*

scenes.synopsis: Laurent, the terrace — the Frenchman, the truth nearer; midnight, minutes. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(He found her on the terrace, as she had known he would, the way one knows the next line of a song.)*
> "Minutes," he said, without preamble. They were ten seasons past preamble. "The unmasking."
> *(He took her hands. His were cold — colder than the night air warranted, the particular cold of a man whose blood has gone elsewhere.)* "Rose. The mask —" He touched the silk at his temple. "Comes off. Permanently." He looked at her through the mask's eyes, and underneath the paint his own eyes were doing the looking. "England. The Englishman."
> "I know," Rose said.
> "You know." His breath showed between them. "All evening I have been —" He glanced back at the glowing hall. "Not afraid of Paris. Not of the hall." He looked at her. "Of the moment after. The face underneath, in the light." He stopped.
> "What if what?" Rose said.
> "What if the mask was the best part?" *(The crooked smile, half under the silk.)* "Ten seasons of polish, Rose. Underneath there is only a man."
> "Only a man is the whole of it," Rose said. "The polish was the loan. The man is the keeping."
> *(He lifted her hands and kissed them — his lips were cold — and then he went back through the glass doors to wait out the minutes among the masks, and Rose stayed on the terrace with the cold stones and the crushed bouquet, and watched him go: the Frenchman's last entrance, straight-backed, trembling.)*
> *(She had seen men walk into battle with less visible effort, though she had never said so to Henry. Courage, at close range, looked a great deal like trembling. The music came through the glass, the last air before midnight, sweet and almost sad, and inside, forty painted faces were living their final minutes, and had no idea.)*
> *(She touched her own mask's ribbons, tied neat at the back of her head. Hers would come off too, when the hour struck — the hostess had no exemption. She found she was not sorry. The silk had been a fine loan, but loans come due, and midnight was the most punctual creditor in the world.)*

scenes.synopsis: the unmasking — midnight; the masks off; the hall, revealed. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Midnight struck, and the hall untied its faces. It began with Laurent: he stepped to the hall's center, and the music stopped, and in the sudden quiet he reached up and untied his mask, and set it down, and stood unmasked.)*
> *(Then the hall followed, all at once, the silk, the paint, the night's faces coming away. Ribbons pulled, masks lifted, a small sigh going through the room like wind through wheat. The émigré ladies, the English, the young officer, the marquise. Faces, blinking in the candlelight, true. The sigh was the night's own sound, relief and loss braided, and Rose felt it move through her own chest too.)*
> *(Rose untied her own. The ribbons caught in her hair for a moment, and she worked them free, and the mask came away, and the air touched her face, cool and sudden. She held the mask in her hand: the triumph quoted, the rose, the domino plain, whichever she had chosen, the night's face, now a relic. The silk was warm from her skin. The paint at the edge was a little smudged. It looked smaller than it had on the white cloths, and more honest.)*
> *(The hall was revealed: the old world, the faces underneath. Without the paint and silk they looked younger, and older, and kinder. The marquise was just a tired old woman with kind eyes. The vicomte was a boy. Letitia, scarlet domino gone, was Letitia, hawk-eyed and warm, grinning at Rose across the room.)*
> *(Somebody laughed, a short surprised laugh, at nothing and everything. Somebody else cried, briefly, behind a hand. A French gentleman stared at his wife's unmasked face as if seeing her for the first time in years, and perhaps he was. The young officer whose mask had been under the hat stood revealed as barely twenty, pink-cheeked, grinning like a boy let out of school.)*
> *(The candles burned low and warm. Octavia had been right. The faces looked true.)*
> *(And in the hall's center stood Laurent, unmasked, waiting, and the old world's last night ended, and the new world's first moment began.)*

scenes.synopsis: Laurent, unmasked — permanently; the mask off; the Frenchman, the truth. (Turns: 9)
scenes.prose:
> *(He stood before her with the mask in his hand, and then he set it down on a side table — carefully, the way one lays down a thing that has served honorably and is now retired — and turned back to her with his whole face showing.)*
> "Rose." His eyes were direct now, no paint between them. "The Frenchman —" A pause, and in the pause she watched ten seasons cross his face and leave it. "Was the mask. The accent, the shrug, the performance." Another pause. "The truth is the Englishman."
> *(The hall had gone silent around them, the way halls do when something real is happening and everyone is afraid to miss it. Rose looked at his face — the lines at the eyes, the mouth that smiled crooked, the unpolished truth of him — and recognized it the way one recognizes a road at dawn: she had traveled it in glimpses for a decade, and now here it was, whole, in candlelight, asking nothing. The gallery, the cold hands, the fast heart under her palm — all the stored moments, redeemed at once.)*
> "England," he said. "Chosen."
> *(She took his hand. It was warm now — the cold had gone out of it somewhere between the terrace and this moment, as if the blood had finally been permitted to return.)* "The Englishman," she said.
> "The Englishman," he agreed, and smiled, crooked and true, and the hall exhaled all at once, and somebody began to clap, and then everybody was clapping, and the candles burned, and the night turned.
> *(The émigré were crying openly. The English were smiling the particular smile of people who have decided to be kind and are relieved to have the excuse. And Harrow, at the hall's edge, had set down his list and was clapping too — the ledger abandoned on a chair — which Rose thought was the finest tribute of the night, because Harrow never abandoned the ledger.)*
> *(Laurent looked around at the clapping hall, unmasked, and laughed — the unpolished laugh, the one that had taken ten seasons to let her hear — and the hall laughed with him, and something that had been wound tight since September came undone all at once, like a cloak slipping off a shoulder.)*

scenes.synopsis: the declaration — England, chosen; before witnesses. (Turns: 9)
scenes.prose:
> *(He turned from Rose to the company, and the company turned to him, the way a field of wheat turns to wind.)*
> "My friends." His English now, the polish gone out of it, the truth of the accent underneath. He picked up the mask from the side table and held it aloft — the silk, the paint, the Frenchman's face — and set it down again, face to the wood. "Off. Permanently." He looked across the hall: the émigré, the English, forty unmasked faces. "I choose England. The Park." He looked at Rose. "The future. Here."
> *(The hall was silent. Somewhere a glass chimed against a table and nobody drank from it. The candles burned low, and the silence went on long enough for Rose to hear her own heart, which was behaving as if it had never been to a ball before.)*
> *(Upstairs his letters to Paris waited, sealed and ready — the practiced English, Harrow correcting his spelling of "permanently" — and Rose thought that every small preparation of the day had been a rehearsal for this unadorned minute.)*
> *(Then the old vicomte with the scarred cheek stepped forward and embraced him, hard, the way men embrace when words would be an insult to the occasion, and the marquise patted them both — the patting, it seemed, was for all occasions — and the silence broke into talk and movement and the particular beautiful noise of forty people exhaling at once.)*
> *(Champagne appeared as if the house had been holding its breath too, and the glasses rose, and somebody shouted "L'Angleterre!" and somebody else answered "England!" and both were cheered, because the hall had decided that both could be true at once.)*
> *(Rose stood beside him with the quoted bouquet in her hands, unmasked, and felt the hall's eyes on them both, and did not mind. Ten seasons of being looked at, and this was the first time the looking had felt like a blessing instead of an audit.)*
> *(He took her hand and held it, in front of them all, the Englishman's hand warm and steady. Nobody announced it. Nobody needed to. The night had made its great statement quietly, the way great statements are made, and the candles burned on.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE CHOICE'S WITNESS (who witnesses Laurent's choice: the company, the family, or Rose alone). The night deepens; decide the witness. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Past midnight, with the declaration still ringing in the hall's rafters, the choice asked its witness. The thing had been said; the hall had heard it. But a moment becomes a memory by being seen, and the memory would take its shape from the eyes that held it.)*
> *(The company: the hall entire. Forty unmasked faces, émigré and English, the witnesses of the ton. The choice remembered as history — told and retold, the night the Frenchman became the Englishman before them all. The grand telling, and the public truth.)*
> *(The family: Augusta and Letitia, the line. The spectacles, the hawk's eyes, the two women who had watched Rose for ten seasons and knew what choosing cost. The choice remembered as the family's — held close, the line's welcome the seal. The intimate telling, and the private truth.)*
> *(Rose alone: the woman herself. No audience but the one who mattered most. The choice made for her, witnessed by her, the two of them and the candlelight. The choice remembered as the heart's — unperformed, unwitnessed except by love. The quietest telling, and perhaps the truest.)*
> *(Each telling had its price. The company's would make the choice history, and history belongs to everyone, which is another way of saying it belongs to no one. The family's would make it the line's, and the line keeps what it is given, but the line also frames it, and frames are a kind of cage. Hers alone would keep it unperformed — but a memory held by one pair of eyes is a candle in a closed room: true, and invisible.)*
> *(She thought of the masks laid on the side tables, retired. She thought of Laurent's hand, warm now, in hers. She thought of the hall's eyes, and the family's eyes, and her own — and of how memory is a choosy thing, and would keep whichever seeing she gave it.)*
> *(The night waited, unmasked and patient, for her to name the eyes. The choosing of the witness was hers, as the choosing itself had been his. Whatever eyes she gave it, the memory would keep their shape — that was the whole of the power, and the whole of the risk.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The choice's witness:*
- **The company** — *the hall, entire.* The choice is witnessed by all — the old world, the farewell's. (Consequence: the witnessing is absolute — but companies are crowds, and the choice was the man's.)
- **The family** — *the line, together.* The choice is witnessed by the family — Augusta, Letitia, the line's. (Consequence: the witnessing is the line's — but families are ceremony, and the choice was the heart's.)
- **Rose alone** — *the woman, herself.* The choice is witnessed by Rose alone — private, the two's. (Consequence: the witnessing is true — but alone is apart, and the hall wants the history.)
> *(She looked once around the hall — the company, the family, the candlelight — and she chose.)*

scenes.synopsis: the company, after — the old world, witnessing; the hall, the choice's. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The congratulations began the way weather begins: all at once, and from every direction.)*
> *(The émigré came first, with the particular grace of the exiled, who know what a country costs because they have paid it. An old gentleman held Laurent's face in both hands and said something rapid that made Laurent laugh — the unpolished laugh — and then the old gentleman wept, briefly, and pretended he hadn't, and everybody pretended with him. A vicomtesse embraced Rose and spoke of the Park as if it were a person of their mutual acquaintance, and Rose, her French suddenly equal to the hour, answered as if it were.)*
> *(The English came next, the ton, curious and kind in the way the ton is kind when it has decided to be. The marquise patted Rose's cheek — the patting, it seemed, was for all occasions — and said England was fortunate, and Rose understood every word this time, or chose to.)*
> *(A young lord, unmasked and pink as a ham, shook Laurent's hand with both of his and declared it the finest thing he had seen since Waterloo, which made Laurent laugh again and made Rose like the young lord very much. The ton's kindness, once decided, was a thorough thing, like its malice.)*
> *(Then Letitia arrived in a rush of scarlet, no mask, hawk's eyes bright.)* "Darling," she said, taking Rose's face in her hands. "The Englishman. Unmasked. Permanently." She kissed Rose's forehead. "The quartermaster approves. The quartermaster is also starving. Is there more of that ham?"
> "There is always more ham, Aunt Letitia. Harrow sees to it."
> "Harrow sees to everything. It is his genius and his curse." *(She turned on Laurent.)* "Young man. Fed, I hope. The Englishman must keep his strength. England expects it."
> *(There was more of the ham — there is always more of everything when Harrow is in charge — and the night went on, and the congratulations found their rhythm: the émigré bowed deepest, the English shook hands longest, and Letitia hugged hardest of all, and meant it most. The champagne kept coming, properly cold, and the musicians — unmasked like everyone else — played as if the night had unmasked them too, the first violin's ornaments wilder than at rehearsal.)*

scenes.synopsis: the émigré houses — Paris, witnessing; the old world, the new. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Through the small hours they came to Laurent in ones and twos, the old world greeting the new, and Rose watched it the way one watches a tide: something large, moving according to rules older than the evening.)*
> *(The vicomte with the scarred cheek clasped Laurent's shoulder and spoke low and fast, and Laurent nodded, and they stood a moment in the particular stillness of men who have both lost the same thing and found it again in different countries.)*
> *(The women were kinder and franker, as women are when the champagne has done its work. The marquise drew Rose aside — patted her hand, a variation on the cheek — and said, in careful slow French that Rose followed perfectly, that Laurent had been a good Frenchman and would be a better Englishman, and that Rose was to take care of him, and that England was cold in winter and he would need a wife who knew about blankets.)*
> "I know about blankets," Rose said, in French, and the marquise laughed, delighted, and patted her hand again, and Rose decided the patting was not a tic but a sacrament.
> *(A younger lady, with tired eyes and a shawl pulled close, told Rose that Paris would write itself into a fury and then into a shrug, and the shrug would be the truer response. "They will say he was always English at heart," she said, smoothing her gloves. "It will become the story. Let them. Stories are all we have left of some things." She said it without bitterness, and Rose thought the exiled understood narrative the way Harrow understood lists: as the only order available when the world stops cooperating.)*
> *(By two o'clock they were writing the night into their letters already — Rose could see them composing over the supper table, the unmasking, the declaration, the Englishman. She thought of her own unsent letters, the ones she drafted in her head on sleepless nights, and was glad tonight's needed no drafting. The truth had announced itself, clearly, before witnesses, and all that remained was the reporting. She found she was not tired. The small hours had a particular clarity, like water after the sediment settles, and she wanted to be awake for all of it.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Dowager, on England — Augusta witnesses; the line, the Englishman. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta came to them where they stood by the windows, magnificent in black velvet, seventy-two years upright, the spectacles catching the low candlelight.)*
> "The Frenchman." She studied Laurent through the spectacles. "Become —" The Dowager's pause, the one that had ended conversations for half a century. "The Englishman." She looked at him a moment longer. "England is fortunate, young man. The Park —" A glance at Rose. "The Park is fortunate." The rarest smile, the one she spent sparingly. "The line welcomes you. Unmasked."
> *(Laurent bowed, deeply, the bow of a man who understood exactly what he was being given.)* "Madame. I am honored beyond —" He stopped. "Beyond expression. Your granddaughter has taught me that the English understate, and I am practicing."
> "Practice harder," Augusta said, but the rare smile stayed. "The line does not welcome lightly, young man. It has welcomed you. See that you are worthy of the expenditure."
> "I will spend my life on it, madame."
> "See that you do." *(She took Rose's hand; her own was cool and steady.)* "Child," she said quietly. "Well chosen. Both of you."
> *(It was the most unguarded thing Augusta had said in Rose's hearing in ten seasons. Rose stored it the way Octavia stored light: completely, and forever. The Dowager's "child," spent as sparingly as her smiles, landed like a knighthood.)*
> *(The company near the windows had gone quiet to watch, and Rose saw the émigré ladies nodding among themselves. This was the seal they had waited for. Without it the choosing would have been romance; with it, it was history. Augusta surveyed the hall, the hall straightened, and the Dowager went on her way, leaving the seal behind her like light through a doorway.)*
> *(Laurent watched her go with something like awe.)* "Seventy-two years," he murmured, "and the room rearranges itself around her."
> *(Rose squeezed his hand.)* "Wait until you see what she does with a seating plan."
> *(He was still watching the doorway where she had gone.)* "I shall spend my life being worthy of the expenditure," Laurent said, "and it will not be enough, and she will know it, and approve of the knowing."
> *(Rose laughed, quietly, so as not to disturb the seal.)* "That is the most English sentence you have ever spoken."

scenes.synopsis: the aunt, on the Frenchman — Letitia witnesses; the quartermaster, the heart. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia found them by the supper room, where Laurent was finally eating — unmasked, with the appetite of a man who had been too nervous to eat for a week.)*
> "Darling." The hawk's eyes were warm, the scarlet gown a flag. "The mask —" A gesture at the side table, where his mask lay retired. "Off. Permanently." She took Rose's hands. "The quartermaster approves, darling. Not the strategy." The real look, the warm one underneath the performance. "The heart."
> "The heart is not a strategy, Aunt Letitia," Rose said.
> "Everything is a strategy, darling. The heart is simply the one strategy I have never been able to argue with." *(She turned on Laurent.)* "Young man. You danced beautifully masked. You will dance beautifully unmasked. The difference is that now we shall all see you stepping on her feet, so do try to improve."
> "I will practice, madame."
> "See that you do. And eat." *(She surveyed his plate with the quartermaster's eye.)* "You are too thin. The Englishman must not be thin. It suggests the Frenchman is still in charge of the kitchen."
> *(Laurent ate, obediently, and then Letitia surprised them both: she took his face in her hands, the way she had taken Rose's, and kissed his forehead, and her eyes were bright.)* "Welcome, darling," she said softly. "Unmasked."
> *(A small silence, the three of them, the supper room's noise going on around them like weather. Then Letitia rallied, as she always did.)* "More ham," she decreed, and a footman was summoned, and the plate was replenished. "And champagne. The Englishman celebrates properly or not at all."
> *(Rose watched the two of them — the hawk and the Englishman — and thought that Letitia's affections, once given, were the most thoroughly defended positions in England. Laurent, eating ham under orders, had just been annexed.)*
> *(She watched him eat with satisfaction, and confided to Rose, not quite under her breath: "The Frenchman starved himself on nerves. The Englishman eats. It is the first improvement. There will be others. I shall supervise them all." Rose thought that being approved by Letitia was rather like being adopted by a hawk: sudden, total, and permanent.)*

scenes.synopsis: the free man, on the masquerade — Julian witnesses; grace, the terrace's. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian found her by the windows, the mended gloves in his pocket, the unguarded look quiet on his face.)*
> "The unmasking." He glanced toward Laurent, laughing with the émigré by the supper room. "The mask off. Permanently." A pause, and the ghost of the old smile. "Brave, Rose. The choosing."
> "He is," Rose said.
> "The terrace —" He touched his pocket. "The terrace is still free. As a life." He bowed over her hand, the familiar bow. "The walk continues, Rose. The masquerade was his night." A glance at the hall, the unmasked, the new. "The terrace is ours."
> *(She held his hand a moment. Ten seasons, and the grace was entire: no bitterness, no performance, nothing asked. She thought of the thousand small kindnesses of the decade — the gloves mended, the walks, the unguarded look — and was glad, suddenly and completely, that the night had room for his grace too.)*
> "The walk continues," she said.
> "Every day," he said. "On foot." The ghost of the old smile, warmer now. "It is the only way I know."
> *(She thought of asking him to stay for the last dance, and thought better of it. Some men say goodbye by leaving the room; Julian said it by going for a walk, which was the same thing, done honestly.)*
> *(The music had softened to something slow, and the dancers were mostly couples now, the young and the hopeful. Julian had never been one for the last dance. He preferred the walk: the cold air, the mended gloves, the Park to himself. It was not a consolation. It was a choice, and he had made it years ago, and the making of it was the whole of his courage.)*
> *(He looked toward the terrace doors, the moonlight beyond.)* "I shall walk it now, I think. Before the night ends. The Park by moonlight, the mended gloves, the whole of it." He bowed again, deeper. "His night, Rose. Ours, the terrace."
> *(He went through the glass doors into the moonlight, and Rose watched him go — the free man's back, straight, unhurried — and then she turned back to the hall, where Laurent was laughing with his mouth uncovered, and the night held them both without spilling either.)*

scenes.synopsis: the soldier, on the night — Henry witnesses; the devotion, the unmasking's. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry had danced little, talked less, and watched everything, the way he did. Rose found him at the hall's edge, where he had spent the better part of the evening being the still point the night turned around.)*
> *(Earlier she had seen him straighten a guttering candle in its sconce, mid-waltz, without breaking his conversation with the Dowager. Nobody else had noticed. That was the whole of Henry, in one gesture: the house kept, invisibly, while the history happened around him.)*
> "The mask off." The smallest smile. "Permanently." He looked across the unmasked hall. "The small things continue, Rose. Every day." A breath. "The devotion doesn't need a mask. It never did."
> "No," Rose said. "It never did."
> *(He bowed over her hand — warm and steady, the soldier's hand.)* "The lanterns are lit, the terrace is watched, the house is settled. The night is well, Rose."
> "The night is well, Henry."
> *(Around them the hall turned — the émigré laughing, the English exclaiming, Letitia holding court by the supper table with a plate she had clearly annexed — and at the edge of it all, Henry, steady as a mooring post, making sure the night didn't drift.)*
> *(She thought of the Park's round, the daily practice, the urns and the lanterns, and of how Henry's unmasking had happened long before midnight: one small thing at a time, until there was nothing left to take off.)* "The small unmaskings," she said. "I have been watching for them."
> "And?" The smallest smile.
> "And they are the truest thing in the house. Midnight took the silk off, Henry. You took the mask off years ago, one lantern at a time. I only just noticed."
> "Noticed is enough, Rose." *(The soldier's bow.)* "It is all any of us get, in the end: noticed."
> *(He went back to his post at the hall's edge, and the unmasked company turned before them both, and Rose thought that some people unmask at midnight and some people had never worn one — and that the house was held up, in the end, by the second kind, the ones who kept the candles trimmed while history happened.)*

scenes.synopsis: the painter, on the unmasking — Octavia witnesses; the faces, the truth's. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia had watched the whole of it the way she watched everything: precisely, completely, storing it. Rose found her at the hall's edge, eyes moving over the unmasked company like a woman reading a letter.)*
> "The masks off." The precise voice, quiet. "The faces, finally. The true ones." She looked at Rose. "You looked like yourself tonight. Finally."
> "You are going to paint it," Rose said.
> "I am going to try. The light at midnight —" Octavia shook her head. "It will not sit still. Nothing true sits still." She was silent a moment, composing. "Not the declaration. His hand, setting the mask down. The care of it. That was the true unmasking. The rest was the hall catching up."
> "You saw that? The care?"
> "I see everything, Rose. It is my affliction and my living." The precise smile, warm now. "He set it down like a man laying flowers on a grave. Honorably. Finally."
> *(Earlier, Rose had watched her watch the young officer dance with his mask's ribbons still tied around his wrist like a favor, and had seen her file it away — the wrist, the ribbons, the unguarded joy — the way other women file away slights. Nothing was wasted on Octavia. It was what made her company both exhausting and indispensable. The painter's eye missed nothing and forgave nothing, and Rose had long ago stopped minding the first and started valuing the second. To be seen truly was rarer than to be praised, and Octavia never praised.)*
> *(They stood together at the hall's edge while the unmasked company turned before them like a living canvas, and the silence between them was the companionable kind, exact.)* "And the arrangement?" Rose asked. "Two houses, one shared life. Will you paint that too?"
> "I am painting it already." Octavia tapped her temple. "In here. The canvas comes later. The seeing is the painting; the paint is only the reporting."
> *(She went back to her wall to study the light a little longer, the painter's prowl, unhurried. Rose watched her go and thought that being seen by Octavia was rather like being painted: uncomfortable, exact, and in the end, entirely true.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dancing, unmasked — the new world's first dance. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(After the declaration the musicians struck up, and the hall took the floor with its true faces, and it was different. The steps were the same, the airs were the same, but the eyes were unguarded now, and the laughter came easier, and the hall turned with the relief of a held breath let go.)*
> *(Rose danced with Laurent, his hand sure at her waist, his eyes direct — they did not need to say anything; the hall was saying it for them. She danced with Julian, easy, the old friendship entire. She danced with a French vicomte who had been charming masked and proved charming unmasked, which was a pleasant surprise, the way it always is. She danced with Henry, who danced the way he did everything: correctly, steadily, with the smallest smile.)*
> *(The marquise proved a tireless dancer and claimed Rose for a country dance, patting her hand in time to the music, which set the whole set laughing. The young officer danced with his mask's ribbons still tied around his wrist like a favor, and nobody thought it odd, because nobody was performing anymore.)*
> *(Letitia danced every dance, scarlet and indefatigable, and between sets she was to be seen at the supper table, restoring herself with ham, like an army refitting between campaigns.)*
> *(The musicians played as if the unmasking had unmasked them too: the first violin's ornaments wilder, the cellist grinning openly. The French airs sounded different under true faces — less like a farewell, more like a beginning. Rose thought of the quiet gavotte in the doorway at rehearsal, and how far the night had traveled since, and then the figure brought her back, and she stopped thinking, which was the point of dancing.)*
> *(The candles burned lower. The champagne kept coming, properly cold. The floor was scuffed with the night's dancing, the wax trodden into the boards, and Rose thought the scuffs were the truest record of the evening — better than any letter, because nobody had composed them. Octavia danced past in someone's arms and mouthed "True" at Rose over her partner's shoulder, and Rose laughed — unmasked, uncovered, entire — and the hall turned, and the night was sweet.)*

scenes.synopsis: the small hours — the old world's end; the night, held. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(By the small hours the hall was half-full, the dancers thinned, the masks lying on the side tables like shed skins. The musicians played slower airs. The candles burned low. The champagne was still cold, because somebody — Harrow, presumably, the invisible hand — was still seeing to it.)*
> *(Laurent was asleep in a chair by the windows, his head tilted back, unmasked even in sleep. One of the émigré ladies had covered him with a shawl. Rose stood and looked at him a moment: ten seasons of polish, asleep under borrowed wool, breathing deeply. The knot in her chest loosened the way a knot loosens.)*
> *(Letitia was still dancing, scarlet and indefatigable, though her partners were thinning and the musicians were eyeing the clock. Augusta had gone up, the spectacles retired for the night. Julian stood on the terrace with the mended gloves in his hand, looking at the Park. Henry was at the hall's edge, watching, the devotion's watch, which never ended.)*
> *(A footman moved among the side tables, collecting the shed masks, handling the silk carefully, as if the faces might still be warm. The champagne bottles stood empty in their coolers, the ice melted to water. The hall had the beautiful exhaustion of a party that has given everything and kept nothing back.)*
> *(Rose picked up her own mask — the silk, the paint, the night's face — and held it a moment. It looked small now, and a little sad, like a thing that had done its work. The ribbons lay curled; the paint was smudged at the edge. It had been the night's first statement. She set it down with the others, to be gathered in the morning, and the night was done being worn.)*
> *(She walked the hall once more, the danced floor, the guttering candles. The old world had ended quietly, the way it had lived: beautifully, and without fuss. She did not feel sad. She felt the way one feels at the end of a long book that has ended well: unwilling to close it, and glad to have read it. Behind her the musicians packed their instruments with the care of men putting children to bed, and the hall settled into its after-midnight quiet.)*

scenes.synopsis: the masks, kept — the relics; the night's, the past's. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(In the morning room, by lamplight, Rose gathered them: the silk, the paint, the untied. Forty-two masks — one lost and found under a hat in the supper room, all accounted for — laid out on the long table while Mrs. Quick inventoried them without comment, as if relics were simply another kind of linen.)*
> *(She found Laurent's among them, the Frenchman's last face, the paint a little smudged at the edge, the silk still warm from his skin. She held it a moment, then set it aside, separate from the others. Kept, not worn. The distinction mattered.)*
> *(Her own mask she kept too — the night's face, the choosing. The ribbons folded neatly, the way Élise folded muslin, laid on the cloth. It would go in the cedar chest with the S1 things: the beginning's relics, the becoming's. The chest was getting full. That seemed right. A life, properly kept, takes up room.)*
> *(The domino she had not chosen, the rose she had not chosen, were here too, the unchosen kept with the chosen. Rose touched them both, lightly, in acknowledgment. The choosing had been the night's first statement; the keeping, she supposed, was its last. She was getting philosophical. It was nearly three in the morning, which explained it.)*
> *(Mrs. Quick's pencil moved down the list without hesitation — forty-two ticks, no flourish — and Rose thought that the house's memory lived less in the cedar chest than in that pencil: everything kept, everything accounted for, nothing mourned.)*
> *(Mrs. Quick folded a cloth over them with the air of a woman putting the past to bed.)* "The masks, miss. All kept."
> "All kept, Mrs. Quick."
> "The past —" The immovable face was nearly warm. "Kept, miss. Not worn." A pause. "A good night, miss."
> "A good night, Mrs. Quick."
> *(It was the longest conversation Rose had ever had with Mrs. Quick, and the warmest, and she treasured it the way she treasured the mask: as a relic of a night when everything true had been said plainly. She left the morning room to the lamplight and the forty-two silk faces sleeping under their cloths, and went up to bed as the sky began to pale.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE NIGHT'S MEANING (what the masquerade was: the old world's farewell, Laurent's becoming, or the mask's end). The small hours; decide the meaning. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The small hours, and the night's meaning undecided. The ball was over, the hall half-dark, the candles guttering. Rose sat in the morning room among the kept masks, forty-two silk faces sleeping under their cloths, and the night asked what it had been.)*
> *(The old world's farewell: the French, honored, the last night. The émigré houses, Paris in the hall, the accents, the champagne, the last dance of a world that had lived beautifully and knew it. The farewell complete, the honoring done, the night worthy of its occasion.)*
> *(Laurent's becoming: the Frenchman become the Englishman, chosen. The mask off, permanently, the declaration before witnesses, his hand warm in hers. One man's transformation, ten seasons in the making, sealed at midnight. The story's heart, beating plainly.)*
> *(The mask's end: the untied, the truth's. Forty-two silk faces set down, the paint and the performance retired. The unmasking itself — the moment the hall breathed out and was true. Not one man's story but everyone's: the end of hiding, the beginning of faces.)*
> *(She thought of the marquise's patting hand, and of Laurent asleep in the chair with a borrowed shawl, and of her own face in the glass at noon, the three silk faces waiting. The night had been all three, of course. Nights are never one thing. But memory is choosy, and the meaning would shape the remembering, the way a frame shapes a painting.)*
> *(She weighed them the way she had weighed the masks at noon: the farewell for its beauty, the becoming for its courage, the mask's end for its truth. Each was the night. None was the whole of it. That was the difficulty with meanings — they were like guests: invite one, and the others stood in the hall waiting.)*
> *(The candles guttered lower. The masks slept. She thought of Élise's words — the beginning, the becoming — and of Octavia's — the setting down — and of Henry's — the small things, continuing — and understood the night had given her not one meaning but a shelf of them, to choose among, like masks on a table.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — The night's meaning:*
- **The old world's farewell** — *the French, honored.* The night was the farewell — the old world, one more night. (Consequence: the honoring is complete — but farewells end, and the meaning wants continuing.)
- **Laurent's becoming** — *the Englishman, chosen.* The night was the becoming — the Frenchman, become. (Consequence: the becoming is the story — but becomings are one man's, and the night was everyone's.)
- **The mask's end** — *the truth, unmasked.* The night was the unmasking — the masks off, permanently. (Consequence: the truth is the theme — but truths are many, and the night wants the one.)
> *(She rose, and named it quietly to the empty room — the way one names a ship, for luck, before it sails — and went up as the dawn came, the meaning settled, hers.)*
