scenes.synopsis: dawn — the first small thing; the lanterns, the day's beginning. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Dawn: the first small thing. Rose woke to the sound she had come to know as the day's beginning: Henry's boots on the terrace, the lantern check, the soldier's round.)*
> *(She went to the window. The Park was grey-gold, the lake misted, the gardens dark shapes. Henry moved along the terrace with a lantern, though the dawn was coming, checking each of the terrace lanterns: the glass, the oil, the wick. The first small thing, done before the house woke. The flame in his hand, the grey-gold morning, the soldier's steady tread.)*
> *(She watched him from the window, unobserved, and thought of all the dawns of ten seasons: the frightened, the watchful, the reckoning. This dawn was the daily's, the quiet, the kept. Henry's boots on the terrace stones, the lantern's glass catching the first light, the small things beginning.)*
> *(She dressed quickly and went down. The hall was cold, the fires not yet lit. The terrace doors stood open, and the morning air came in, sharp, clean. The house slept around her, and the Park woke beyond the doors.)*
> "All steady." He reported from the terrace, seeing her. "The lanterns —" The smallest smile. "The day, Rose. Beginning."
> "Beginning," Rose agreed.
> *(He checked the last lantern, the glass clean, the wick trimmed, and set it back in its bracket. The dawn came up over the Park, and the lanterns — lit all night, steady — were quenched one by one, the small flames going out like stars at morning. The terrace brightened, and the Park brightened, and the day was the beginning's.)*
> *(Rose stood beside him while he hung the snuffer on its hook, and the Park lay before them grey-gold and misted, waiting to be walked. The round's first hour was done before the house had woken — that was the devotion entire, the work finished before anyone thought to ask for it, the day's account opened in lantern-light.)*
> *(Henry checked the last bracket out of habit, nodded once, and they went in to breakfast. Behind them the terrace brightened and the Park brightened, and the small flames went out like stars at morning, one by one, until only the daylight was left.)*

scenes.synopsis: the drive — the morning's check; the limes, the gravel. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The drive: the morning's check. They walked it together, Rose and Henry, the limes, the gravel, the day's second small things.)*
> *(The drive was a mile of gravel between the limes, the Park's approach, the first thing visitors saw. Henry walked its length the way he walked everything: steadily, seeing. The gravel raked smooth — he bent, once, to move a fallen twig. The limes lit by the morning sun, the leaves turning. A rut where a carriage had cut too close — he noted it, the soldier's eye, for the gardeners.)*
> "The drive is well," he said.
> *(She thought of all the drives of ten seasons: the arrivals, the departures, the carriages in the rain. This morning the drive was just the drive, gravel and limes, and that was the point. The ordinary, the kept, the daily's.)*
> *(They turned at the gates and walked back, the Park opening before them, the house on its hill. The morning's check: the drive, the limes. The small things, continuing. The gates stood open, the lane beyond, the village waking.)*
> *(A blackbird sang from the lime walk. Henry's boots crunched the gravel, steady. Rose's slippers were quieter. The two sounds went up the drive together, and the morning held them. The limes arched overhead, the leaves turning gold, and the drive was the morning's own.)*
> *(The mile of gravel, the limes, the morning sun. The drive was the Park's approach, and the approach was kept. Henry's eye missed nothing: the twig moved, the rut noted for the gardeners, the leaves turning gold overhead.)*
> *(They walked back up to the house, the drive behind them checked and kept, and the morning's second small thing was done. Rose thought the drive looked the way honest work looks: nothing shining, nothing wanting, the gravel smooth and the limes lit.)*
> *(Henry made a note of the rut in his pocket book, the pencil stub short and efficient. The gardeners would see to it by noon. The round went on, and the village woke beyond the gates, and the day was the drive's, well kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the urns — the flowers, watered; the terrace's, the morning's. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The urns stood along the terrace balustrade — stone, mossed, flowers in them — and Henry took the watering can from its stand and went down the line, the soldier's care serving the garden.)*
> *(There were a dozen urns on the balustrade — she had counted them once, years ago, when the boredom of a tea had driven her to the terrace — and each had a history, or the house said so: this one from Hartwell's grandfather's planting, that one cracked in the frost of the year Rose was born and mended by a mason who was still proud of the seam. The stone held the stories the way the soil held the flowers.)*
> *(The watering can was always there, filled, waiting, because the first small thing had happened at dawn and the round's habits held. The water darkened the soil in each urn in turn, and the flowers lifted: the late roses, the asters, the small white things Rose could never name, all Hartwell-grown.)*
> *(Rose watched his hands: steady, gentle, checking as he watered. A spent rose came away between his fingers, neat. The deadheading was the day's first unglamorous mercy, and he performed it like a duty, which it was.)*
> "The urns are well," he said, setting down the can.
> *(She thought of the masquerade's bouquets — the quoted lilies, the blush roses — and of the unveiling's flowers, arranged for a triumph. These were different. Nobody photographed the urns. Nobody toasted them. They stood on the terrace through ten seasons of grand gestures and asked for nothing but water, and got it, daily, from a soldier's hands.)*
> *(There was a lesson in the urns, and Henry had learned it long before she had: the keeping was the thing. Not the gesture — the water. Not the unveiling — the morning after, and the morning after that. She touched a late rose as they turned to go, the petals cool, the blush deep, and thought of all the mornings he had done this without her noticing, the can filled, the line walked, the flowers lifting. That was the third small thing, and it was done, and tomorrow there would be another morning, and the urns would be waiting.)*

scenes.synopsis: the post — the letters, carried; the morning's, the delivered. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(They met the post boy at the gates — fourteen, red-eared, proud of the bag — and Henry took it the way he had taken dispatches, weighing it, thanking the lad by name. The boy straightened and went back down the lane, and the round noticed him, and the noticing was the point.)*
> *(They walked back up the drive, Henry carrying the bag with the dispatch case's care. Rose thought of the letters of ten seasons: the forged, the true, the ones that had changed everything. These were the morning's, ordinary — the bills, the invitations, the paper of the day — and the ordinary was the point, and she found she preferred it.)*
> *(In the hall he sorted them on the table: Harrow's pile, the house's, hers. The bills for Harrow — the thickest pile, always, the estate's honest paper, the accounts, the leases. The invitations for her — the season's social machinery. A letter in a glittering hand — Lavinia's — set aside, unopened, for the evening. The house's was the servants' own: the orders, the replies. Three piles, three worlds, and Henry sorted them without looking at the addresses, because he knew the hands, and the knowing was the care.)*
> *(The bag had come up from the village, where the postmistress sorted the Park's mail with the house's, and Henry knew her by name, as he knew the boy, as he knew everyone on the lane. The round was not only the Park's. It reached down the drive and into the village, and the village answered, daily, and the answering was the point.)*
> "The post is well," he said.
> *(Rose picked up Lavinia's letter and weighed it in her palm. Evening, she decided, setting it aside again. Some letters were for daylight and some for lamplight, and she had learned over ten seasons to tell them apart. The hall table stood ordered, the day's paper begun, and the ordinary went on being the ordinary, which was the gift.)*
> *(Henry shouldered the empty bag for the return to the gates — the dispatch case's care even for emptiness — and they walked on. The post was carried, sorted, delivered: the fourth small thing, done, and the morning's paper kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden's small things — the peas, the beds; the growing, the tended. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The kitchen garden lay beyond the stables, walled, the beds ordered, the peas on their sticks, the late beans, the herbs. The rosemary grew by the wall, grey-green, bee-loud. Henry walked the beds the way he walked the drive: steadily, seeing.)*
> *(A pea stick fallen — he set it upright. A bed weedy — he noted it for the gardeners. The gardener's boy was already at work, hoeing, and touched his hat; Henry nodded, the soldier's nod, and the boy straightened, proud, and the morning's industry went on around them.)*
> "The peas are well," Henry said.
> *(Rose thought of the Gazette's sting — the peas counted, the small things noticed — and of the season's small things, gathering. The kitchen would eat from these beds, and the house from the kitchen: the oldest economy in the world, and the morning's. The peas, the beds: the tended, the growing, and the growing was the point.)*
> *(The walled garden was the head gardener's kingdom, and he ruled it with a spade and a grudge against slugs. The pea rows were his pride — three varieties, each staked and named — and the herb beds his pharmacy: the rosemary for remembrance, the thyme for the cook, the sage for the stuffing at Christmas. He had once thrown a boot at a blackbird, Henry had said, and missed, and apologized to the bird. Rose believed it, and liked him for it. The blackbird, Henry said, had accepted the apology.)*
> *(They walked the wall's length, the rosemary, the bees, and the late beans climbing their frames, and the herbs in their rows, and the greenhouse glass catching the sun at the far end, and the compost heaps steaming quietly in their corner, the garden's own industry, the whole walled acre working. Henry set the last pea stick upright and brushed the soil from his hands, and the gardener's boy went back to his hoeing, the nod received, and the kitchen garden stood ordered — the fifth small thing, done among the bees and the rosemary — and the round went on, to the office, and the paper Park.)*

scenes.synopsis: the map — the estate's, checked; the Park, the known. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(In the estate office the map covered the wall — the Park, the zones, the paths — Harrow's honest map, and Henry stood before it with the pointer, the soldier's eye, and checked.)*
> *(The drive, the lake, the gardens, the cottages, the stables. The pointer moved, steady, missing nothing. Rose watched from the doorway: the whole Park held in a glance, paper and ink, the office smelling of the morning's work. The map had been drawn twenty years ago by a surveyor with a trembling hand and a steady eye, and Harrow had had it corrected twice since — the new cottage, the drained meadow — and the corrections showed in a different ink, a palimpsest of the Park's changes. Rose had watched Henry check it before, and the ritual never varied: the pointer, the zones, the accounting. The surveyor was long dead. The Park went on being mapped.)*
> "The Park is well," he said.
> *(Harrow looked up from his desk, the dry face.)* "The map is current, Major. The zones —" A pause. "All accounted for. The surveyor's corrections —" another pause — "in the second ink."
> "All accounted for," Henry agreed.
> *(Harrow went back to his desk, satisfied, and his clerk had not looked up from the copying through any of it — the quill scratching steady, the ledgers in rows, the estate's memory growing line by line. The office held the Park's paper self: the maps, the accounts, the leases, the honest record. Rose envied the clerk the uninterrupted line for a moment — no weather, no weeds, no mares with filled legs. Then Henry closed the office door, and the real Park was outside waiting, unreduced, and she was glad.)*
> *(The sixth small thing, done among the paper. The honest map hung, current, the zones all accounted for — and the pointer rested against the wall, and Henry stood a moment longer before the paper Park — the drive, the lake, the gardens, all accounted for, all true — and then the round went on, to the larger thing the map described, the unreduced, the real.)*

scenes.synopsis: Henry, the morning — the soldier's round; the devotion, stated. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(They stood on the terrace, the round's first hour done, and Henry reported the morning's.)*
> "The round." He straightened, the soldier's straightening. "The lanterns. The drive. The urns. The post. The —" The smallest smile. "The peas, Rose." The unguarded look. "Every day." A breath. "On purpose."
> "Henry," Rose said.
> *(He bowed over her hand, the familiar bow.)* "The small things." He straightened. "The gift —" He stopped. "Of attention, Rose. Every day. On purpose." Another stop. "The devotion —" He stopped again. "The practice, Rose."
> *(She looked at him — the soldier, thirty-three years, the honor intact, the inquiry whispers buried — and saw the resolution's shape: not the grand gesture, the daily. The lanterns, the urns, the post, the peas. The gift of attention, every day, on purpose. The practice, not the performance.)*
> "The practice," she said.
> "The practice." *(The smallest smile, the morning's.)*
> *(She had heard him report the round before — the lanterns, the drive, the urns, the post, the peas — and each time the list was a little different, a little the same, the way liturgy is different and the same. The military form held the devotion the way the watering can held the water: a container, not the thing. The thing was the hands.)*
> *(The devotion was stated, the practice named, and the morning held them both. She watched him walk back toward the drive, the soldier's steady tread, and thought that thirty-three years had taught him what ten seasons had taught her: the practice was the devotion, and the devotion was the daily, kept. Not performance. The distinction was the whole of it, and Henry had lived it before she had named it.)*
> *(The inquiry whispers were buried — the old scandal, the questions, the ton's long memory — and what remained was the man: the boots on the gravel, the hands on the can, the smallest smile. He had been the soldier in disgrace and the soldier restored, and now he was simply the soldier, and the terrace brightened around them, and the devotion was the day's — stated, named, kept, and the keeping was the practice.)*

scenes.synopsis: the breakfast — the small service; the morning's, the served. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(They breakfasted in the morning room — the small service, the served — and the round's first hour was reviewed over chocolate.)*
> *(The chocolate, properly hot. The bread, fresh. The butter, the honey. Laid by the maids, served without fuss, eaten without haste. Henry ate the soldier's breakfast — neatly, completely — and Rose ate with an appetite the morning air had given her, and the morning room was warm, the sun in the windows.)*
> *(They talked of the round: the rut in the drive, the weedy bed, the post boy's new boots. The chocolate was good. The bread was good. The day was good. The chocolate pot was the morning room's own, dented, older than Rose, and the cook swore by it. The honey came from the Park's hives, the bread from the village oven, the butter from the dairy. Everything on the table had a provenance, and Rose knew them all, and the knowing was part of the eating — the small service, served from the estate's own hands, eaten without haste, the morning's own pace.)*
> *(Letitia swept through on her way to the stables, kissed Rose's forehead, stole a piece of bread, and swept out, the morning's whirlwind.)* "Devotions!" she called over her shoulder. "I approve! Carry on!"
> *(Rose laughed, and Henry's smallest smile appeared, and the maids cleared around them, unhurried, the morning room's own rhythm. Henry buttered his bread with the same economy he brought to the dahlia stake. Rose watched him and thought that the soldier's breakfast was the round in miniature: neat, complete, unhurried, everything taken, nothing wasted. The morning room emptied, the sun moved higher in the windows, and she thought of all the breakfasts of ten seasons — the tense, the hungover, the triumphant — and liked this one best: the small service, the eaten, the day reviewed over chocolate and found good. Letitia's stolen bread, the rut and the weedy bed and the new boots all accounted for. Fed and steady, they went back to the round, and the day was the morning's, well begun, and the round's first hour complete, the chocolate drunk to the dregs.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE DEVOTION'S FORM (how Rose honors the devotions: by noticing, by joining, or by naming). The morning deepens; decide the honoring. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning deepened, and the devotions asked their honoring. The round's first hour was done — the lanterns, the drive, the urns, the post, the peas — and Rose walked beside Henry, and the question was how to honor what he did.)*
> *(By noticing: the seeing, the attention's. To watch the round, to see every small thing, to let the seeing be the gift's mirror. The lanterns checked, the urns watered, the post carried: seen, truly seen. The attention, returned. But seeing is apart, and the devotions want the with, and the watcher is not the walker, and the gift wants the sharing.)*
> *(By joining: the doing, the round's. To walk beside him, to carry the can, to check the lanterns, to make the round the two's. The sharing complete, the doing shared. The boots and the slippers, the gravel together. But joining is doing, and the devotions were the gift, and the gift wants receiving, not matching, and the doing is his.)*
> *(By naming: the saying, the gift's. To say it aloud, the gift of attention, to name the devotion for what it is. The saying is the truth, spoken. The words, the frame. But sayings are words, and the devotions were the doing, and the doing speaks its own language, quieter than words.)*
> *(Henry walked on, steady, unaware of the philosophy happening beside him, which was — Rose thought — exactly the point. The devotions did not ask to be honored. They asked to be continued. The lanterns, the urns, the post, the peas: the doing, daily.)*
> *(The morning deepened. The honoring was hers to choose, and the choosing would shape the day's every hour. Noticing, joining, naming: each true, each incomplete. The devotions asked, and the morning waited.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The devotion's form:*
- **By noticing** — *the seeing, honored.* Rose honors by noticing — every small thing, seen. (Consequence: the seeing is the gift's mirror — but seeing is apart, and the devotions want the with.)
- **By joining** — *the doing, shared.* Rose honors by joining — the round, walked together. (Consequence: the sharing is complete — but joining is doing, and the devotions were the gift.)
- **By naming** — *the saying, spoken.* Rose honors by naming — the gift of attention, said aloud. (Consequence: the saying is the truth — but sayings are words, and the devotions were the doing.)
> *(She chose, and the choosing was quiet, and the day went on.)*
> *(The devotions' form was hers, as the round was Henry's. Noticing, joining, naming: whichever she had chosen, the honoring was true. The small things continued, every day, on purpose, and she honored them her way. The morning deepened, and the round went on, and the honoring held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the midday — the small things, continuing; the day's, the steady. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The sun stood directly overhead, and the Park lay bright and still beneath it, and the shadows had gone to nothing — the one hour of the day when nothing hid — and Henry's round went on through it, and the midday asked nothing of anyone, and gave nothing back but the light, and the light was enough.)*
> *(They checked the terrace again — the urns, the morning's watering holding, the soil still dark. They walked the garden's edge — the beds in the midday sun, the dahlias bright, the bees loud. Rose walked with him, the honoring hers as she had chosen, and the small things were the steady's.)*
> "The midday," Henry said, "is the round's truest hour."
> "Truer than the dawn?"
> "The dawn promises. The evening counts." He bent, once, to straighten a fallen dahlia stake, the soldier's economy. "The noon only continues."
> *(Rose thought he was right, and filed it. The morning had been the beginning's, full of promise; the evening would be the counting's. The noon was neither. It was the practice itself, done in bright sun, with no witness but the bees — and she thought of the morning's lanterns, quenched at dawn, and of the evening's, waiting to be lit, and of the afternoon holding between them, bright and still, and the devotions held, steady, every day, on purpose. The bees worked the garden's edge, loud in the heat, and the dahlias nodded over them, and the air smelled of cut grass and hot stone. The midday was the round's truest hour because it was the least romantic: no dawn's promise, no dusk's counting, only the work, in the heat, with the bees.)*
> *(They walked on, the noon bright around them, the lake glittering at the Park's edge, the gardens glowing, the urns holding their water, and the shadows gone to nothing, and the hour was the continuing's — the small things done, in the sun, needing no other reason, and the day was the midday's, steady, and the round went on through the heat, the checked, the tended, the noon's, the practice in the heat.)*

scenes.synopsis: the stables — the horses, checked; the midday's, the groomed. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The stable yard smelled of hay and leather and horses, the good smell, and the grooms touched their hats, and Henry went down the boxes with the soldier's knowledge, the horses' heads coming over the doors, the nickering, the midday sun in the yard.)*
> *(He checked each: the legs, the eyes, the feed, the water. A mare with a filled leg — he noted it, for the farrier. A gelding off his feed — he noted that too, the feed to be changed, the appetite coaxed. The knowledge served the horses the way it served everything: steadily, completely, the soldier's eye missing nothing.)*
> "The horses are well," Henry said, "barring the mare's leg and the gelding's appetite, which are noted, and will be seen to."
> "Noted," Rose agreed.
> *(The head groom walked with them, the report given: the shoeing done, the feed ordered, the new hay in. He had been at the Park longer than Henry, and the two men spoke the short language of people who both know horses — the leg, the shoe, the feed — and Rose listened, and learned the mare's name was Jess, and that Jess had filled the leg before, in the spring, and it had passed.)*
> *(Rose stood in the yard's sun and thought of ten seasons of horses: the arrivals, the departures, the hunting mornings. These were the Park's, the kept, the midday's. She ran her hand down a bay's neck as they left, the coat warm, the nickering soft, and made a note in her head, the ledger-mind, automatic: farrier, feed, the midday's two exceptions. The rest were well — the legs, the eyes, the water — the groomed and the fed, and the good smell hung in the yard behind them.)*
> *(The mare would see the farrier by evening; the gelding would be watched. The two were noted, and would be seen to, and the rest were well — the legs, the eyes, the water. The round went on, and the midday held, and the horses were kept, and the good smell hung in the yard behind them, hay and leather and horses.)*

scenes.synopsis: the cottages — the people, visited; the midday's, the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The estate cottages stood along the lane, the gardens neat, the chimneys smoking, and Henry knocked at each door the way he did everything: steadily, kindly. The lane was quiet, the midday's, and every door opened.)*
> *(An old woman with a bad leg: the leg asked after, the liniment noted, and they left a basket at her door — the kitchen's, the cook's serene generosity. A child with a lost shoe: the shoe found under the bed, the child triumphant, waving it as they left. A man mending a fence: the fence admired, the mending discussed at length, and the fence-mender touched his hat.)*
> *(There were six cottages on the lane, and they knocked at every one. A widow with a new grandchild: the grandchild admired, the name learned. A laborer with a cough: the cough listened to, the doctor mentioned. The lane's quiet held them, and Henry's knock, steady and kind, opened every door, and Rose stood in the doorways and listened, and the mistress's listening was the keeping's own.)*
> *(The lane was the Park's oldest road, older than the house, and the cottages had stood along it for two hundred years — the gardens neat, the chimneys smoking, the generations turning over like soil. Henry had walked it as a boy, Rose knew, before the army, before the disgrace, before the return. The knocking was older than the soldier.)*
> *(Rose stood in the doorways, the mistress, the keeper, and listened. Henry knew every name, every ailment, every fence — the soldier's memory, serving the peace — and she thought of how the peace was kept the same way the Park was kept: by knowing, and by knocking.)*
> *(They walked back up the lane, and the cottages stood in their neat gardens, and the chimneys smoked, and the midday's peace held. The old woman's liniment, the child's shoe, the fence-mender's pride, the widow's grandchild, the laborer's cough: the human's small things, asked after and noted, the basket, the shoe, the fence — the midday's human account, balanced, every door knocked, every door opened — and the round went on, to the lake.)*

scenes.synopsis: the lake — the water, watched; the midday's, the flat. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The lake at midday was the day's stillest hour — the water flat, the noon sun silvered on it, the light lying flat, the gardens sloping down, the house on its hill behind. They stood at the edge, and the small things were the silvered, and the watching was the gift, the stillness the keeping.)*
> *(They stood at the lake's edge at midday, and the water lay flat, the noon sun on it, silvered, and the noon's stillness lay over the water like a held breath.)*
> *(A moorhen crossed, the wake spreading behind it in a long V. Henry stood in the soldier's stillness, watching the water the way he watched everything: completely, without fidget. Rose stood beside him, the honoring hers, and the watching was shared between them, quiet. They did not speak. The lake did not need it, and neither did they.)*
> *(A fish rose, the rings spreading, gone before the rings finished, the water closing over it like a kept secret. The moorhen reached the reeds and vanished.
> *(The gardens sloped down to the water, the Park's green, the house on its hill behind, reflected in the flat silver. Henry checked the lake's edge path for fallen branches as they left, the soldier's completeness, and found none. The water stayed, flat and silvered, and the midday held it.)* Rose thought of all the lakes of ten seasons — the frozen, the moonlit, the storm-dark — and of how this one asked nothing: flat water, noon sun, the moorhen's wake spreading. The watching was the gift, the stillness the keeping.)*
> *(The fish rose again farther out, the rings spreading wider, and Henry watched the rings finish before he turned away, the soldier's completeness even in idleness. They came up from the lake's edge to the garden's slope, and Rose looked back once: the flat silver, the reeds, the house reflected, the moorhen out again, the wake spreading. The lake asked nothing and kept everything, and the watching had been the gift, and the midday held, and the water stayed behind them, flat and silvered, the noon's own, the stillest hour.)*

scenes.synopsis: the garden — the beds, walked; the midday's, the blooming. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The flower garden lay in its order, the beds bright, the order complete, the late roses, the asters, the dahlias, and Henry walked the paths, the soldier's eye, the blooms checked, the petals counted. A dahlia past its best — he deadheaded it, neat. A rose with blackspot — he noted it for the gardeners, the leaf to be burned, not composted.)*
> *(The head gardener was at work, the hat touched, the morning's report given: the beds well, the blooms well, the Park's pride intact. He walked with them a little way, the hat in his hands now, and talked of the dahlias: the new variety, the color holding, the show next month. Henry listened the way he listened to everything — completely — and asked after the blackspot, and the gardener brightened, grateful to be asked, the blackspot a shared enemy.)
> *(The show next month was the county's, and the head gardener had his eye on a prize for the new dahlia — the color holding, the form true — and Henry wished him luck with the gravity of a man who understands competition. Rose thought of the Hartwell rose in the walled garden, the legacy literal and living, the breeding's work across the seasons, and of how the Park's color was kept by many hands: the gardeners', Henry's, the bees'.)**
> *(Rose bent to a late rose, the blush deep, the petals perfect, and thought of the Hartwell rose in the walled garden, the legacy literal and living. The Park's color was kept by many hands: the gardeners', Henry's, the bees'. She thought of the masquerade's quoted bouquet, the unveiling's flowers, the urns' morning watering — the garden was the Park's color, and the color was kept, daily, the blooming the kept, the tended.)*
> *(They left the garden to the bees, loud in the midday heat, the dahlia deadheaded, the blackspot noted, the dahlias discussed, the show wished. The beds stood bright, the Park's pride intact — the color kept, daily, by the gardeners' hands and Henry's eye — and the round went on, to the afternoon, the color kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the day's thesis — dress the small things; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief — The daily devotions:** "A day of small things. The lanterns, the urns, the post, the peas. Dress for the daily — the attention's, the practice's. **Editorial criterion: attention.**"
>
> **A. The Attention** — dove grey, the morning's; the noticer, the honored. Motif: the eyelet, small and exact — the attention, embroidered. Thread: **silver** (the exact, edged) / **dove silk** (the morning, matched) / **pearl** (the attentive, lit). Colorway: dove grey + silver + pearl. Accessories: a silver ribbon; the grandmother's pearls, at rest; grey kid gloves.
> **B. The Practice** — deep blue, the round's; the joiner, the doing. Motif: the footstep, stitched at the hem — the practice, embroidered. Thread: **silver** (the steady, edged) / **blue silk** (the round, matched) / **cream** (the honest, lit). Colorway: deep blue + silver + cream. Accessories: a silver hair comb; no pendant — the throat, plain; blue kid gloves.
> **C. The Quiet** — green, the garden's; the namer, the saying. Motif: the leaf, small at the cuff — the quiet, embroidered. Thread: **gold** (the landed, stated) / **green silk** (the garden, matched) / **pearl** (the quiet, lit). Colorway: green + gold + pearl. Accessories: a gold ribbon; pearl drop earrings; green kid gloves.
>
> *(The dressing room, the daily's morning: the small things' dress. She dresses the way the attention asks: the noticer, the joiner, the namer.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the attention, the practice, or the quiet — the day's thesis, remembered. The hair, practical for the round. The accessories, exact. The mirror, to be passed with attention. **Direction.** A day of small things — dress for the daily. **Editorial criterion.** Attention — every choice must answer the small, not the grand.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the day. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*

> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, practical:** the attentive — the round's, the walked, the small things' in cloth. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** the doer's — the round's, the tending, giving nothing to the brambles. *5 coins.*
> *(The pins accumulate — the gown's line set, the doer's sleeves — and the dressing room holds its morning the way the round holds its small things: attentively.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, modest:** the woman's — the attention asks for the serious, and the serious is the woman. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, practical:** the round's — the walked, the kept; the wind's none. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Ribbon, throat's:** the direction's punctuation — silver, silver, or gold — the attention, tied. *5 coins.*
> *(The throat's ribbon tied — the attention's knot — and the morning leans in, the round waiting.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, working:** the doer's gauntlets — expected, and the round's. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Boots, walking:** the round's — the Park's length, the worn. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Shawl, warm:** the morning's — the round's air, the doer's wrap. *5 coins.*
> *(Working gloves, walking boots, the warm shawl — the attention asks for the doing, and she gives it.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, small:** the noticer's — the seen, the unshowy; the woman's, not the grand's. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** the day's — the Park smells of morning; the lady adds nothing. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, attentive:** the attention's — the noticing, the stood; the spine's, easy. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine attends — the noticing, stood — and the mirror is passed with attention from the corner of her eye.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, noticing:** the noticer's — the small things, the seen. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, quiet:** the attention's — the day's, the unhurried. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, doing:** the doer's — the tending, the kept. *5 coins.*
> *(Noticing gaze, quiet voice, doing hands — the attention's instruments, tuned for the day.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, with:** the round's — the walked-together, the shared. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, quiet:** the attention's — the noticed, the priced. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Nod, to the small:** the day's answer — the tended, the returned. *5 coins.*
> *(The step with, the smile quiet, the nod to the small — the day's own grammar, spoken fluently.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Turn, at the urns:** the tended — the watered, the seen. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — Door, the garden's:** the day's — passed, attending closer, the attention's. *5 coins.*

> *(Story morsel: Henry at the garden door, waiting — "The round, Rose. The small things. Today —" the smallest smile — "today, counted.")*
> *(Story morsel: the urns, watered — the day's first small things, the flowers'.)*

scenes.synopsis: the afternoon — the devotions, the quiet; the day's, the deepening. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The lime walk was a tunnel of gold and green, the leaves turning overhead, the light coming through in shafts, and they walked the Park's west where the sun slanted and the shadows lengthened, and the afternoon was the day's hinge.)
> *(The limes had been planted by Hartwell's grandfather, a double row, and the walk was the Park's cathedral — the gold and green, the shafts of light, the leaves turning. Henry checked the west urns' brackets as well as the soil — the glass, the oil, the iron — the soldier's completeness even in the afternoon's ease, because the afternoon's ease was not an excuse.)**
> *(Henry checked the west terrace urns — the afternoon's sun full on them, the morning's watering holding — the brackets, the glass, the oil, the soldier's completeness even in the afternoon's ease. Rose picked up the watering can. It was heavier than it looked, the water sloshing, and she carried it to the farthest urn, the one the morning's round had watered lightest, and watered it herself, and felt the can's weight in her hands, and watched the water pour.)*
> "The west urn," Henry said, "was the morning's lightest."
> "I noticed," Rose said. "Noticing is the honoring. Or the joining. I have not decided which."
> *(The smallest smile.)* "The urn does not mind which."
> *(The can was heavy, and her arms knew it by the farthest urn, and she thought of Henry carrying it every morning without comment, the way he carried everything — the bag, the hamper, the round. The weight was the devotion’s own, and he had never once set it down in front of her.)*
> *(She set the can down, and they walked the lime walk's length, the gold and green overhead, the long light on the gravel. The morning's work was done and the evening's not yet begun, and the round went on through the hinge anyway, steady, because the devotions did not pause. They simply continued, every day, on purpose, and the lime walk glowed behind them, gold and green, and the afternoon deepened, and the west was walked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the library — the books, the maps; the afternoon's, the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library smelled of leather and dust and time, the good smell, and the books stood in their ranks, the maps in their cases, and Henry went along the shelves with the soldier's order: the dusted, the straightened, the kept.)*
> *(A book shelved wrong — he righted it. A map case ajar — he closed it. Rose watched from the window seat, the afternoon light on the shelves, the dust motes in the light. The library was the house's memory, the paper kept, and Henry kept it the way he kept the Park: daily, completely.)*
> *(Harrow's clerk looked up from the desk, nodded, went back to the copying — the quill scratching, the copying endless, the house's paper memory growing line by line. Rose thought of the ledgers in the estate office, the accounts balanced, the day's devotions waiting to be written down — the paper kept, the daily recorded.)
> *(The library held the atlases too, the great folio volumes, and Rose remembered Henry poring over them once, years ago, tracing a campaign's route with one finger — the soldier's geography, the paper wars. The maps in their cases were the Park's; the atlases were the world's. Both were kept the same way: dusted, straightened, the soldier's order.)**
> *(Henry ran a finger along a shelf, checked for dust, found none, and nodded to himself. The books stood in their ranks like soldiers on parade, the maps lay in their cases like folded orders. The soldier's order served the paper, and the paper held the house's memory.)*
> *(She rose from the window seat, and ran a finger along a shelf of estate ledgers, the leather worn, the years in rows, the ink brown with age. The library kept the house's memory the way Henry kept the Park: daily, completely, the dusted and the straightened. They left the clerk to his copying, and the round went on, and the books stood, and the maps lay.)
> *(The globe stood in the corner, the world in miniature, and Henry spun it once with one finger as they left — the oceans turning, the continents — and caught it, and steadied it, the way he steadied everything.)**

scenes.synopsis: the ballroom — the floor, walked; the forty paces, the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The tall windows threw the daylight in bars across the shining floor, and Henry walked the ballroom's length, counting under his breath, the soldier's habit, and Rose matched her stride to his — boots on the boards, slippers on the boards: two sounds, one measure.)*
> "Thirty-eight," Henry said. "Thirty-nine. Forty."
> *(They turned at the far wall and walked back. The footmen had polished the floor that morning, on their knees, the wax, the cloths — the daily's labor, invisible by afternoon, the shine the only witness. Rose thought of the masquerade's night: the candlelight, the French airs, the dancers' feet turning where they walked. The same boards had held both, the grand and the daily, and asked nothing of either.)*
> "The floor remembers," she said.
> "The floor," Henry said, "is polished. The remembering is ours."
> *(They walked the forty paces back, the dust motes turning in the light. She thought of the unmasking at midnight — Laurent's hand setting the mask down, the hall's sigh — and of this afternoon's quiet: the daylight, the polish, the counted paces. The ballroom had held the old world's farewell. Now it held the round's measure, and the measure was the devotion's own.)
> *(The chandeliers hung dark above them, the candles unlit, the crystal catching the daylight in small fires. The musicians' gallery stood empty at the far end, the chairs stacked, the music stands folded. The ballroom at rest was a held breath — the grandeur waiting, patient, for the next night it would be asked to be grand.)**
> *(The portrait was not here. It hung where she had named it, in the chosen place, the laugh in paint. The ballroom held the floor, the light, the forty paces, and that was enough. Some rooms held the triumph. This one held only the walking — the counted, the polished, the kept — and they left the floor shining, and the round went on.)
> *(The parquet's pattern ran in diamonds under the polish, the wood dark and light, and Rose had danced on it, and unmasked on it, and now she walked it, counting, and the floor held all three the same way.)**

scenes.synopsis: the portrait — the hung, visited; the afternoon's, the truest. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(They went to the chosen place in the afternoon, and the round paused, and the afternoon light moved slow over the picnic, the laugh, the two houses on the hill.)*
> *(Henry stood before it in the soldier's stillness, his hands behind his back, and looked at the laughing woman the way he looked at everything: completely, without fidget, missing nothing.)*
> "The truest thing," he said quietly. "The painter saw."
> "She saw," Rose agreed.
> *(She thought of the picnic itself — the blanket, the slope, the wasps — and of Henry somewhere at its edge that day, unnoticed, the way he was unnoticed everywhere, doing whatever the day had asked of him. He had probably carried something. He always carried something. The painter had painted the laugh, and the soldier had carried the hamper, and between them the day had been the day.)*
> "Were you there?" she asked. "At the picnic. In the paint, I mean."
> *(The smallest smile.)* "I carried the hamper, Rose. The paint has the laugh. The hamper is not painted."
> *(She laughed, and the painted laugh laughed, and the soldier's stillness was his witnessing: the standing, the seeing, held without adornment. Octavia had caught the laugh in months of chasing. Henry had kept the Park in years of doing. The laugh was the day's, forever. The keeping was the every-day's, forever. The afternoon light moved over both — the painted woman, the standing soldier — and the chosen place held them.)*
> *(The light caught the brass plaque beneath the frame — the name lettered, the naming permanent — and Rose read it again, slowly, the way one reads a stone.
> *(The gilt edge caught the light, and the picnic shone: the blanket, the slope, the two houses on the hill, the laugh. Henry's stillness beside her was the reverence, unadorned, and the laugh had received it. The round had paused to honor the forever, and the honoring was the pause itself.)* They left the laugh shining, and the round went on. The visited, the seen: the portrait's afternoon, the devotion's pause, the afternoon's own, the kept, the honored.)*

scenes.synopsis: the bloom — the rose, checked; the afternoon's, the opening. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(In the walled garden, the Hartwell's own, the bud was opening on its own time — the green casing split, the color showing within, not open, not closed, the in-between that gardeners watch the way soldiers watch weather.)*
> *(Henry bent to it with the soldier's gentleness, and checked: the stem, the leaves, the bud.)*
> "The bloom is well," he said.
> *(Rose bent beside him, and counted. Five buds on the stem, two showing color, three still tight. The ledger-mind, automatic: five, two, three. The gardeners had said it would be full by the final assembly, and she believed them, and she counted anyway, because counting was the attention's own.)*
> "Five," she said. "Two showing."
> "The gardeners say the assembly," Henry said. "The season's last."
> *(The head gardener had promised it himself, the bud's opening timed like a campaign — the pruning in March, the feeding in May, the watching, daily. The gardeners knew the rose the way Henry knew the Park: by the doing, not the naming.)*
> *(The gardeners would cut the first open bloom for the house, the way they always did, and leave the rest for the final assembly. She touched the bud's green casing, lightly, with one finger. It was firm, cool, the color showing like a promise kept in stages. The walled garden stood quiet around them, the legacy literal and living: the breeding, the tending, the years.)*
> *(She thought of the legacy as the gardeners knew it: the work. The pruning in March, the feeding in May, the watching, daily. The rose did not know it was a legacy. It only knew the sun, the water, the season. That was the whole of it, and it was enough.)*
> "It will be cut for the assembly," she said. "Carried in from the garden."
> "The gardeners will cut it," Henry said. "The bloom full. The color —" he stopped, looking at the bud — "the color as it should be."
> *(They left it to its opening, the five buds, the two showing color, the green casing split. The walled garden's quiet held, and the round went on, and the bloom was well, and the season's last triumph approached on its own time, daily, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: Letitia, on the devotions — the aunt, the day's; the quartermaster, the small. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia found them in the walled garden, the hawk's eyes warm, the quartermaster seeing the small.)*
> "Darling." She took in the round, the rose, Henry's straight back. "The round. The —" She gestured, the whole Park. "The small things, darling. All day." She took Rose's hands. "The quartermaster —" A laugh. "The quartermaster mapped the war, darling. Henry —" The warm look. "Henry maps the peace. The —" She stopped. "The daily, darling. The devotion." She squeezed, the rings winking. "Notice it, darling. It's —" Another stop. "The truest thing."
> "I am noticing, Aunt," Rose said.
> "Good. Noticing is the whole of it." *(Letitia turned to Henry.)* "Major. The lanterns, the urns, the post, the peas. The quartermaster —" The warm eyes. "The quartermaster salutes you."
> *(Henry bowed, the soldier's bow, and Letitia patted his cheek, and swept off, the day's whirlwind.
> *(The quartermaster had mapped real wars, once — the dispatches, the lines, the true reports — and now she mapped this one, the peace, with the same warm eyes. Rose thought of the aunt's seeing as the day's truest commendation, and of how the hawk's eyes, warm, missed nothing, the way Henry's missed nothing.)*
> *(The pat on Henry's cheek had been the aunt's own salute — no parade, no formality, just the hand, the warmth. The soldier had bowed, and the quartermaster had patted, and the garden had witnessed.)* The walled garden's quiet returned, and the rose opened, and the round went on.)*
> *(The hawk's eyes had been warm, the quartermaster seeing the small. Letitia had mapped wars, and now she mapped peace — the lanterns, the urns, the post, the peas — and her salute was the day's truest commendation. Rose watched her go, the whirlwind, the warmth, and thought the quartermaster metaphor was exact: the shortest war report, and the best. The daily's devotion, saluted.)*
> *(Henry stood a little straighter after the salute, the soldier's pride, and Rose squeezed his arm. The aunt's seeing, the day's: the devotion noticed, named the truest thing. Letitia's warmth stayed in the garden after she left, the hawk's eyes, the squeeze of the hands, the pat on Henry's cheek — and the garden's quiet held, and the rose opened, and the round went on.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE SMALL THINGS' KEEPING (how the devotions are kept: in a book, in the doing, or in the telling). The afternoon deepens; decide the keeping. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The afternoon deepened, and the small things asked their keeping. The round was nearly walked — the lanterns, the urns, the post, the peas, the map, the horses, the cottages, the lake, the garden, the books, the floor, the portrait, the bloom — and the keeping waited.)*
> *(In a book: the written, the recorded. Every small thing, written down, the day's account, the ledger's. The written is permanent, the record kept. The fourteen devotions, the fourteen gifts. But books are read, and the devotions were the doing, and the doing is not the writing, and the record is not the round.)*
> *(In the doing: the practiced, the daily. Every day, practiced, the round walked, the small things done. The practiced is the truth, the devotion's own. The boots on the gravel, the hands on the can. But doings pass, and the memory wants the keeping, and the keeping wants a shape, and the shape is hers to choose.)*
> *(In the telling: the spoken, the shared. The gift, spoken, the devotion told. The spoken is shared, the attention given words. The naming, the frame. But tellings are words, and the devotions were the attention, and the attention is quieter than words, and the quiet is the point.)*
> *(Henry walked on, steady, the round's end approaching, unaware of the philosophy. The devotions did not ask to be kept. They asked to be continued. But Rose was the keeper, and the keeping was hers to choose. The afternoon deepened, and the keeping waited.)*
> *(The light slanted lower. The book, the doing, the telling: each true, each incomplete. The keeping was hers, as the doing was Henry's. The keeping would shape the devotions' memory, and the memory would shape the years — and the afternoon waited, and the keeping waited with it.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The small things' keeping:*
- **In a book** — *the written, recorded.* The devotions are kept in a book — every small thing, written. (Consequence: the written is permanent — but books are read, and the devotions were the doing.)
- **In the doing** — *the practiced, daily.* The devotions are kept in the doing — every day, practiced. (Consequence: the practiced is the truth — but doings pass, and the memory wants the keeping.)
- **In the telling** — *the spoken, shared.* The devotions are kept in the telling — the gift, spoken. (Consequence: the spoken is shared — but tellings are words, and the devotions were the attention.)
> *(She chose, and the choosing was quiet, and the round went on.)*
> *(The small things' keeping was hers, as the doing was Henry's. The book, the doing, the telling: whichever she had chosen, the keeping was true. The devotions would be kept her way, every day, on purpose. The afternoon deepened, and the round went on, and the keeping held.)*

scenes.synopsis: Augusta, on Henry — the Dowager, the day's; the line, the soldier. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta received them in the drawing room, the spectacles, the seventy-two, the line seeing the soldier.)*
> "The round." She looked at Henry, the direct. "The —" A pause. "The small things, child. All day." She looked at Rose. The blackbird sang from the lime walk. The Park was the round's ground, and the round was the Park's keeping, and the morning was the daily's own, the tended.)*
> *(She stopped at the lake's edge, and looked back: the house on its hill, the gardens dewed, the terrace stones cool in the morning's light. The whole of it, held in a glance — the way the map held it, but larger, and breathing. The paper Park was the honest one. The real Park was the kept one, the breathing. She walked home through the tended whole, the blackbird singing in the lime walk, and the Park walked with her, kept, and the round went on.)*

scenes.synopsis: the woman, the daily's — Rose, the morning's; the mistress, the attention's. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Her bedroom, the morning: she sat at the window, the Park beyond, the round's, and the day was the woman's quiet.)*
> *(Below, the Park woke: the lake's flat silver, the gardens' green, the terrace's stones, the gardeners at the beds, the blackbird in the lime walk. Henry was somewhere in it — the drive, the urns, the round — doing the small things, every day, on purpose. She did not need to see him. The Park's keeping was the proof.)*
> *(She sat, and the morning light lay on the window seat, and she thought of the attention as her own devotion: the mistress's, the seeing's. Henry kept the Park by doing. She kept it by noticing. The round was his. The watching was hers. Between them, the Park was held.)*
> *(The small things counted, the meaning decided, the devotion honored. The day behind her was complete; the morning ahead was daily. She had honored the devotions her way — by watching, by doing, and once, by saying — and the honoring had been true, and the day had balanced, and the night had received the count. She was the daily's woman now, the attention's mistress, whole: the woman at the window, watching the Park wake, the round going on below, every day, on purpose, and her part in it the seeing, the attention's own.)*
> *(The window glass was cool against her palm. Below, a gardener's barrow rattled on the terrace path, and a door closed somewhere in the house, and the morning went on being the morning, and she sat in the middle of it, quiet, in no hurry to be anywhere else. Her hands rested on the window seat, empty, and she thought of Octavia's empty hands after the triumph — the finishing, the strange part — and of Henry's full ones, the can, the brackets. The seeing was her keeping. The hands could rest, the keeping done.)*
> *(She sat a while longer, and then she rose, and went down to the day. The window stayed, the morning stayed, the Park woke, and the round went on, the daily's own.)*

scenes.synopsis: the small things, the season's — the gathering; every day, on purpose. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(She sat at the window, the morning's, and gathered the season's small things one by one — the year's whole harvest — and the gathering was the season's sum.)*
> *(The balls had been the season's grandeur, the reckonings its trials, the portraits its triumphs. But beneath them, the small things had gone on: the lanterns, the urns, the post, the peas. Every day, on purpose. The season's sum was the daily's.)*
> *(She gathered them the way one gathers flowers: carefully, completely. The lanterns lit in the November rain, the glass steaming. The urns watered in the August heat, the soil cracking by noon. The post carried through the March mud, the bag heavy on the shoulder. The peas staked in the May wind, the sticks leaning, set upright again.)*
> *(The map checked in the lamplight, the pointer steady. The horses checked in the frost, the breath steaming in the boxes. The cottages visited in the snow, the lane white, the knock answered. The lake watched in the freeze, the ice holding, the moorhen gone south. The garden walked in the thaw, the first green showing. The books kept through it all, the quill scratching. The floor walked in the candlelight, the forty paces. The bloom watched, the bud tight, then showing, then open.)*
> *(Ten seasons of small things, and this season's the gathered. Nobody had applauded the lanterns in the rain. Nobody had toasted the urns in the heat. The devotions had not asked to be honored. They had asked to be continued — and they had been, every day, on purpose, and the continuing was the whole of it.)*
> *(The gathering was complete: the year's devotions, the daily's own — the lanterns, the urns, the post, the peas, and all the rest, gathered carefully, completely, the season's small things, the kept. She sat at the window, and the Park woke, and the round went on. Below, Henry's boots crunched on the terrace gravel, steady, and the watering can caught the morning's light, and the day began — every day, on purpose — and the small things went on being done.)*

scenes.synopsis: Bell's quiet report — the unnoticed, noticed; arch, precise; reward-only, never mystery. (Turns: 1 — the reading)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning Gazette, read over chocolate. Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, in her own dry voice:)*
> *"The Gazette — having counted the balls, the concessions, and the portraits — turns today to the uncounted: the lanterns lit, the urns watered, the post carried, every day, on purpose. A soldier keeps the Park. The Gazette — which notices everything — notices this."*
> (T1 · stance) *Rose reads it twice — the amusement first (the peas! counted!), then the reckoning: the devotions are pronounced noticed in print as well as in the round's light, and Bell has made the small things permanent, which is Bell's way of making them matter. She files the sting under its lesson: in London, the small thing the Gazette notices is the small thing that's large.* — remembered: *the lesson: the small thing the Gazette notices is the small thing that's large.*

scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, and the letter comes — the glittering hand, Lavinia's — and brilliance writes.)*
> *(She opens it — the glittering letter, the loyal — and Lavinia's final beat begins: the advance guard's last brilliance, the loyal's.)*
> "Darling —" the letter, the glittering — "the young are restless, and the Season —" she reads — "the Season wants its last brilliance. I'm —" another line — "planning something, darling. Glittering. Loyal. Final." The letter's last line — "For the house, darling. For you."
> *(She folds the letter — the glittering, the loyal — and the final beat approaches: Lavinia's last brilliance, the loyal's.)*
> "The last brilliance." She looks at the letter — the glittering hand, the loyal. "For the house."
> *(The chapter closes on the letter — the glittering hand, the loyal — and the Season turns toward Lavinia: the final glittering beat — and the Season holds its breath.)*
