scenes.synopsis: the charter, continued — the founding's work; the morning, the written. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at seven, and the charter continued — the founding's work, taken up where the night left it. Rose sits at the desk with the household book open to the blank pages at the back, and the heading she wrote a week ago —* The Hartwell Assembly *— stands at the top of the page like a door not yet opened.)*
> *(She reads it over once, the way she reads everything: for the true weight. The heading is a promise. This morning she begins to keep it. The pen — the good pen, the one Quill gave her when the settlement was enrolled — moves across the page in her ledger-hand, and the charter takes its first shape: the annual house party and ball, convened by her, on her terms.)*
> *(The terms come first, because terms are the spine. Not a Season's entertainment, hired and forgotten. An *institution*: the house party in summer, the ball at its height, the guests convened — not invited, *convened* — by the mistress of Hartwell Park. She writes it plainly, the way Quill writes: no ornament, no apology. The plainness is the point. Ornament can be argued with. Plainness can only be answered.)*
> *(A footman brings chocolate, and she drinks it without tasting it, the way she has drunk chocolate through ten seasons of mornings that mattered. Outside, the Park does its morning work — the gardeners at the beds, the grooms at the yard — unaware that inside the library, at the desk, the ton's future is being chartered one line at a time.)*
> "The annual," she says aloud, testing it. The word holds. "The *convened*." That holds too. She writes them both into the charter's margin, and underlines them once — not twice, the way Lavinia underlines; once is enough for a founding.
> *(By eight the first page is full, and the second begun, and the founding's work — the morning, the written — has the particular momentum of things that were always going to happen. The Assembly is taking shape. The charter is being written. And Rose — twenty-five, mistress of the finished whole — is doing what she has always done: building the institution first, and letting the brilliance follow.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quartermaster, on the founding — Letitia, the charter's; strategy, the annual's. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room at nine, and Letitia summoned to inspect the charter. She arrives with the Gazette folded unopened under her arm, and Rose understands this is the highest compliment in the aunt's repertoire: the news can wait. The founding cannot.)*
> "Darling." Letitia reads the pages through twice, the hawk's eyes moving fast. She sets them down with unusual care. "Well. The quartermaster approves."
> "Entirely?" Rose pours the chocolate. "Or with the usual reservations, to be revealed at the worst possible moment?"
> "Entirely." Letitia cradles her cup, and the warm look comes with the grave one underneath. "Do you know why? Because it is the masterstroke, darling. Ten seasons we have *attended* things — balls, routs, breakfasts, other people's brilliance on other people's terms." She taps the charter with one finger. "Now they come to *us*. Once a year. On *your* terms."
> "The terms are still being written."
> "Then write them boldly." She pulls the household book toward her — the quartermaster cannot plan a campaign without the book — and opens a fresh page. "The house party in summer, when the Park is at its greenest. The ball at the full moon, when the drive lights itself." She writes swiftly. "The guests convened, not invited. There is a difference, darling, and the difference is power."
> "And the cost?"
> "Harrow will do the figures." Letitia does not look up. "Harrow *loves* figures. It is his entire personality."
> "The dragon," Letitia says, tapping the charter's list, "is first, darling. Before the ton, before the many." The hawk's eyes go grave. "The guest-list war ended in the spring, but wars have aftermaths. Convene her first, by your own hand, and the aftermath becomes the peace."
> "By hand," Rose says. "This afternoon."
> "This afternoon." Letitia writes it in the book. "The dragon, convened first. The ton, convened after." She looks up. "It is strategy, darling, but it is also courtesy. The two are not enemies, whatever the old may tell you."
> *(They laugh together, and the charter gains its first ally. Letitia reaches for the Gazette at last, unfolds it one-handed, and reads the first leader with the air of a woman rewarding herself after a campaign well begun.)*
> "Darling." The hawk's eyes do not lift from the page. "Bell has opinions about the new opera house. Bell is *wrong* about the new opera house." She turns a page. "The founding, darling — the founding is *right*."
> *(Outside the window the Park goes about its morning, unaware that the year's campaign has just been planned over chocolate and the quartermaster's marginalia.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Dowager, on the convening — Augusta, the charter's; the line, the annual's. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta's morning room at ten, and the Dowager receiving the charter the way she receives everything: seated, spectacled, seventy-two years fully deployed, with the air of a judge who has already written the verdict and is merely waiting for the evidence to catch up.)*
> "The Assembly." Augusta reads the pages slowly, the spectacles low on her nose. "Annual." She turns a page. "A house party and ball." Another page. "Convened —" a pause — "by you, child. On your terms." She sets the charter down. The rarest smile.
> "And the line's verdict, Grandmama?"
> "The line —" the voice does something extraordinary, going soft at the edges — "the line *convenes*, child." Augusta removes the spectacles — twice a year, perhaps — and looks at Rose with unguarded eyes. "Do you know what your grandfather would have said to this? *Break the entail*, he said, *to save the house*. He broke it. Your father let it rot, to punish it." She replaces the spectacles. "And you, child —" the dry verdict — "you have *finished* it. And now you convene the ton to *witness* it. Annually."
> "The dragon," Rose says. "She must be first."
> "The dragon —" Augusta's mouth does something nearly warm — "the dragon will come, child. To be convened." She takes Rose's hand — the old hand, the rings, the weight. "The ton, child, will come. They will come because it is *annual*, and because it is *yours*, and because —" the driest pause — "because no one in London will dare to be the *one* who was not convened."
> "The seal." Augusta holds out her hand, and Rose gives her the signet — the Hartwell oak, the grandmother's. The Dowager turns it in the light. "Your grandfather broke the entail with *this* hand." She closes her fingers around the seal. "Not the seal. The *hand*." She returns it. "Use it, child. Sparingly." The driest pause. "Except for *this*. For this —" the rarest smile — "use it *annually*."
> "Grandmama." Rose hesitates. "The terms. Are they —" she searches — "are they *bold* enough?"
> "The terms —" Augusta considers the pages — "the terms are *plain*, child. Boldness is for *battles*. Plainness is for *institutions*." She rises, the audience concluded. "The line convenes. The charter *holds*. Write it fair, child, and seal it *red*."
> *(Rose holds the old hand, and the Dowager's receiving stands — the line's, the spectacles', the annual's — and the charter, which had a quartermaster at nine, has a dynasty by ten.)*

scenes.synopsis: the steward, the charter's practicalities — Harrow, the annual's costs. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The estate office at eleven, and Harrow with his books open — the steward's reckoning. He lays the convening's costs out the way he lays out everything: in columns, in order, without ornament. The house party: the beds, the boards, the servants' extra wages. The ball: the candles, the musicians, the supper. The annual: the whole of it, multiplied by forever.)*
> "The annual, Miss Hartwell." He turns a page with the care of a man handling scripture. "The house party. The ball. The convening." The dry smile. "I have done the figures three ways —" he taps the columns — "the modest, the proper, and the *Lavinia*."
> "And the verdict?"
> "The Park can bear it, miss." He looks up, the historian's eyes meeting hers. "Annually." He closes the book with a soft, definitive sound. "The charter is sound, miss."
> "Even the *Lavinia* way?"
> "Even the Lavinia way, miss." A beat. "Though I have taken the liberty of costing the *proper* way, and leaving the Lavinia way as a *supplement*." The dry smile deepens. "For occasions of particular brilliance."
> *(Rose looks at the columns and does her own arithmetic: once for the sum, once for the nerve. The candles alone run to a figure that would have stopped her heart in the first season. She does not flinch. She has learned what things cost and what they are worth, and the two ledgers are not the same.)*
> "The charter is sound," she says. "Write it so, Mr. Harrow. In the book. *Sound*."
> "The musicians." Harrow turns to a marked page. "The full number, miss. The proper way." The dryest. "The Lavinia way is the full number —" he consults the column — "with *trumpets*."
> "Trumpets," Rose says faintly.
> "Trumpets, miss." He closes the book on the supplement. "Costed, miss. As a supplement. For occasions of particular brilliance." He looks at her over the pages. "The founding, miss, may qualify."
> "The founding will begin with the *proper* way. No trumpets." She pauses. "The *first* year."
> "The first year, miss." Harrow writes it down — the historian's hand, the pensioner's satisfaction. "The trumpets wait, miss. Annually."
> *(She leaves him to his columns, and the office door shuts on the soft sound of his pencil resuming — the man already costing next year's candles, the founding's first honest debt, entered before the ink of the charter is dry.)*

scenes.synopsis: the terms — the Assembly's terms; convened, not joined. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at noon, and the terms — written fair. Rose copies the charter's spine onto a clean page, the three terms that will govern every year of the convening, and reads each one aloud as she writes it, testing the weight the way Quill tests a clause.)*
> *(The first term: the Assembly is annual — the house party in summer, the ball at the full moon — fixed, returning, forever. Not a Season's whim. An institution. She writes it, and the word* annual *sits on the page like a cornerstone.)*
> *(The second term: the Assembly is convened — by the mistress of Hartwell Park, on her terms. Not joined, not attended. Convened. The ton has spent a century inviting itself to itself. The Assembly turns the invitation around: they come to *her*, or they do not come at all.)*
> *(The third term: the guests are the convened — the family, the lovers, the ton, the dragon — named by the convener, welcomed by the house. No one convenes himself. No one arrives unlooked-for. The house party belongs to the Park; the ball belongs to the night; the terms belong to her.)*
> *(She reads the three together, and they hold. Letitia was right about the masterstroke. The terms do not merely organize a party. They declare a power: the power to convene. For ten seasons she has earned the house. The terms earn the future.)*
> *(Letitia comes in at two with the luncheon tray and reads the three terms over Rose's shoulder.)*
> "Darling." The hawk's eyes move down the page. "The *terms*." She reads the first again. "Annual." The second. "Convened." The third. "The convened." She straightens. "It is —" the warm look — "it is *Quill*, darling. Plain as a *brief*."
> "Quill," Rose says, "would charge for the plainness."
> "Quill —" Letitia laughs — "Quill would charge for the *ink*, darling." She taps the page. "But the terms are *yours*. Not joining the ton. Convening it." She writes in the margin, in the quartermaster's hand: *Three terms. Annual, convened, the convened. The charter's spine.* "Most foundings are jelly, darling. This one has bones."
> *(She sands the page dry and sits back, and the library holds the noon the way it holds everything: patiently. The terms are written, and they will bear the weight of every year to come — the house party, the ball, and the woman who convenes them.)*

scenes.synopsis: the date — the annual's; the choosing, the fixed. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at one, and the date — to be chosen and fixed. Rose turns the household book to the year's calendar, and the months lie before her like guests waiting to be convened.)*
> *(June: the roses, the longest days, the Park at its greenest — but June belongs to the Season's height, and the Assembly is not the Season's. It stands beside the Season, above it. July: the heat, the ton fled to the country — the wrong country, other people's houses. August: the grouse, the men distracted, the young restless.)*
> *(She considers the moon, the way Letitia taught her to consider everything: as a guest. The full moon lights the drive for nothing. It has attended every great night of the ten seasons, uninvited and indispensable. The ball wants the full moon. The charter wants the fixed.)*
> *(Letitia comes in with the luncheon tray and reads the deliberation off Rose's face.)*
> "Darling." She sets the tray down. "You are choosing a *date* as if it were a *husband*. It will repeat, darling. It need only be right once."
> "That is exactly why it must be right." Rose taps the calendar. "The full moon. Late summer. After the Season's thin end, before the autumn's shooting." She looks up. "The young will be restless. The Park will be golden. The drive will light itself."
> "Late summer." Letitia writes it in the book. "The full moon." The hawk's eyes gleam. "Darling, the moon is a guest too, and she will want the good candles — annually." She caps her pen. "Do you know what the ton will say? They will say the Hartwell Assembly is *fixed* — the way the almanac is fixed."
> "The almanac," Rose says, "does not convene."
> "The almanac —" Letitia rises, pausing at the door — "does not *dare*, darling." The warm look. "Late summer. The full moon. Yearly." She touches the doorframe. "The date is chosen, darling, and it will not move. The Assembly has its *when*."
> *(Rose writes it into the charter's margin —* late summer, the full moon, yearly *— and underlines it once. Through the window the Park lies in its afternoon order, and somewhere above the oaks the moon is already rising toward a date it does not yet know it has been given.)*

scenes.synopsis: the guests — the first list; the convened, the named. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at two, and the guests — the first list, to be convened and named. Rose takes a clean page and writes the headings the way Quill writes a brief: in order, without sentiment, the sentiment to be supplied by the event itself.)*
> *(The family: Augusta — the Dowager, the line, seventy-two and indispensable. Letitia — the quartermaster, the aunt, the household book's keeper. The family's convening is not a courtesy. It is the foundation. The Assembly stands on the family the way the Park stands on its stone.)*
> *(The lovers: Julian — the free man, the mended gloves in his pocket. Laurent — the Englishman, the unmasked, the direct. The heart's convening is not a decoration. It is the proof: that the convener is loved, and loves, and convenes from the center of a life, not the edge of one.)*
> *(The ton: the great houses — the Almerias, the Craykes, the Micklethwaites — the young, in their dozens, orbiting. The many are the point: the Assembly convenes the ton because the ton is the audience, the witness, the reason the charter was written at all.)*
> *(The dragon: Lady Agatha Drummond. First. Before the ton, before the many — the dragon is convened *first*, by hand, by the convener herself. The guest-list war ended in the spring; the charter seals the peace in ink. She writes the name last and underlines it once.)*
> *(She reads the dragon's name once more — underlined once, the way foundings underline — and thinks of the spring: the private word, on her terms; the guest list, surrendered; the war, ended.)*
> *(Honoria's name is not on the list — the daughter comes with the dragon, the way the tide comes with the moon — but Rose writes it in the margin anyway, in the small hand:* Honoria — convened as herself. *The margin holds what the list cannot: that the convening is personal, even when it is institutional.)*
> *(The page is full. The list is exact. Every name on it is a load-bearing wall, and the dragon's — underlined once — is the cornerstone. Rose sands the page, and the Assembly has its company.)*

scenes.synopsis: the dragon, the first guest — Drummond, the convened; the peace, the annual's. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room at three, and Drummond — the dragon, the first guest, received alone. Rose has kept this hour empty the way she keeps the good candles for the full moon: deliberately. The invitation lies on the table between them, sealed, the wax still soft.)*
> *(Lady Agatha Drummond takes it with the exact hands — the hands that once held the guest list like a weapon, in the spring, before the private word on Rose's terms ended the war. She breaks the seal slowly. She reads. The room is very quiet.)*
> "Lady Drummond." Rose holds the exact courtesy, the charter's own. "The Hartwell Assembly —" she nods at the invitation — "annual. A house party and ball." She looks at the dragon — the equal, the reconciled. "Convened by me. On my terms." A breath. "The peace. Annually."
> *(Drummond reads the invitation twice — the first time for the terms, the second time for the woman — and when she looks up, the honest look is there, the one from the spring.)*
> "The Assembly." Drummond sets the invitation down with care. "Convened." The honest look, held. "Miss Hartwell —" the rarest — "Rose." A pause. "The peace, annually." She takes Rose's hand. "I accept." The smallest smile, the dragon's, the true one's. "The dragon is convened."
> *(They sit a moment in the quiet — the convener and the convened, the war ended, the peace chartered — and Rose understands what the first guest means: the Assembly is not a defiance. It is a settlement. The dragon, convened first, makes the convening unassailable.)*
> *(Drummond rises, the invitation in her hand, and at the door she turns — the dragon's own pause, the one that once preceded terms and conditions.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." The exact voice, the honest look. "The *private word*, in the spring, was on your terms, Rose. This —" she holds up the invitation — "this is on your terms, *annually*." The smallest smile. "The dragon is *convened*."
> "Annually, Rose." The dragon's bow — the exact, the true. "I shall *come*."
> *(She goes, and the morning room holds its quiet, and Rose sits a moment with the empty table — the seal, the wax, the gone. The founding's hardest convening, accomplished before the ink is dry.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE CHARTER'S FIRST ARTICLE (the Assembly's founding principle: the house, the convening, or the annual). The morning deepens; decide the principle. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at dusk, and the charter asking its first article. Rose stands at the window with the draft pages in her hand, and the morning deepens around the question — no, the *afternoon* deepens; the founding has taken all day, and the light is going.)*
> *(The house: the Park's, the stone's. The first article could name the house — Hartwell Park, the stone, the whole, the finished. The principle would be the stone's. But stones are still, and the Assembly — she pictures them arriving, the young laughing, the dragon exact — the Assembly is the *gathering*. A house cannot gather. Only people gather.)*
> *(The convening: the ton's, the gathered. The first article could name the convening — the ton, gathered, on her terms. The principle would be the gathered's. But gatherings are people, and the Assembly — she pictures the charter's pages, the seal, the date fixed — the Assembly is the *annual*. People scatter. The charter returns.)*
> *(The annual: the year's, the returning. The first article could name the annual — the year, the returning, forever. The principle would be the returning's. But returnings are future, and the Assembly — she touches the draft pages, the ink still fresh — the Assembly is the *now*: this charter, this seal, this founding.)*
> *(Letitia comes in with the evening post and reads the indecision off Rose's face.)*
> "Darling." The hawk's eyes, amused. "The *first article*, darling. The charter's *spine*." She sets down the post. "The house is the *where*. The convening is the *what*. The annual is the *when*." She taps the draft. "A first article, darling, is the *why*."
> "The why," Rose says slowly, "is —" she looks at the pages — "that the ton is *convened*, by the *house*, *annually*." She picks up the pen. "The house, the convening, the annual." The pen hovers. "All three are true. But a first article —" she looks at Letitia — "a first article names *one*."
> "One, darling." The hawk's eyes, warm. "The founding's spine. Choose it boldly."
> *(The pen waits over the page — the house, the convening, the annual, all three true, only one the first article's. Outside, the Park darkens into its evening order, and inside the library the founding waits on its *why* — and the pen is in her hand, and the book lies open to receive it.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The charter's first article:*
- **The house** — *the Park, first.* The first article names the house — Hartwell Park, the stone, the whole. (Consequence: the principle is the stone's — but stones are still, and the Assembly is the gathering.)
- **The convening** — *the ton, gathered.* The first article names the convening — the ton, gathered, on her terms. (Consequence: the principle is the gathered's — but gatherings are people, and the Assembly is the annual.)
- **The annual** — *the year, returning.* The first article names the annual — the year, the returning, forever. (Consequence: the principle is the returning's — but returnings are future, and the Assembly is the now.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: house, convening, or annual. The charter's first article is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the writing — the charter, written; the founding, the inked. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at four, and the writing — the charter, written fair. Rose takes the drafts — the morning's pages, Letitia's annotations, Augusta's verdict, Harrow's figures — and copies the whole into the household book in her ledger-hand: the fair copy, the permanent one.)*
> *(The pen moves steadily: the heading, the terms, the date, the first list. The ink is the good ink, the paper the Park's, the hand — Quill once called it the only honest thing in Chancery — exact. She writes the way the house was built: one deliberate thing at a time, until suddenly it is all at once.)*
> *(Letitia comes in midway and watches over her shoulder, the quartermaster's inspection.)*
> "Darling." The hawk's eyes on the page. "The fair copy." She reads a line. "The *terms*." Another line. "The *date*." She straightens. "It is —" the warm look — "it is *beautiful*, darling. Not the hand —" a laugh — "though the hand is *adequate* — the *thing*. The charter."
> "The first article," Rose says, not looking up, "is as I chose. The house, the convening, the annual — whichever the morning decided." She writes on.
> "The morning," Letitia says, "decided *all three*, darling. That is what foundings do. They *include*." She watches the pen. "Write it fair. The household book has waited ten seasons for a page like this."
> *(The pen falters once — on the date, late summer, the full moon — and Rose stops, the nib hovering.)*
> "Darling." Letitia, watching. "The *date*. It is only the annual's."
> "It is the *when*." Rose writes it — late summer, the full moon, yearly — and the nib moves on. "It must be exact."
> "Exact." Letitia reads the line. "The moon is a guest too, darling, and she will want the good candles." The hawk's eyes, warm. She touches the margin. "Write it fair, darling. The household book has waited ten seasons for a page like this — and the *margin* has waited for the quartermaster's hand." She writes, in the small decisive script: *Fair copy, the founding's. Witnessed by the quartermaster.*
> *(The writing goes on into the evening — the pen steady, the pages filling — and the household book fills the way the Park filled: completely, and as a promise kept. When the last line is sanded dry, Rose sits back, and the book lies open, and the Assembly exists as ink on paper.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sealing — the charter, sealed; the founding, the permanent. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at dusk, and the sealing. Rose heats the wax with the steady hand of ten seasons' practice, and the stick softens, and the first drop falls — red, the Park's own — onto the charter's final page.)*
> *(The seal is the Hartwell oak — the signet, the grandmother's, the one Augusta pressed into her hand in the spring with the words* use it sparingly, child *— and she presses it now, firmly, into the wax. The oak rises in red. She holds the seal a moment longer than necessary, feeling the metal warm through the handle.)*
> *(She thinks of all the seals of the ten seasons — the Network's paper, the entail's true history, Quill's final enrollment — and of this one, different from all of them: a *beginning*. The first seal she has ever pressed for joy.)*
> *(Letitia, summoned to witness, stands at the desk with the air of a godmother at a christening.)*
> "Darling." The hawk's eyes on the wax. "The seal." She touches the cooled edge with one finger. "The oak." The warm look. "Do you know what you have done? You have *pressed* the future, darling. Like a flower." A laugh. "A *very* expensive flower, annually."
> "The founding," Rose says, "is sealed."
> *(The wax cools, and the oak stands in red. Rose looks at the seal a long moment, the signet warm in her hand.)*
> "The *first* seal." Letitia, very quietly. "For joy."
> "The first." Rose sets the signet down. "The others were —" she searches — "defenses. Settlements." She touches the cooled wax. "This one is a *beginning*."
> "Beginnings —" Letitia closes the household book on the sealed page, with the particular tenderness she reserves for finished things — "beginnings are the quartermaster's favorite maneuver, darling. They require everything." The warm look. "And they *return* everything." She ties the book's ribbon. "The wax —" she says it the way other women say *amen* — "is pressed."
> *(The ribbon tied, the book closed, the room holds its dusk. Rose carries the sealed charter to the strongbox herself — no footman, no ceremony — and turns the key twice, the way the house has always turned its keys: once for the lock, once for the keeping.)*

scenes.synopsis: the announcing — London, informed; the convening, the declared. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library the next morning, and the announcing. Rose sits with the fair copies — the charter's public face, the letters of announcement — and the pen moves again, but differently now: the convener's hand, the one that declares.)*
> *(The letters go first to the family — Augusta, Letitia, already convened in person — then to the lovers, then to the ton's great houses, then to the young. Each letter is the same and each is different: the same charter, the same terms, the same date — and each addressed by hand, each sealed with the oak, each personal. The convening is not a proclamation. It is a correspondence.)*
> *(The footmen carry the packets to the post — the London post, the country post, the expresses for the great houses — and Rose stands at the library window and watches the first packet go down the drive. London will be informed by Thursday.)*
> *(She returns to the desk and writes the last of the letters — the Gazette's. Not an invitation; the Gazette is never invited, it *attends*. A notice: the Hartwell Assembly, chartered, annual, convened. She addresses it to Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, in her fairest hand, and seals it with the oak.)*
> "The charter," she says aloud, to the empty library, "is public."
> *(The Gazette's letter gives her pause. She drafts it three times. The first is too grand. The second is too plain. The third —)*
> "The Gazette," she reads aloud, testing it, "is *informed* of the Hartwell Assembly's chartering. The Gazette will *attend*, annually." She looks at the draft. "Bell will read the informing and hear the convening underneath."
> *(Letitia, at the door with the luncheon tray, laughs.)*
> "Darling, Bell hears the convening underneath *everything*. It is her entire *profession*." She sets down the tray. "Seal it, darling. The oak. The proprietor —" the hawk's eyes gleam — "respects a *seal*."
> *(The letter goes with the rest, and the charter's public face travels toward the Gazette the way the convening travels toward the ton: declared, and certain. The library settles into its noon, and the shelves hold their ordered paper memory, and the thing is done.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ton, the news — the convening, received; London, the answering. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday, and the ton answers. The replies begin with the midday post, and they come the way weather comes: first one, then three, then a packet, then a flood.)*
> *(Rose reads them at the library desk in the order Letitia decrees — the great houses first, the young second, the curious last — and the convening is received the way the charter intended: as a fact to be answered. The Almerias accept. The Craykes accept. The Micklethwaites accept *and* ask about the shooting, which Letitia says is the truest acceptance of all, because a family that asks about the shooting has already decided to stay the week.)*
> "Darling." Letitia tallies on a spare page, the quartermaster's hand swift. "Forty-one acceptances. Three regrets —" she squints — "all *lying*, all from people who will come next year when they see the *notices*. And one —" she holds up a letter — "one *demand* to be convened, from a dowager I have never liked. I am *framing* that one."
> "The convening," Rose says, "is welcomed."
> "The convening," Letitia corrects, capping her pen, "is *assumed*, darling. There is a difference. They are not deciding whether to come. They are deciding what to *wear*." The hawk's eyes gleam. "That, darling, is the masterstroke's proof."
> *(The dowager's demand arrives with the evening post — three pages, magnificent, furious — and Letitia reads it aloud in the library with the delight of a general reading the enemy's surrender.)*
> "'*Demands* to be convened.'" The hawk's eyes shine. "Darling, she *demands* it. In *writing*." She folds the letter with care. "It goes on the morning-room wall, next to the *triumphs*."
> *(The replies keep coming through the afternoon — the post bag empties and fills and empties again — and by evening the household book's new pages hold the first year's company. London did not deliberate. London answered. The charter has passed its first test.)*
> *(Rose writes the fifty-ninth name into the book herself, in the ledger-hand, and sands it dry. Outside, the Park darkens into its evening order, unaware that the ton has just agreed — forty-one times over, and once by demand — to come and be convened.)*

scenes.synopsis: Bell, the charter's — the Gazette, the founding's; the reporting, the dry. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room at four, and Mrs. Nance Bell — the Gazette's proprietor, come down from London by invitation, the charter's pages waiting on the table between them. She reads the way she does everything: completely, and without hurry. The soft voice does not rise. The sharp eyes do not miss.)*
> "Miss Hartwell." Bell sets the last page down. "The Assembly —" the dryest pause — "annual. Convened." She looks at Rose over the pages. "The Gazette —" another pause — "the Gazette *reports*, Miss Hartwell. It does not convene things. It *witnesses* them."
> "The Gazette," Rose says, "is welcome to witness. Annually."
> "Annually." Bell turns a page back, rereads a term. "The first article." The dry voice, considering. "The house, the convening, the annual — whichever you chose, Miss Hartwell." A nod, the proprietor's own. "The *terms*." She stops, and the bluntness does something rare: it hesitates. "They are *sound*, Miss Hartwell. I have read a great many foundings. Most of them are aspirations with seals. This one is a *charter*."
> "The convening," Rose says, "is the story."
> "The convening —" Bell rises, the interview concluded in the proprietor's exact way — "is the *story*, Miss Hartwell." The sharp eyes, warm, once. "The Gazette will attend. Annually." At the door: "And Miss Hartwell —" the dryest — "convene the *dragon* first, always. It makes the best *copy*."
> *(She goes — the proprietor's exact departure, no wasted motion — and Rose sits with the charter's pages, and the dry voice stays in the room the way good ink stays on paper. Through the window she can see Bell's carriage waiting at the steps, the coachman holding the greys, the whole of London's judgment idling in the drive.)*
> *(Rose writes in the household book's margin, in the small hand:* Bell read the charter. Found it sound. The Gazette will attend. *The founding has its witness, and the witness is the one person in London who cannot be flattered into attendance — which is what makes her attendance worth having.)*
> *(Through the window she watches Bell's carriage go down the drive, the proprietor upright in the corner, the notebook already open. By tomorrow the Gazette will have its notice. By Thursday, London will have its verdict.)*

scenes.synopsis: the founding's thesis — dress the convener; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief — The Assembly's founding:** "The charter is written today. The annual house party and ball, convened by you, on your terms. Dress for the convener — the woman who convenes. **Editorial criterion: convening.**"
>
> **A. The Convening** — dove grey, the Park's stone; the convener, the gathering. Motif: the gathered knot, at the waist — the convening, embroidered. Thread: **silver** (the exact, edged) / **dove silk** (the stone, matched) / **pearl** (the convening, lit). Colorway: dove grey + silver + pearl. Accessories: a silver ribbon; the grandmother's pearls, at rest; grey kid gloves.
> **B. The Annual** — deep blue, the year's; the returning, the fixed. Motif: the circling year, stitched at the hem — the annual, embroidered. Thread: **silver** (the fixed, edged) / **blue silk** (the year, matched) / **cream** (the honest, lit). Colorway: deep blue + silver + cream. Accessories: a silver brooch; pearl drop earrings; blue kid gloves.
> **C. The Terms** — ivory, the charter's; the woman, the terms'. Motif: the sealed line, architectural — the terms, embroidered. Thread: **gold** (the landed, stated) / **ivory silk** (the charter, matched) / **pearl** (the termed, lit). Colorway: ivory + gold + pearl. Accessories: a gold chain; ivory kid gloves.
>

The mirror, to be faced as the convener. **Direction.** The charter is written — dress for the convener. **Editorial criterion.** Convening — every choice must answer the gathering, not the joining.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the founding. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*

> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** the founder's — the written, the sealed, giving nothing to the doubt. *5 coins.*
> *(The pins accumulate — the gown's line set, the founder's sleeves — and the dressing room holds its morning the way the charter holds its terms: exactly.)*

> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, composed:** the convener's — the gathered, the kept; the ornament's none. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Ribbon, throat's:** the direction's punctuation — silver, silver, or gold — the convening, tied. *5 coins.*

> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, immaculate:** the woman's gauntlets — expected, and without a mark. *5 coins.*

> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Shawl, light:** the morning's — the founding's air, the convener's wrap. *5 coins.*
> *(Founding's slippers, the light shawl — the convening asks for the composed, and she gives it.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, seals:** the charter's — the wax's, the small; the woman's, not the clerk's. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** the founding's — the Park smells of morning; the lady adds nothing. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** the convening's — the gathering, the stood; the spine's. *5 coins.*

Rose stands at the library window and watches the packets go: the London post first, heavy with the ton's great houses; the country post after, for the neighbors; the expresses last, for the dragon's circle — though the dragon herself was convened by hand, first of all.)*
> *(The footmen carry them down the drive in the post bag, and the bag goes to the village, and the village post goes to London, and London — by Thursday — will know. The last footman turns at the gate and waves, and Rose — alone at the window, the convener — waves back, which is not in any protocol and is entirely in hers.)*
> *(She thinks of all the posts of the ten seasons — the Network's paper, the entail's true history, Lavinia's galloping letters — and of this one, different: a *convening*. The first post she has ever sent for joy.)*
> *(Letitia joins her at the window, the household book under her arm.)*
> "Gone, darling." The hawk's eyes on the drive. "Dispatched." She opens the book, writes in the margin: *The invitations, sent. Four o'clock.* "The quartermaster has *dispatched*, darling."
> "And now?"
> "And now —" Letitia closes the book — "now we *wait*, darling. The founding's hardest maneuver." The grave look. "Thursday. The replies."
> *(The village post goes at half past — the bag, the packets, the invitations traveling. Rose watches from the library window until the cart is out of sight.)*
> "Thursday." Letitia, at the window beside her. "The replies." The hawk's eyes on the empty drive. "The founding's hardest maneuver, darling —" the warm look — "the *waiting*."
> "The waiting," Rose says, "is the *charter's*." She searches. "The convening is *done*. The answering is the ton's."
> "The ton's." Letitia closes the book. "And the ton, darling —" the quartermaster's certainty — "the ton *answers*. They always do."
> *(The drive holds its emptiness, and the house holds its breath, and the invitations travel toward the ton like seeds toward soil. Rose stays at the window a while after Letitia has gone, watching the road the cart took, as if will alone could hurry Thursday.)*

scenes.synopsis: the replies — the ton, answering; the convened, the accepted. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday, and the replies. They come with the midday post in a packet thick as a book, and Rose and Letitia open them together in the library, the way generals open dispatches: swiftly, and without ceremony.)*
> *(The great houses first: the Almerias accept. The Craykes accept. The Micklethwaites accept and ask about the shooting. The young second — acceptances in hands still learning confidence, in their dozens, one of them enclosing a drawing of the ballroom with the chandeliers as small exploding suns. The curious last: the dowager who demanded to be convened accepts *magnificently*, in three pages.)*
> "Darling." Letitia tallies, the quartermaster's hand flying down the list. She looks up, the hawk's eyes bright. "Complete, darling. *Complete*." She sets down the pen. "And the dragon —" the warm look — "was convened by *hand*, and answered by *hand*. The set is *complete*."
> "The convened," Rose says, very quietly, "are coming."
> "The convened —" Letitia gathers the letters — "are *coming*, darling." She ties the packet with ribbon, the way she ties everything that matters. "The replies, the accepted. The post —" the quartermaster's satisfaction, complete — "the *returned*."
> *(The drawing — the ballroom, the chandeliers as small exploding suns — goes into the household book's margin, pressed flat. Letitia insists, and the paste brush comes out, and the girl's suns dry into the page like small promises.)*
> "Darling." The hawk's eyes on the drawing. "The *mythology*, darling. The Park should own its own *mythology*." She presses it flat with her palm. "The convened are *coming*, darling. With *drawings*."
> "The dowager's three pages." Rose holds them up. "Magnificent. Furious."
> "Magnificent —" Letitia takes them — "and *framed*, darling. The morning-room wall. Next to the *triumphs*." She ties the packet with ribbon. "And the bell-laugh girl's single line —" she reads it aloud twice, helpless with laughter — "the truest letter of the post."
> *(Rose sets three letters aside to answer herself — the drawing girl, the dowager, the bell-laugh girl — and the rest go into the household book's new pages, the ton's own hand. The founding has passed its second test: not only did London answer, London is *coming*.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Park, the charter's — the whole, the convened; the light. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The Park at dusk, and the charter's own ground holding its light the way the charter holds its terms: completely. Rose walks the evening circuit — the terrace, the lake pavilion, the walled garden — and the Park does what it has done since the first chapter: it behaves.)*
> *(At the terrace, the orange trees stand in their tubs, waiting for the ball's night and the lanterns. At the lake pavilion, the water holds the sky's last color. At the walled garden, the gardener — working late — touches his hat and shows her, without being asked, the buds: the Hartwell rose, still tight, still certain. "For the Assembly, miss," he says. "Yearly.")*
> *(She walks the drive's length, and the drive is empty, and the empty is full — full of the carriages that will come, the convened. She pictures them: the dust, the wheels, the young arriving laughing, the dragon arriving exact. A carriage passes on the high road beyond the gates — someone else's errand, someone else's evening — and the sound of the wheels fades into the dusk like a rehearsal.)*
> *(At the gallery window she stops, as she always stops, and looks at the whole — the Park, the charter's — and does the arithmetic: once for the sum, once for the nerve. The sum is the company, one charter, one Park. The nerve is steady. The drive will fill the way the ballroom filled: completely, and without effort.)*
> *(At the lake pavilion she stops — the water holding the sky's last color — and thinks of the charter's pages: the heading, the terms, the date, the list, the seal. Every zone the ten seasons restored, holding the convening: the terrace, the pavilion, the garden, the drive. A moorhen crosses the water, leaving its exact line, and is gone.)*
> *(The light does what light does in a finished house: it stays. The Park holds its dusk, and the founding's ground waits for the full moon, patient as the charter's ink.)*

scenes.synopsis: the bloom — the annual's flower, imagined; the legacy, the yearly. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The walled garden at dawn, and the bloom — imagined. Rose walks the Hartwell rows before the household is up, and the buds stand in their restored order, green and tight and absolutely certain of themselves.)*
> *(She bends to the row's end — the bud she has watched since the first chapter, the legacy literal and living — and the gardener's verdict comes back to her, word for word: another week, perhaps two. It will open when it is ready, and not a day before. Roses are like the ton, he said. They bloom on their own terms.)*
> *(She imagines it — the Hartwell rose opening for the Assembly's first house party, the charter's flower, yearly. The guests will walk through flowers the Park grew itself. The ton will know it. The rose will not hurry for them. That is the whole of the lesson, and it is enough. She straightens, and her knees are damp from the grass, and she does not mind.)*
> *(A bee works the neighboring row, early and industrious. The dew holds the light. The garden smells of green and patience, and Rose stands among the buds and understands what the charter's flower means: that some foundings are *ink*, and some are *roots*, and the Assembly — convened annually, returning yearly — will be both.)*
> *(She thinks of the charter — the terms, the seal, the company — and of the rose: the ink and the roots. The charter convenes. The rose *returns*. Yearly.)*
> *(The gardener's boy comes down the row with the watering cans, and the water falls silver in the dawn light, and the buds stand green and tight under it, absolutely certain of themselves. Rose watches him work the length of the row, and the day begins, and the garden smells of green and patience and wet earth.)*
> *(A second bee joins the first, and the rows hum — early, industrious, certain. The dew holds the light. The garden smells of green and patience. The bloom imagined this dawn will be witnessed at the full moon, and every year after, the way the charter returns: annually, and on its own terms. Rose turns for the house, and the rows hum behind her, and the day begins.)*

scenes.synopsis: the portrait — the Assembly's wall; the hung, the convened. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The west gallery at noon, and the portrait's wall. Rose stands before the empty frame at the gallery's end — the frame that held Harrow's plan, the Park drawn whole — and sees, instead of the plan, the future: Octavia's picnic portrait, the laugh nearly finished, hung here, on the Assembly's wall.)*
> *(She pictures it: the portrait hung where the plan hung, the laugh caught mid-joy, the Park behind her. The guests will pass it on their way to the ballroom, and they will see the convener as the painter sees her: laughing, from the picnic, with the light doing what it did.)*
> *(Octavia finds her there, brushes in hand, and reads the thought off her face the way she reads everything: at a glance. A dab of rose-madder stands on her cuff, bright as a small wound.)*
> "The wall." The precise voice, quiet. "You are choosing the *wall*, Rose."
> "The Assembly's wall," Rose says. "For the laugh. When it is finished."
> "When it is finished —" Octavia considers the empty frame, the precise eye measuring — "it hangs *here*, Rose. Not in London. Here." The precise smile. "Two houses, one shared life. The arrangement is convened, Rose. The portrait is my half of it. The *wall* is yours."
> "The wall." Octavia measures the empty frame — the precise eye, the north light's own. "Where the plan hung."
> "Where the Park was *drawn*," Rose says. "The whole."
> "Where the whole was *drawn*, Rose." The precise smile. "And now the whole is *laughed*." Octavia touches the frame. "The portrait is my half of it." The rare hesitation. "The *wall* —" she looks at Rose — "is *yours*. And the *laugh* —" the precise voice, warm — "is *everyone's*."
> *(The west gallery holds its noon, and the empty frame waits at the gallery's end. Rose looks at it a moment longer — the plan gone to the archive, the laugh not yet dry — and goes down to luncheon, leaving the wall to its future. Behind her, Octavia's brush has already resumed, quick and certain, laying in the laugh one stroke at a time.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ballroom — the annual's ball, imagined; the forty paces, the yearly. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The ballroom at dusk, empty, and the annual's ball — imagined. Rose walks the floor alone, counting the paces the way she counts everything: once for the sum, once for the nerve. Forty. The charter's dance, the coming.)*
> *(She imagines it — the chandeliers lit, the fiddles, the convened filling the forty paces. The quadrille first, then the waltz, then the country dances the young will demand when the night is old. The candles burning at exactly the rate Letitia will calculate. The ices — rose-shaped, annually — going out with the champagne. The dowager who demanded her invitation holding court by the terrace doors, magnificent and furious and entirely convened.)*
> *(The musicians' gallery stands empty above, the field marshal's stand waiting. She pictures the first violin tapping his bow, the tuning resolving, the waltz beginning — and the floor turning, the silks moving, the candlelight doing what candlelight does in this room: carrying.)*
> *(She stops at the center of the floor and turns slowly, taking the room in: the plaster, the glass, the waxed floor, the terrace doors standing open to the Park's dusk. The ballroom, the night. The awaited, the coming.)*
> *(In the imagined, the tuning resolves and the first violin sings alone, and the ballroom answers: the plaster, the glass, the waxed floor giving the note back warmer than it came. The floor turns. The silks move. The convened fill the forty paces.)*
> *(The terrace doors stand open to the Park's dusk, and the evening comes in like a guest: unhurried, expected, welcome. She stands at the center of the floor, and the imagined holds her completely — the charter's dance, the annual's ball, the coming.)*
> *(She walks the forty paces once more, heel to toe, the waxed floor giving back the small sound of her slippers, and goes out by the terrace doors into the Park's dusk, leaving the empty room to practice holding a full one. The doors swing to behind her, and the ballroom keeps its dusk, and forty paces of polished floor wait — patient, exact, expectant — for the tuning to resolve.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE FOUNDING'S MEANING (what the Assembly means: the convening, the house, or the future). The afternoon deepens; decide the meaning. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The gallery at dusk, and the founding asking its meaning. Rose walks the west gallery alone — the portraits in their evening order, Harrow's plan at the end — and the light goes the way it always goes here: slowly, and all at once at the end.)*
> *(The convening: the ton, gathered, on her terms. It would be the power to gather — held by the house, returning yearly. But gatherings are people, and people scatter. The meaning must outlast the guests.)*
> *(The house: Hartwell Park, the stone, the whole. It would be the finished thing — the ten seasons' work, witnessed annually. But the house is the where. The meaning is the *what for*.)*
> *(The future: the year, the returning, forever. It would be the promise — the charter outliving the charter's maker. But the future is not yet written, and the Assembly is the now: this charter, this seal, this founding.)*
> *(She stands before Harrow's plan a long time — the Park drawn whole, every zone inked in the historian's hand — and the meaning settles the way the dusk settles on the lawn. The mistress convenes. The house holds. The years return. A footman comes to light the gallery sconces and withdraws on silent feet, and the portraits take the candlelight the way they take everything: as their due.)*
> *(She takes out the household book — she carries it now, the way Letitia carries hers — and writes in the margin, under the seal's page: the meaning, as she chose. The convening, the house, the future. The pen moves. The meaning is hers.)*
> *(The gallery holds its evening. The portraits hang straight. The book goes back into the library, and the Season turns toward the convened: the Assembly, the annual, the coming. The Ravencrofts who built and the Hartwells who kept and broke and sold look down from their frames, and the woman below them writes the last of the founding's questions into the margin, in ink, and sands it dry.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: convening, house, or future. The founding's meaning is hers.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — The founding's meaning:*
- **The convening** — *the gathered, meant.* The Assembly means the convening — the ton, gathered, on her terms. (Consequence: the meaning is the gathered's — but gathereds are people, and the Assembly is the annual.)
- **The house** — *the stone, meant.* The Assembly means the house — Hartwell Park, the stone, the whole. (Consequence: the meaning is the stone's — but stones are still, and the Assembly is the gathering.)
- **The future** — *the returning, meant.* The Assembly means the future — the year, the returning, forever. (Consequence: the meaning is the returning's — but returnings are future, and the Assembly is the now.)

scenes.synopsis: the charter, the kept — the household book, the permanent; the forever. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at night, and the charter kept. Rose turns to the founding's pages — the heading, the terms, the date, the list, the seal pressed in red — and reads them the way she read Lavinia's letter at the last chapter's start: twice, once for the sense, once for the person.)*
> *(The Assembly exists — as ink, as wax, as acceptances tied with ribbon. She writes one line more, in her own hand, under the seal — not a term, not a date. A sentence, which the household book has never held before in all its ruled and ledgered years:)*
> *She does not join the ton. She convenes it. The books balance.*
> *(She closes the book. The founding's record goes into the Park's keeping, where stone and paper and memory do what they have always done: hold.)*
> *(The pages hold the founding entire: the heading, the terms, the date, the list — the family, the lovers, the ton, the dragon — the seal pressed in red, the acceptances tied with ribbon. The ink is dry. The wax is cool. She runs one finger along the page's edge, feeling the slight ridge where the fair copy begins, and the paper is smooth under her hand, and the charter is *kept*.)*
> *(She reads the sentence she wrote —* She does not join the ton. She convenes it. The books balance. *— and the nib's scratch comes back to her, and the quiet of the library, and the weight of the pen. The household book has never held a sentence before. It will hold this one — and, she suspects, very few others. Sentences are for foundings, and foundings are for ink.)*
> *(She closes the book — gently, the way one closes a door on a guest not yet arrived — and carries it to the strongbox herself, and turns the key twice. The strongbox lid shuts with the particular finality of well-made oak. Outside, the Park's lamps are lit one by one, and the house settles into its evening order, and the charter waits under a closed cover for the full moon.)*

scenes.synopsis: the letters — the founding, reported; London writes. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The library at noon, and the letters. They come by the midday post, the ton's own hand, and they are — without exception — the same letter: the Assembly is the Season's true event; the charter is magnificent; may they bring a cousin; will there be dancing; please.)*
> *(Rose reads them at the desk, one by one, and Letitia — uninvited, indispensable — reads over her shoulder.)*
> "London," she says, "has *opinions*." The hawk's eyes scan a dowager's three pages. "Darling, this one has *planned her gown*." She sets it down. "The founding, reported. The charter, the convening, the annual — all of it, in hands still learning that the ton can be *convened*."
> "Shall I answer them?" Rose asks. "All of them?"
> "You shall answer *three*." Letitia holds up three fingers — the quartermaster's arithmetic, deployed again. "The truest letters. The rest will hear of it." She rises, pausing at the door. "And darling —" the warm look — "the founding is *news*, and news is the Gazette's. But the *letters* —" she taps the packet — "the letters are *ours*." She is gone before Rose can answer, the tray balanced, the campaign's colors borne off to the morning room.
> *(The truest letters are the shortest — the bell-laugh girl's single line, the drawing girl's exploding suns, the dowager's magnificent fury. Rose answers them in the convener's hand: the charter's terms in miniature, the date, the full moon.)*
> *(Letitia files the rest — the letter file, under* Assembly, Hartwell, chartered *— and the packet grows: the founding, reported, remembered.)*
> "Darling." The hawk's eyes on the file. "The *paper memory*, darling. The Park's." She closes the drawer. "The founding is *news*, darling. But the *letters* —" she taps the drawer — "are *ours*. Annually."
> *(The drawer closes on the packet, and the library holds its noon, patient as ever, as a promise kept. Rose answers three — the drawing girl first, the dowager second, the bell-laugh girl third — and files the rest, and the pen moves in the convener's hand, and London writes, and the Park *keeps*, and the drawer holds them all.)*

scenes.synopsis: the ton, the year's — the annual, awaited; the convened, the coming. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning room at dusk, and the ton awaited. Rose stands at the window with the charter's list in her hand, and the Park lies beyond the glass, golden in the late light, waiting with her.)*
> *(She pictures the drive in late summer: the dust, the wheels, the carriages in their long line. The young arriving laughing. The great houses arriving exact. The dragon arriving —* she smiles — *first, as convened.)*
> *(The waiting has the particular quality of foundings: *full*. Full of the charter's ink, the seal's wax, the acceptances, the gardener's buds, the cook's theories, the quartermaster's columns.)*
> *(Letitia joins her at the window, the household book under her arm, and they stand together in the dusk.)*
> "Thursday is past, darling." The hawk's eyes on the drive. "The replies are *in*. The company is *set*." The warm look. "And now —" she breathes — "now we *prepare*, darling. The founding's next maneuver."
> "The annual," Rose says, "awaited."
> "The annual —" Letitia closes the book — "the *coming*, darling."
> *(The drive lies empty in the dusk — the gravel raked smooth, the oaks standing, the full moon still weeks away. But the empty is full: full of the carriages that will come. A groom leads a grey across the yard below, and the horse's hooves strike the gravel in the particular rhythm of evening stables, unhurried and exact.)*
> *(Letitia's hand finds Rose's on the windowsill — the aunt's, the quartermaster's — and they stand together in the dusk, watching the light go.)*
> "The preparing, darling." The hawk's eyes on the drive. "The founding's *next* maneuver." The warm look. "The house party. The ball." She squeezes Rose's hand. "The *annual*, darling. Awaited."
> "The annual —" Rose watches the dusk — "the *coming*."
> *(The dusk deepens over the Park, and the first stars come out above the oaks. Rose stands at the window long after Letitia has gone down to dinner, and the list stays in her hand, and the empty drive stays full of carriages, and the waiting holds its fullness a little longer — the particular fullness of foundings, which is the fullness of things about to happen.)*

scenes.synopsis: the woman, the founder's — Rose, the evening's; the mistress, the convener's. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Her bedroom at night, and the woman at the window in her petticoat, the Park beyond the glass dark and whole. Rose does the accounting she always does when the house is quiet: the columns, the sums, the nerve, the particular arithmetic of evenings that matter.)*
> *(The charter: written, sealed, announced, answered. The company: convened. The costs: accounted, bearable, annually. The meaning — as she chose — decided. The sums are large. The nerve is steady.)*
> *(But the ledger is not where she feels it. What she feels is an image she would never say aloud: Drummond at the morning-room table, breaking the seal slowly, saying* the dragon is convened *— and Honoria in the gallery, saying* not her soldier *— and the letters tied with ribbon — and the heading, alone on the blank page a week ago, now surrounded by ink.)*
> *(She lets the images stand, unentered, unaccounted. Some things the household book cannot hold. The convener's unaccounted wealth: a dragon's slow smile, a daughter's steady eyes, forty-one acceptances, one demand in three furious pages, and a heading that began the week alone on a blank page.)*
> *(She thinks of the first chapter's dawn — the west gallery, the inventory, the counting — and of this night's accounting: the charter written, the meaning decided, the Assembly chartered. The sums are large. The nerve is steady. The woman is *whole*.)*
> *(Below, the Park's lamps are lit one by one. The house settles into its evening order. The lamps burn below, steady in their rows, and the Park lies dark and whole beyond the glass, and the founder's own view holds steady as the flame.)*
> *(She sits at the window a while longer, watching the light go out of the sky and come on in the windows — the founder's own view, the convener's — and the quiet of the room is the quiet of a thing finished, and kept. Her maid comes to turn down the bed and withdraws without a word, and the petticoat lies where she left it, and the night is hers, and the house is hers, and the year is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the convening, the imagined — the annual, the future's; the forever. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Midnight, and the convening imagined. Rose walks the state rooms with a candle, the way she walked them in the last chapter's small hours: the ballroom dark, the dining room bare, the gallery's portraits in their dark order.)*
> *(She imagines it — the house party and ball, yearly, forever: the founding's dream. Late summer, the full moon, the drive lit for nothing. The company arriving. The young dancing. The dragon, convened, exact. The ices, rose-shaped. The garden, lit. The portrait's laugh, hung. The charter's rose, blooming.)*
> *(The dream has the particular solidity of things chartered: a *term*. The Assembly will convene. The ton will come. The Park will hold them. Yearly. Forever.)*
> *(She stops at the gallery window — the drive empty, the night entire — and the founding's dream stands around her like the house itself: built, and waiting to be lived in.)*
> *(Not a wish — a *term*. The Assembly will convene. The ton will come. The Park will hold them.)*
> *(The candle gutters. She shields it with her hand — the kept flame — and walks on through the sleeping house: the ballroom dark, the dining room bare, the small saloon quiet. Her slippers make no sound on the waxed floors, and the portraits keep their dark order, and the house keeps its own counsel until morning.)*
> *(The portraits hang in their dark order as she passes — the Ravencrofts, the Hartwells, the whole long argument of blood, at rest. The convening will wake them, annually. She nods to them as she goes, the way one nods to guests already seated, and the candle steadies in her hand.)*
> *(She walks home to bed through the sleeping house, the candle guttering, and the convening goes with her — the founding's dream, patient as the charter's ink, until the full moon. At her door she stops, and looks back down the dark corridor, and the house gives back nothing but its own held breath — and that, she thinks, is enough for one night.)*

scenes.synopsis: Bell's founding report — arch, precise; reward-only, never mystery. (Turns: 1 — the reading)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning Gazette, read over chocolate. Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, in her own dry voice:)*
> *"Yesterday Miss Hartwell chartered the Hartwell Assembly — an annual house party and ball, convened by her, on her terms — and the Gazette — having witnessed the convening's founding — finds it the Season's true event. She does not join the ton. She convenes it. The Gazette will attend, annually."*
> (T1 · stance) *Rose reads it twice — the amusement first (the convening! annually!), then the reckoning: the founding is pronounced true in print as well as in the charter's ink, and Bell has made the Assembly permanent, which is Bell's way of making it forever. She files the sting under its lesson: in London, the convening the Gazette attends annually is the convening that's real.* — remembered: *the lesson: the convening the Gazette attends annually is the convening that's real.*

scenes.synopsis: the first invitations, answered — the post, the returned; the Assembly, the coming. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, and the post returns — the first invitations, answered — and the Assembly is the coming.)*
> *(They come — the replies, the accepted — the family, the lovers, the ton, the dragon: the convened, the annual, the coming.)*
> "The Assembly." She reads them — the accepted, the coming. "Annual." She looks at the Park beyond — the whole, the convened. "Convened —" she stops — "by me. On my terms." She folds the replies — the accepted. "The ton —" she breathes — "the ton is convened."
> *(The chapter closes on the replies — the accepted, the coming — and the Season turns toward the convened: the Assembly, the annual — and the Season holds its breath.)*

scenes.synopsis: the arrivals — the first guests, the drive; the convened, the coming. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Morning, and the drive is holding its breath. Rose stands at the doors and listens to the stillness: the gravel raked clean, the oaks in their rows, the terrace urns filled with Hartwell-grown flowers, the lake pavilion catching the first light. Ten seasons of work, and the Park has put its face on for company.)*
> *(Mrs. Quick has been up since five. The footmen stand at their stations with the drilled alertness of men told once, in the immovable voice, exactly what the day requires. The boot boy — commended personally, and scarlet to the ears for a month — holds the doors. The household is ready. It has been ready since dawn.)*
> *(Dust, on the drive. The first carriage.)*
> *(Rose counts the way Augusta taught her: once for the sum, once for the nerve. The sum is the charter, sealed a week ago, the invitations sent by hand and answered in kind. The nerve is steady. The carriage rounds the oaks and she catches the crest, and her breath catches with it — the particular joy of a plan turning into a fact.)*
> "Miss." The boot boy, very low, eyes shining. "The first, miss."
> "The first." Rose straightens and steps forward into the morning. "The Assembly," she says, under her breath, "begins."
> *(A second carriage follows the first, and a third, and the drive comes alive the way the Park comes alive in April: all at once, the dust hanging golden, the oaks standing in their rows like an honor guard. She keeps the charter's words where she can find them as the doors swing — every guest by name, every guest by hand, as promised.)*

> *(The Assembly, the first: the convened, the real — and the house party's second morning proves it the way the Park proves the spring: completely, and without argument. The charter, the kept. The founding, the proven.)*
> *(It is real — the Assembly, the first — the convened, the kept: the breakfast tables, the Park's light, the guests in the garden, the dragon at her toast, the young on the terraces. The founding, the proven.)*
> *(The real, the proven: the Assembly, the first. The charter — the kept. And Rose walks the house — the hall, the morning room, the terrace — and the Assembly is everywhere: the convened, the real, the kept.)*
> *(Bell is there — the proprietor, the dry, the attended — with her notebook shut and her sharp eyes open, watching the house party the way the Gazette watches everything: completely. The Gazette was received. The Gazette reports. The convening is real.)*
> *(The Assembly, the first: the convened, the real. The charter, the kept. The founding, the proven. And the Season turns toward the house party's continuance: the Assembly, the annual, the real — convened, and kept, and *true*.)*
> *(The Season turns — the house party's continuance, the annual's — with the particular certainty of the charter kept: the convened, the real, the proven. The Assembly is everywhere: the breakfast tables, the Park's light, the guests in the garden.)*
> *(The Gazette reports — the proprietor, the dry, the attended — with the notebook shut and the sharp eyes open: the house party, the convened, the real. The Gazette was received. The convening is real. The Season turns toward the Assembly's continuance: the annual, the real — convened, and kept, and *true*.)*
> *(The Season turns — the continuance, the annual's, the kept — and the Assembly holds its real: the convened, the proven, the true. Convened, and kept, and *true*.)*
> *(The Season's turning settles — the continuance, the annual's, the kept — and the Assembly proves itself real: the breakfast tables, the Park's light, the dragon at her toast, the young on the terraces. The charter, the kept. The founding, the proven. Convened, and kept, and *true*.)*

scenes.synopsis: Bell's arrival report — arch, precise; reward-only, never mystery. (Turns: 1 — the reading)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning Gazette, read over chocolate. Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, in her own dry voice:)*
> *"Yesterday the Hartwell Assembly welcomed its first guests — the great houses, the young, the dragon herself — and the Gazette — having attended the welcome from the first — finds the convening real. She does not join the ton. She receives it. The Gazette was received, and reports accordingly."*
> (T1 · stance) *Rose reads it twice — the amusement first (received! accordingly!), then the reckoning: the welcome is pronounced real in print as well as in the drive's dust, and Bell has made the first guests permanent, which is Bell's way of making them history. She files the sting under its lesson: in London, the welcome the Gazette calls real is the welcome that's true.* — remembered: *the lesson: the welcome the Gazette calls real is the welcome that's true.*
scenes.sting: Yesterday the Hartwell Assembly welcomed its first guests — the great houses, the young, the dragon herself — and the Gazette — having attended the welcome from the first — finds the convening real. She does not join the ton. She receives it. The Gazette was received, and reports accordingly.

scenes.synopsis: the bloom's season — the rose through the year; the charter's flower, the turning. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, and she walks the rose garden — the bloom's season, coming — and the Hartwell rose turns through its year.)*
> *(She watches — the buds, the year's — the bloom's season, the turning: the charter's flower, through its year.)*
> "The bloom's season." She touches a bud — the year's, the turning. "The rose —" she stops — "through its year." She looks at the Park beyond — the whole, the convened. "The charter's flower —" she breathes — "the legacy, the yearly."
> *(The chapter closes on the turning — the buds, the year's — and the Season turns toward the bloom: the rose's year — and the Season holds its breath.)*
