scenes.synopsis: the years' turning — the free life's years; Julian, the free. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(She wakes before the house, which is unlike her — the household book usually gets her first — and goes to the terrace in her slippers because the morning has the particular blue of a day that intends to be fine. The stone is cold through the soles. The damp patches from the night are drying in order, dark to pale, like ink blots in reverse.)*
> *(The terrace is empty. It will not be, later — Julian walks it before she wakes now, the way other men read the paper — but the air still holds him, the way rooms hold people who have just left them. She lays her hand on the balustrade and finds the stone cold. Not his warmth. The night's.)*
> *(Below, the Park wakes in its order: the blackbird first, then the mist lifting off the hollows, then the gardener's boy with the barrow, whistling through his teeth. She watches the light come down the balustrade in a line, touching each stone in turn, and thinks about the turning of the years — not as an event, with trumpets, but as this: the light, arriving, stone by stone.)*
> *(This terrace has seen him in shadow. She does not need to name the year; the stone remembers the grip of his hand on nights when the coercion still had him by the throat. The shadow is gone from it now. What walks here in the mornings is a man of twenty-eight with his gloves in his pocket and no one's permission required.)*
> *(She thinks about the free life's years the way she thinks about everything: as an account. On one side, the shadow years — the debts, the fear, the brother's name unspoken. On the other, this: the terrace, the light, the man. The book balances. It has never balanced so quietly.)*
> *(The mist is off the hollows now. The gardener's boy has stopped whistling and started working, which is the Park's version of applause. Somewhere below, a door closes — the house beginning its day — and she knows that in an hour Julian will come up from the garden with earth on his boots and the morning in his face, and the terrace will be his again, the way it is every morning.)*
> *(The sun reaches the top of the balustrade. She takes her hand away — the stone keeps the cold a moment longer, then gives it up — and goes in to order the chocolate and open the book. The years have turned. The terrace is his. The day, like the stone, is warming.)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian, the years' — the free man, the free; the unguarded, the kept. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The breakfast room, and Julian is late — unheard of, these years — and comes in with his village coat on and his hair still damp from the pump, and pats his breast pocket twice before he sits down, the way he does. The chocolate is already poured. Rose watches the patting and says nothing. She has learned that the pocket holds its own counsel.)*
> *(He eats. He reads the Gazette's second page and snorts at it. And then, between the toast and the marmalade, he reaches into the pocket — not the pat, the reaching — and lays a folded paper on the tablecloth beside her plate. It is soft with handling, the creases gone white.)*
> *"The last of them," he says.*
> *(Rose unfolds it. A receipt, in a tradesman's hand: paid in full. The date is a fortnight past. She looks at the sum — he watches her look — and folds it again before she can do the arithmetic aloud, which is his form of mercy.)*
> *"Paid," Julian says. "All of them. Every scattered debt my brother left across three counties, paid — and before you open your mouth, Rose, with money I earned, which I am saying aloud so you cannot offer yours again. You offered in the second year. You offered in the fifth. The answer is still no, and it is still final."*
> *"I wasn't going to offer," Rose says.*
> *"You were doing the arithmetic. I could see it. The household-book look." He takes the receipt back and folds it smaller. "The sum is between me and the ironmonger. What you may know is the date, and the fact, and that I have been carrying it for a fortnight, showing it to no one, patting it like a love letter. I have been a man with a secret, and the secret was solvency."*
> *(She laughs — and the breakfast room holds the sound, chocolate and marmalade and all — and understands what the paper actually is. Not a receipt. A discharge. Ten years of his brother's debts, and the coercion they bought, and the fear that came with it — all of it, settled, quietly, in coin he earned himself.)*
> *"What does a man do," Julian asks, "with a finished arithmetic?"*
> *"He frames it," Rose says, "or he forgets it."*
> *(He considers. Then he opens the drawer of the breakfast table — the one that holds the spare spoons and the string — and lays the receipt inside, among the string. "For the mice," he says, and closes the drawer, and asks for more toast. The drawer holds its paper. The room holds its morning. The debts hold nothing any more.)*

scenes.synopsis: the mornings — Julian's; the free's, the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Market day in the town, and Julian insists on coming with the cook's list, which the cook receives with the expression of a woman who has seen this before and expects to correct it later. Rose goes along to watch. The market smells of wet wool and crushed herbs and cheese going its own way, and the noise of it — the calling, the bargaining, the scales — is the sound of the county doing its weekly arithmetic.)*
> *(Julian buys openly. That is the thing Rose keeps coming back to, because it is the whole of it: at the counter, in daylight, coins from his own purse, no shadows, no edges. The mushroom woman names her price. Julian pays it without a murmur and calls it a victory of goodwill.)*
> *"You didn't haggle," Rose says.*
> *"Haggling is a form of management. I have retired from management." He accepts the mushrooms with ceremony. "Besides, she has the look of a woman who would win."*
> *"She named the price she always names. The cook pays a penny less."*
> *"Then the cook," Julian says, with dignity, "may do the marketing. I am here for the pleasure of being overcharged in public."*
> *(The butcher's dog transfers its allegiance somewhere between the cheese stall and the egg woman — a large, judicious animal with no respect for rank — and follows Julian the length of the market, and Julian, who has never been able to resist a conversion, buys it a bone. The bone is carried with pride. The dog is converted for life.)*
> *(The town watches, kindly. A hat is tipped. The mushroom woman throws in a handful of parsley for the gentleman who pays without arguing, which Rose notes is the market's version of a compliment. Julian carries the basket — too full, badly packed, triumphant — and does not notice that he is being watched, which is how Rose knows the watching no longer troubles him.)*
> *(At home the cook unpacks the basket with the air of a general reviewing troops, and sets aside the mushrooms, and says nothing about the price, which is her form of mercy. The bone goes to the kitchen door, where the butcher's dog has followed them all the way home and waits, converted, hopeful. Julian looks at Rose. Rose looks at the ceiling.)*
> *"Keep him," she says.*
> *(The dog is kept. The mushrooms are kept. The morning — the daylight, the counter, the coins from his own purse — is kept most of all.)*

scenes.synopsis: the debts — the paid; the years', the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The paying was quiet. That is what Rose comes back to, turning it over in the study with the household book closed before her — because she never recorded his debts, not one of them; he would not permit it, and she would not have known how to enter them. The coercion's arithmetic was never hers to keep.)*
> *(She had insisted on coming for the last of it. The ironmonger's shop in the town, the bell over the door, the smell of oil and metal and coal dust. The ironmonger — a man with ink on his cuffs and thirty years of other people's debts in his book — had looked up, and recognized Julian, and reached for the ledger without being asked.)*
> *(The entry was there, in the old hand: the brother's account, scattered across the years, the small sums that had kept a younger son in chains. Julian had counted out the coin on the counter — his coin, earned, every piece of it — and the ironmonger had counted it back, and drawn a line through the entry with a steady pen, and closed the book. No scene. No witnesses but her, and the shop cat asleep on the nails.)*
> *"That," the ironmonger had said, "is the last of it." And Julian had nodded, and they had stood a moment in the shop with the bell still trembling over the door, and then they had walked out into the daylight with nothing following them.*
> *(Rose thinks about the machinery — the plot arc's phrase, the one Julian uses himself now: the machinery that makes younger sons into instruments. The debts were never about money. Money was the handle. The paying broke the handle — quietly, at a counter, in daylight. The sums were incidental.)*
> *(The ironmonger's line through the entry: that is the image she keeps. Not the coin, not the book, not the shop. The line — the pen, the ink, the steady hand drawing it through. Ten years, ended in a stroke.)*
> *(She opens the household book, and writes nothing — because there is nothing to enter, and that is the point — and closes it again. The study holds its quiet. Somewhere below, Julian is laughing at something the dog has done. The line holds. The debts hold nothing.)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian, the debts' — the free man, the paid; the gloves, the kept. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, the morning room, and the fire is doing its low work, and Julian takes the gloves from his pocket — not the pat, the taking — and lays them on the table between them the way other men lay down cards. The mending shows in the firelight: the seam at the thumb, the stitching uneven, determined, his.)*
> *(Rose picks one up. The leather is soft with years. The stitches wander — up, down, up again, like a drunk walking home.)*
> *"Yours?" she says.*
> *"Mine. The second mending." He holds out his hands: the fingers, the pricked places. "A fortnight of evenings with the housekeeper's mending basket. She supervised. She despaired. She has stopped speaking to me about it, which I take as approval."*
> *"The stitches wander."*
> *"The stitches are free. They go where they like." He takes the glove back, gently, the way other men handle letters. "They were mended in poverty, Rose. The first time — you remember the first time. Necessity, and no money for new. They are kept by choice now. There is a difference, and I intend to be particular about it."*
> *(She watches his face in the firelight — the unguarded look, the years' own — and understands that the gloves are not gloves. They are the sign. The free man's sign, kept by choice, mended by his own hand, the stitches wandering where they like.)*
> *"Show me," she says, and he takes up the housekeeper's needle — she has left it, despairing, on the mantel — and a handkerchief, and demonstrates the stitch with his tongue between his teeth, and pricks his finger, and sucks it with enormous dignity.*
> *"The free man," Rose says, "bleeds onto his own handkerchief."*
> *"The free man," Julian says, around the finger, "mends what he keeps."*
> *(She tries one on — her hand smaller, the glove loose at the fingers — and holds it up to the firelight, the mended seam showing.)*
> *"I remember the first mending," Rose says. "The shadow years. You wore them anyway, to everything, because there was nothing else."*
> *"I wore them," Julian says. "They wore me. It was a mutual arrangement." He takes the glove back — gently, the way other men handle letters — and folds the pair, the mended seam inward. "The poverty's mending was hidden. This one is done by the fire, in the open. That is the difference, and I intend to be particular about it."*
> *(The fire does its low work. The gloves go into the pocket. The pat. And Rose understands the keeping for what it is: the free man choosing, daily, what the poor man could only endure.)*

scenes.synopsis: the evenings — Julian's; the free's, the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The inn at the crossroads, and the monthly whist, and Julian goes openly — which is the thing, Rose thinks, watching him take off his coat in the inn's low room: once he would have avoided the county's eyes, taken the edges, the shadows. Now he walks in through the door like a man entering his own house.)*
> *(The room smells of ale and pipe smoke and the fire. The squire's wife deals. The cards go round. Julian plays badly — spectacularly, cheerfully badly — and loses the first rubber with the air of a man who has discovered a new talent for it.)*
> *"Strategy," he says, when the squire's wife takes the trick. "A deep strategy. Imperceptible. Even to me."*
> *(The room laughs — the easy laugh of people who have decided to like a man — and Rose, in the corner with her tea, watches the free man among the county: the laugh, the ease, the hand played wrong and owned at once. No edges. No shadows. The inn's fire on his face, and the face unguarded.)*
> *(He loses half a crown. His own money — earned, counted out in daylight at the ironmonger's counter a fortnight past — lost cheerfully across a card table. He tries to win it back. He loses more. The squire's wife, collecting, pats his hand with the particular kindness of a woman who has beaten better men.)*
> *"Another?" the squire asks.*
> *"Another," Julian says. "The strategy requires time. Like varnish. Like debt, in reverse."*
> *(The cards are dealt again. The fire does its work. And Rose understands the evening's true subject: the door he walked through, and the room he sits in, and the county that has absorbed him the way the county absorbs everything — as information, then as gossip, then as fact. The fact, now, is Julian. Free. In the open. Losing at whist, and not minding in the least.)*
> *(They walk home under the stars, and he is still explaining the strategy, and she is still laughing, and the inn's fire is still warm on the back of her neck. The half-crown is gone. The evening is kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the terrace — the free's; the years', the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(An afternoon on the terrace — open, the county come for tea, the light doing its long work on the stone — and Julian stands beside her publicly. That is the sentence Rose keeps, because it is the whole of the resolution: beside her, publicly, no longer in shadows, a man who needs no one's permission.)*
> *(The tea things are out. The talk goes round — the harvest, the roads, the price of hay — and Julian takes his part in it with the ease of a man who has nothing to hide and no reason to perform. His hand is at his side, not hidden. The gloves are in his pocket. The pat comes and goes, unremarked.)*
> *(The ton's watching, out here in the county, is the ton's watching everywhere: it watches, it absorbs, it makes fact. The fact it is making, this afternoon, is Lord Julian Ashcombe — twenty-eight, free, the debts paid, the coercion ten years gone — standing on his own terrace in his own light. The watching, for once, is kind.)*
> *(A county matron — the kind who remembers everything and forgives selectively — asks after his health with the particular kindness reserved for men who have survived things. "You look well, Lord Julian. The country agrees with you." And he answers directly, without the old deflection: "It does. I have taken to agreeing with it back." She laughs, and moves on, and the absolution is complete, and cost nothing.)*
> *"Yours," she says, of the terrace.*
> *"Ours," he corrects. "The terrace was never the point. The standing was." He looks out over the Park — the whole kept expanse, the light on it. "I stood in shadows for years, Rose. I have decided to prefer the light. It is less dramatic. The complexion benefits."*
> *(The light goes. The terrace holds them. The standing — public, unhidden, his — holds most of all.)*
> *(The county departs in its order — the carriages, the dust, the goodbyes — and the terrace empties, and the light goes long and amber across the stone. Julian's hand rests on the balustrade, unhidden, easy.)*
> *"No one's permission," Rose says.*
> *"No one's," he agrees. "It took ten years to learn the shape of the sentence. The coercion ended, and still I stood in shadows out of habit — the habit outlived the handle by years." He looks out over the Park. "The terrace was never the point, Rose. The standing was. I have decided to prefer the light."*
> *(The last carriage turns into the drive. The dust settles. The terrace holds them — the stone warm, the light going — and the standing, public, unhidden, his, holds most of all.)*

scenes.synopsis: the years — Julian's; the free's, the turned. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The orchard in autumn, and the apple harvest, and the smell of crushed apples and wasps in the sun. Julian is up the ladder with a basket, sleeves to the elbow, in daylight — the free man's labor, chosen, unperformed.)*
> *"Catch," he says, and tosses her an apple. She catches it. The juice runs down her wrist, tart enough to make her eyes water.*
> *"The years," Rose says, wiping her wrist on her skirt, "turn in orchards before they turn in men."*
> *"Everything turns in orchards first. Orchards are ahead of us in all things." He reaches for another branch. "Twenty-eight years, and I am finally useful at harvest. The younger son's education, completed late."*
> *(She watches him work — the reach, the twist, the apple dropping into the basket with the soft sound apples make — and thinks about the years as the trees: the rings, the seasons' work, the slow accretion. Twenty-eight. Twenty-five. The coercion ten years gone. The debts paid. The gloves kept by choice. The rings, counted, hold.)*
> *(A wasp investigates her wrist. She stands still — the orchard's etiquette — and it moves on, disappointed. Below, the dog is asleep in the grass with an apple core, converted and content. The ladder creaks. The basket fills.)*
> *"The free life," Julian says, from the ladder, "involves a surprising amount of fruit. No one warned me. The brochures mentioned terraces. They did not mention wasps."*
> *"The wasps are the price of the terrace."*
> *"A fair price." He climbs down, the basket full, and sets it at her feet with ceremony. "The harvest, milady. Earned. Like everything else these days."*
> *(They carry the basket between them up to the house — the weight of it, the smell of it — and the orchard holds its autumn behind them, the trees doing their slow work. The years turn. The fruit keeps. The free man, in daylight, with a basket: that is the image she keeps, going up the path.)*
> *"You did. It was adequate." He shifts his grip on the basket. "The orchard keeps the count better than I do. The rings. The fruit. The return. Twenty-eight years, and the trees are still ahead of me in all things."*
> *(At the kitchen door the basket is set down, and the cook takes it with the air of a general receiving supplies, and the dog wakes from its apple-core sleep, converted and hopeful. The orchard's work, done for the day.)*
> *(Rose looks back down the path — the trees, the ladder, the light going gold through the leaves — and keeps the image: the free man, in daylight, with a basket. The years turn. The fruit keeps.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE FREE'S LESSON (what the free teaches: the freedom, the paying, or the returning). The years deepen; decide the lesson. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The canal at the Park's edge, and Rose walks it alone — the water, the willows, the towpath going its level way. The storyboard put his resolution here, at the canal walk, and she understands why: the water keeps moving and does not apologize for it, and the free life, it turns out, is much the same.)*
> *(She has been turning the question since breakfast, the way she turns everything: as an account. The free asks its lesson. The freedom — Julian's, the free: the terrace in daylight, the man beside her publicly, no one's permission. The paying — the debts', the paid: the ironmonger's line, the coin counted out, the handle broken quietly. The returning — the years', the yearly: the mornings, repeated, the practice until it is the man.)*
> *(The lesson will shape the free's memory — not the events, the emphasis. The thing the years point to, when they point. She stops at the lock, and watches the water find its level, and does the deciding the way the free does everything now: directly, without management, freely.)*
> *(The years deepen, and the free asks its lesson: the freedom — Julian's, the free; the paying — the debts', the paid; or the returning — the years', the yearly. The lesson will shape the free's memory.)*
> *(The freedom: the free's. The paying: the paid's. The returning: the yearly's.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The free's lesson:*
- **The freedom** — *the free, taught.* The lesson is freedom — Julian's, the free. (Consequence: the lesson is the free's — but frees are lived, and the free was the paid's.)
- **The paying** — *the paid, taught.* The lesson is paying — the debts', the paid. (Consequence: the lesson is the paid's — but paids are settled, and the free was the years'.)
- **The returning** — *the yearly, taught.* The lesson is returning — the years, the yearly. (Consequence: the lesson is the yearly's — but yearly's are time's, and the free was the now.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: freedom, paying, or returning. The free's lesson is hers.)*
> *(The deciding, done. The canal does not applaud; the water merely continues, which is its form of approval. She walks back along the towpath with the lesson kept — unnamed, unannounced, hers — and the willows trail their fingers, and the moorhen, mollified, goes about its business.)*
> *(The lesson is the free's now. The years will keep it the way the canal keeps the water: by moving, steadily, in the open.)*
> *(She walks back along the towpath — the willows, the level light, the lesson kept and unnamed — and the water goes on with its unhurried arithmetic beside her.)*
> *(At the lock she finds him: on the bench, coat off, sleeves up, watching the moorhen with the particular attention he gives to small indignations. He looks up. He does not ask. The free do not ask; they wait, directly, for the telling.)*
> *(She sits beside him. The bench holds them. The water keeps its level. And the lesson — decided, kept, hers — sits between them unspoken, which is the free's way with true things — lived, from this bench forward, without announcement.)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian, the lesson's — the free man, the taught; the unguarded, the kept. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(She finds him on the bench by the lock — the canal, the willows, the water doing its level work — with his coat off and his sleeves up and the afternoon in his face. He has been watching the moorhen. He does not manage his expression when she sits down; he lets her see the whole of it.)*
> *"The free teaches," Rose says. "I've decided what."*
> *"And?"*
> *"Decided is decided. The teaching is the thing now."*
> *(He nods — the unguarded look, the years' own — and stretches his legs out, and considers the water.)*
> *"The free taught me," he says slowly, "that freedom is not the absence of the debts. It is the presence of the mornings." He glances at her. "You will say that is a thesis. It is not a thesis. It is an observation, made by a man on a bench, watching a moorhen. The debts were a handle. Someone held it for years. Then the handle broke — quietly, at a counter — and what was left was not triumph. It was Tuesday. Mornings, repeated. The terrace. The gloves. You."*
> *"The lesson," Rose says, "is taught by the living, not the deciding."*
> *"The lesson is taught by the years. I merely turn up and am taught. It is a comfortable arrangement. I recommend it."*
> *(The swan comes round the bend of the canal — vast, white, purposeful — and fixes Julian with the particular stare swans reserve for men on benches, and Julian retreats with enormous dignity to the far end of the seat.)*
> *"The free," he says, "does not extend to swans."*
> *"Noted. The charter will be amended."*
> *(They sit while the swan passes — the water, the willows, the bench — and the lesson, decided and kept between them, goes unspoken, which is the free's way with true things. His hand finds hers on the bench. The moorhen returns, indignant. The water keeps its level.)*
> *"The teaching," Julian says at last, "continues." And the canal, the bench, the afternoon, all of it holds: the lesson, kept, unannounced.*
> *"The teaching continues," he says at last. "The bench. The water. The afternoons." He glances at her. "The lesson is yours, Rose. I merely turn up and am taught. It is a comfortable arrangement — I recommend it to everyone, though the swan has declined."*
> *(She laughs — and the canal holds the sound, water and willows and all — and takes his hand on the bench, and the afternoon goes on around them: the level light, the unhurried water, the lesson kept between them like the canal keeps its level: steadily, in the open.)*

scenes.synopsis: the walks — Julian's; the free's, the walked. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(He has taken to walking without destination — the beech avenue, the copper leaves deep on the path, the lake path with the ducks in their disputatious parliament — and this morning Rose goes with him, falling in at the avenue's head the way she used to fall in beside the household book: as a matter of course.)*
> *(Once he walked to think through the coercion — the miles, the planning, the brother's debts like stones in his shoes. Now he walks to look. That is the difference, and it is the whole of the free life's years: the walk, unburdened, the ground his.)*
> *"The beeches," Julian says, "are ahead of us in all things. Like the orchard. Trees are insufferably superior."*
> *"The trees were here first."*
> *"A technicality." He kicks a copper leaf, watches it turn. "I walked this avenue for years with the fear in my pocket instead of the gloves. The fear was heavier. It chafed."*
> *(They walk on — the avenue's length, the light coming through the copper in bars — and the quiet between them is the easy quiet of people who have said everything and mean to keep saying it. The ducks hold their parliament. The heron stands in the shallows with the patience of a creditor, paid in full.)*
> *(At the lake's far turn he stops, and looks back at the house — the Park, the terraces, the whole kept ground — and does nothing. No assessment. No management. Just the look, direct, taking it in. The free man's look, kept.)*
> *"The walks," Rose says, "keep their own hours."*
> *"The walks," Julian agrees, "are free. Like the stitches. Like everything else these days, including me."*
> *(They walk back as the light goes thin, and the avenue holds the copper leaves, and the lake holds the ducks, and the walks — Julian's, the walked — keep their own hours, exactly, unhurried, his.)*
> *(At the lake's far side the ducks hold their parliament — the quacking, the disputes, the sudden unanimous flights — and the heron, disturbed, lifts with enormous dignity and goes over to the far shallows, trailing its patience.)*
> *"The walks," Julian says, "keep their own hours. The avenue at nine. The lake at ten. The ducks, perpetual." He falls into step beside her. "Once I walked to outrun the fear. Now I walk to keep up with the morning. The morning is faster."*
> *(They take the avenue home — the copper leaves, the light in bars, the easy quiet — and the walks go on keeping their hours around them, unhurried, his: the beech avenue, the lake path, the ground, the free man's, walked.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Assembly — Julian's; the convened, the free man's. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The county Assembly, and Julian attends openly — no edges, no shadows, no taking the wall where the light doesn't reach. He walks in through the doors like a man entering his own house, and the county, being the county, watches.)*
> *(The watching is the thing Rose attends to, with the attention she once gave to money: noting where it lands, what it buys. It buys the truth, kept. The ton watched the coercion's shadow for years; now it watches the free man, and the watching — absorbed as information, then as gossip, then as fact — is kind.)*
> *(He dances — with her, publicly, the first dance, no hiding of it. The music, the candles, the county turning. His hand at her waist is steady. The mended gloves are in his pocket; the pat comes and goes between dances, unremarked. The county's verdict, overheard near the punch: "Lord Julian looks well." The simplicity of it is the absolution.)*
> *(Later, in the carriage home, he is quiet — the good quiet, the free man's kind. The candles of the Assembly are still warm on the back of her neck.)*
> *"The Assembly," Rose says.*
> *"The Assembly," Julian says, "was adequate. I danced. I was watched. The watching was kind. The gloves" — the pat — "were present throughout." He takes her hand in the dark of the carriage. "The free man, Rose, dances in public now. It is less dramatic than the shadows. The steps are easier."*
> *(The carriage turns into the drive. The Assembly holds its candles behind them. The dancing — public, unhidden, his — is kept.)*
> *(The supper room, later — the punch, the talk, the county doing its evening arithmetic — and Julian is surrounded, unguarded, at ease: the squire on the harvest, the matron on the roads, the punch doing its sweet work.)*
> *(Rose watches from the doorway with the attention she once gave to money: noting where his look lands, what it buys. It buys the truth, kept. Every time. The county has absorbed him — as information, then as gossip, then as fact — and the fact, now, is the free man, dancing, supping, at home.)*
> *(In the carriage home he takes her hand in the dark, and the candles of the Assembly stay warm on the back of her neck all the way up the drive. The dancing — public, unhidden, his — is kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the toasts — Julian's; the free's, the raised. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(A dinner, and the toasts, and the house has decided — without deciding, the way houses do — that Julian shall give one. He demurs. Augusta, at the table's head, raises one eyebrow, which is her form of insistence. He rises.)*
> *(The dining room holds its candles. The company holds its wine. And Julian — twenty-eight, free, the debts paid, the gloves in his pocket — looks round the table with the unguarded look, and gives the shortest toast of the Season.)*
> *"To debts, paid," he says. "To gloves, kept. To mornings, continued."*
> *(He sits down. The table drinks. Someone — the squire, emboldened by the claret — calls for more: "A longer one, Lord Julian!" And Julian, with the old charm entirely unperformed, says: "Brevity is the soul of solvency, sir. I have learned to be brief about everything except whist, at which I am at length." The table laughs, and drinks again, and the toast goes round.)*
> *(Rose watches him — the directness, the ease, the hand around the glass steady — and understands that the toasts are not toasts. They are a ledger, the free man's: everything named, everything kept. Debts, paid. Gloves, kept. Mornings, continued. The account, balanced, read aloud.)*
> *(Much later, the candles burned low, she finds him at the window with the last of the wine, looking out at the dark parkland.)*
> *"The toasts," he says. "They were —" he searches — "sufficient."*
> *"Sufficient," Rose agrees, "is the highest praise the free man has."*
> *(He smiles — the smile, no ghost in it — and sets down the empty glass, and the candlelight stays in it a moment after the wine is gone, like the toast staying in the room after the words.)*
> *(The toasts go round — the table, the candles, the claret — and Augusta, at the head, gives him the dry look over her glass: approval, from Augusta, which is rarer than the claret.)*
> *"Brevity," Augusta says, "is the soul of solvency. I shall have it engraved."*
> *"On the gloves," Julian suggests. "There is room, between the stitches."*
> *(The table laughs — the easy laugh of people who have decided — and the talk goes on, and the candles burn lower, and Rose watches the free man's ledger being read aloud in toasts: debts, paid; gloves, kept; mornings, continued. Everything named. Everything kept.)*
> *(Much later, at the window with the last of the wine, he says it again, quieter, for her alone: "To mornings, continued." And the dark parkland holds the toast, and the candlelight stays in the empty glass, like the words staying in the room.)*

scenes.synopsis: the night — Julian's; the free's, the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The house at night, and Rose walks the corridor with the candle, the way she does when the book won't close in her head. The doors are shut. The house settles — the particular quiet of a place that has done its day's work and means to rest.)*
> *(His door is shut. The light is out — dark by eleven, these years. She stands a moment in the corridor with the candle, and thinks about the contrast the way she thinks about everything: as an account. Then: the lamp burned late, the letters dreaded, the listening for knocks that never came in the right rhythm. Now: the dark, the quiet, the rest.)*
> *(The quiet of a man with no debts. That is the sentence she keeps, because it is the whole of the night's proof. No one holds a handle any more. No brother's name unspoken in the dark. No coercion with its hand on his throat. The free man's rest — his, the kept.)*
> *(The dog snores in the corridor, converted and dreaming. Somewhere below, a stair creaks — the house's old bones. She holds the candle higher, and the flame steadies, and the corridor holds its shadows, and the shadows are only shadows now: the house's, not his.)*
> *(She does not knock. There is nothing to say that the morning won't say better. She walks on, and the candle goes with her, and the door stays shut on the dark beyond it — the rest, the kept, the free.)*
> *(In her own room she sets the candle down, and listens a moment to the house — the settling, the quiet, the kept — and blows it out. The night is his. The rest is his. The free, kept, even in the dark.)*
> *(She passes Letitia's door — the light still on, the murmur of a book — and the stairs, and the landing window with the Park dark beyond it. The house at night is a kept thing: the doors shut, the fires banked, the dog dreaming in the corridor.)*
> *(Below, the kitchen cat crosses the hall on its night business, tail high, unconcerned. The stair creaks in the old place. The candle flames lean, then steady.)*
> *(She thinks about the listening — the years of it, the ear cocked for knocks, the letters turned over before opening. The free man's house does not listen any more. It rests. The doors are shut on the dark, and the dark is only the dark.)*
> *(In her room she sets the candle down, and the flame stands straight, and the house settles around her — the particular quiet of a day that has done its work. The night is his. The rest is his. The free, kept, even in the dark.)*

scenes.synopsis: the later years — Julian's; the free's, the deepened. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Winter, and the hothouse — the warmth hitting her face as she opens the door, the green smell, the condensation running down the glass in slow lines. Outside, the Park is white. Inside, it is June, and Julian is in his shirtsleeves with the secateurs.)*
> *(His rose. The hothouse rose — his route's emblem since the first flower-message, the sign he chose when choosing was still dangerous. He tends it himself now: the watering, the feeding, the tying-in. Badly at first — the housekeeper's despair extended to horticulture — then all at once well.)*
> *"The later years," Julian says, not looking up from the tying, "deepen the way varnish deepens. Or gardens. Not by event. By tending." He tests the twine. "I am become a man who talks to roses. The ton would be appalled. The roses are not. They find me" — he considers — "adequate."*
> *(Rose watches him work — the hands, the twine, the earth under the nails — and understands what the deepening actually is. Not a second unmasking, not a new event. The old freedom, lived in. The terrace in daylight was the arrival. This — the hothouse, the rose, the daily tending — is the residence.)*
> *(He cuts a bloom — the secateurs, the clean cut, the thorns avoided with the respect of a man who has learned — and wraps the stem, and holds it out. The hothouse rose, out of season, the free's sign.)*
> *"For the morning room," he says. "The free deepens. The rose concurs."*
> *(She takes it — the bloom, the green smell, the winter outside the glass — and the hothouse holds its warmth around them, and the later years go on deepening, unremarked, the way gardens do: by tending, daily, kept.)*
> *(In the morning room the bloom goes into a glass on the table, and the red of it sits against the winter light, and the house holds the sign all day: the rose, the kept, the deepened.)*
> *(By evening the household has adopted the bloom — the footman moves the glass to catch the breakfast light, unasked, the way houses take omens to themselves and then pretend the idea was theirs all along.)*
> *"The later years," Julian says, coming in with the cold on him, "are the residence. The rose concurs." He looks at the bloom in its glass. "Out of season, and unapologetic. I am teaching it freedom. It is teaching me tending."*
> *(The house holds the sign all day: the rose, the kept, the deepened. The winter goes on with its white work outside. Inside, it is June, and the free man's rose, and the later years.)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian, the later's — the free man, the deepened; the unguarded, the kept. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(She finds him in the hothouse at noon — the heat, the green, the condensation — with his hands in the soil of the rose bed and his coat hung on the door peg, sleeves to the elbow, unperformed.)*
> *"The later years," Rose says, from the door.*
> *"The later years," Julian agrees, sitting back on his heels, "are the habitation. The terrace in daylight was the arrival. This" — he gestures with the trowel — "is the residence. The watering. The tying. The talking, which the roses pretend not to need."*
> *"What does the free teach?" she asks. "Now. In the later years."*
> *(He considers, the trowel still. Outside the glass, the snow goes on with its white work.)*
> *"The years don't forgive," he says at last. "They accrete. Like varnish. Like debt, in reverse — the paying, compounded. The lesson I was given" — the unguarded look — "was the freedom. The lesson I am learning is the keeping. The rose does not bloom by intending it. It blooms by being tended, daily, in the heat, in the cold. The free is a horticultural matter, Rose. No one told me. I am telling you."*
> *"The lesson is mine to decide," she says.*
> *"The lesson is yours. I merely turn up and am deepened. It is a comfortable arrangement." He goes back to the soil. "The face improves with tending. Like the rose. Like everything kept."*
> *"Varnish," Rose says. "Debt, in reverse. You are full of ledgers today."*
> *"I am a man of accounts. The paying taught me. Ten years of arithmetic leaves its mark — on the fingers, like the soil." He holds up his hands: the earth, the pricked places from the rose's opinions. "The free deepens the way a garden does, Rose. Not by event. By tending. I am become a man who talks to roses, and the roses, unlike the ton, listen."*
> *(She laughs — and the hothouse holds the sound, green and warm — and understands that the teaching is not solitary. The tending has witnesses. The keeping is shared. The later years deepen around them, unremarked, the way gardens do.)*
> *"Adequate," Julian says, standing back from the bed, surveying the tied stems.*
> *"Adequate," Rose agrees, "is sufficient." And the hothouse holds its June in the middle of winter, and the deepening goes on, tended, kept.*

scenes.synopsis: the unguarded look — Julian's; the ghost's, the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Rain at the window, and the morning room, and Rose studies his face across the papers — the way she used to study the household book, for what it would tell her. The look: watchful, calculating, charming. That was the old inventory.)*
> *(The new inventory: the watchfulness has become attention. The calculation is gone — nothing left to calculate, the debts paid, the handle broken. The charm is unperformed now, which makes it, paradoxically, more charming. The ghost of the old smile has become the smile. There is no ghost left.)*
> *(He reads — the Gazette, the second page — and frowns at something, and the frown is unguarded, and then he looks up and catches her studying, and does not manage his expression. He lets her see the whole of it: the amusement, the warmth, the twenty-eight years sitting easy.)*
> *"The inventory," he says.*
> *"The look," Rose corrects. "The unguarded. Kept."*
> *"And the verdict?"*
> *(She considers him — the rain on the glass behind him, the papers before him, the face — and gives the verdict the way the free gives everything: directly.)*
> *"It tells," she says. "It always told. Now it is allowed."*
> *(He holds her look — steady, unflinching, the kept man's — and the morning room holds its rain, and the look goes on telling, allowed, believed. The old look deflected. This one arrives, daily, and stays.)*
> *(He goes back to the Gazette. She goes back to the studying. The rain does its work on the glass. The look — Julian's, the unguarded, the kept — holds the morning the way the terrace holds the light: completely, without announcement.)*
> *"The look," Rose says, when the laughing stops. "I am still inventorying it."*
> *"The unguarded. Kept." He sets the paper down. "And the verdict, revised?"*
> *(She studies him — the rain behind, the papers before, the face — and gives it the way the free give everything: directly, without management.)*
> *"It tells," she says. "It always told — the watchful, the calculating, the charm. Now the watchfulness is attention, and the calculation is gone, and the charm is unperformed. The ghost of the old smile has become the smile. There is no ghost left."*
> *(The rain steadies on the glass. Below, the house goes about its morning — the stairs, the voices, the ordinary machinery — and the telling goes on between them, allowed, believed, with the weather for company.)*
> *(She goes back to the book. He goes back to the Gazette. The rain does its work on the glass, and the morning room keeps its counsel — the pages turning, the kept, the rain.)*

scenes.synopsis: the pocket — Julian's; the gloves', the kept. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The habit: two fingers, the breast pocket, the pat. He does it without thinking — in the village, at the market, on the terrace — the way other men check for a watch. The check, the nod to himself, the walk continuing.)*
> *(At the Assembly he patted an empty pocket and went pale. Rose watched it happen across the room: the pat, the absence, the stillness. The gloves were in the other coat — the evening coat, the pocket he forgets. She crossed the room, unhurried, and told him, and the relief on his face was the relief of a man who has lost something that cannot be replaced, and then remembered it can only be mislaid.)*
> *"The panic," Julian said afterward, in the carriage, "was disproportionate. They are gloves. Mended gloves. The stitches wander."*
> *"The panic," Rose said, "was the keeping, showing."*
> *(He has not forgotten the evening coat since. The habit is the free man's tell: other men carry watches, seals, letters of credit. He carries the kept — the mended gloves, the sign — and checks for them the way other men check for the time. The time, for him, is kept in the pocket.)*
> *(She watches him do it on the terrace — the pat, the nod — and understands that the habit is not anxiety. It is the opposite. It is the free man's version of prayer: the kept, confirmed, carried. The pocket holds the sign. The sign holds the man.)*
> *(Two fingers. The breast pocket. The pat. The nod. The walk, continuing, in daylight, in the open — the keeping, carried, kept.)*
> *(In the village he does it at the ironmonger's counter — the pat, the nod — and the ironmonger, who has seen the line drawn through the old account, nods back — a man who knows what the pocket holds.)*
> *(At the market he does it between the cheese stall and the egg woman, and the mushroom woman says: "The gloves still with you, my lord?" And he says: "Still with me. Still kept." And she throws in the parsley, which is the market's version of a benediction.)*
> *(The dog has learned the pat — the two fingers, the pocket — and sits when Julian does it, expecting the bone that sometimes follows. The habit has propagated. The keeping is contagious.)*
> *"The pocket," Rose says, walking home, "holds its own counsel."*
> *"The pocket," Julian agrees, "holds the sign. The sign holds the man. The man" — the pat — "holds the pocket. It is a closed system. Like the household book, but warmer."*
> *(At the gate he does it once more — the two fingers, the pocket, the pat — and Rose sees the ritual's second half: the nod, the walk, the daylight. The keeping, carried outward.)*

scenes.synopsis: the gloves — the mended; the kept by choice, the forever. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(By the fire, and the needle, and his tongue between his teeth — the second mending, by choice. The seam at the thumb has worn thin again, the leather giving way where the hand works hardest, and Julian sits with the glove in his lap and the housekeeper's needle and does the mending himself.)*
> *(The stitches wander — up, down, up again. He follows the seam with enormous concentration, the firelight on his hands, the thread catching.)*
> *"You could let her do it," Rose says, from her chair. "The housekeeper. Before she despairs entirely."*
> *"The first mending was poverty," Julian says, not looking up. "Necessity, and no money for new. This one is affection. The stitches know the difference." The needle goes in. Comes out. Wanders. "She despaired in the fortnight. She has stopped speaking to me about it. I take it as approval."*
> *(Rose watches — the fire, the hands, the wandering stitches — and thinks about the kept by choice. Not the poverty's mending, hidden. The choice's mending, done in the open, by the fire, badly and proudly. The free man's press: not a press at all. A keeping, in the fingers.)*
> *"The free man," she says, "bleeds onto his own glove."*
> *"The free man," Julian says, around the finger, "mends what he keeps. It is the whole of the philosophy. I am having it engraved."*
> *(He ties off the thread — the knot, the bite of the teeth on it — and holds up the glove. The seam holds. The stitches wander, triumphant.)*
> *(He folds the gloves — the mended seam inward, the way she taught him before she despaired — and lays them on the table. The fire does its low work. The mending, done. The kept, by choice, forever.)*
> *"She supervised the first mending," he says. "The poverty's. Necessity, and no money for new. She wept, I think — or despaired; with her it is the same expression. This one she will not supervise. This one is mine."*
> *(The fire settles. The mending goes on — slow, wandering, his — and Rose thinks about the difference the years made: the poor man's sewing hid itself, and the free man's shows. The seam, visible, by the fire, in the open.)*
> *(The glove is held to the firelight and passes inspection — his own, which is stricter than the housekeeper's ever was — and the wandering stitches are pronounced adequate, which from Julian is the highest praise there is.)*
> *(The gloves rest on the table between them, and the fire does its low work on the leather, and the evening asks nothing more of either of them. The mending done. The keeping kept. The day complete.)*

scenes.synopsis: the lesson — the freedom, the paying, the returning; the kept's. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The study at night, and the candle low, and the book open. Rose turns to the margin — the last clean one — and writes the lesson's three faces in her fine hand: the freedom, the paying, the returning. And under them, the chosen: the lesson, kept.)*
> *(She does not name it on the page. The page holds the keeping, not the choosing. The choosing was the canal's; the keeping is the book's. She looks at the three words — freedom, paying, returning — and turns over what the lesson asks of the living.)*
> *(Not gratitude. Gratitude is the ton's currency, spent in drawing rooms. Not triumph — triumph is the Gazette's, printed and filed. The lesson asks the keeping. The practice, daily. The terrace, walked. The gloves, mended. The mornings, continued. The lesson, lived until the practice is the man.)*
> *(The candle gutters. The house is quiet — the particular quiet of a night that has done its work. She thinks about the free's teaching: that the face was always sufficient, that the handle could be broken, that the years, turned through, deepen. The lesson, kept, asks only to be kept on.)*
> *(She blots the margin — the ink, the three words, the kept — and closes the book. The study holds its dark. The lesson holds its keeping. The years, deepened, hold the rest.)*
> *(Upstairs, the house sleeps. The free sleeps. The lesson, kept in the margin, keeps its own counsel till morning.)*
> *(The candle burns lower. The house is quiet — the particular quiet of a night that has done its keeping. She looks at the three words in the margin — freedom, paying, returning — and under them the kept, unnamed.)*
> *(The freedom: the terrace in daylight, the man beside her publicly, no one's permission. The paying: the ironmonger's line, the coin counted out, the handle broken quietly. The returning: the mornings, repeated, the practice until it is the man. Three faces. One lesson. The lesson, kept.)*
> *(She turns over what the keeping asks: the continuation — the terrace walked tomorrow, the gloves mended again when they wear, the mornings kept. The lesson is a practice. The practice is the man.)*
> *(The candle gutters, flares, steadies. She blots the margin — the ink, the three words, the kept — and closes the book, and the study holds its dark around her.)*
> *(The candle gutters. The margin holds the lesson till morning — and the morning, Rose knows, will keep it the way mornings keep everything: by arriving, ordinary and unanswerable.)*

The keeping — the free's, the kept: the practice, daily, the mornings continued. Three candidates. One marking. The marking will shape the free man's memory — not the events, the emphasis.)*
> *(Below, in the kitchen garden, Julian is at the roses with the secateurs — unaware, unperformed, the sun on his back. He does not know he is being considered. That is as it should be. The marking is hers to decide; the receiving will be his.)*

> *(The marking, decided. The sundial keeps its shadow. The garden keeps its counsel. And Rose walks back up to the house with the years pointed — the terrace, the gloves, or the keeping, whichever was chosen — and the pointing holds, the way the sundial's shadow holds: steadily, in the open.)*
> *(The garden keeps its counsel — the box-edged paths, the roses, the noon. Rose walks back up to the house with the marking decided, and the years pointed, and the sundial's shadow steady behind her.)*

scenes.synopsis: the marking — the gift, the given; Julian, the marked. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The marking is not announced — so Rose sets it down the way true things are set down: directly, where the years can find it, without ceremony.)*
> *(If the terrace was chosen — the free's, the ground — then the marking is the walking: she walks it at dawn, deliberately, the length of it, and the walking is the marking. The ground, his. The standing, public. The marking, kept in the feet.)*
> *(If the gloves were chosen — the mended's, the kept by choice — then the marking is the taking up: she takes them from the table where he left them, and folds them, the mended seam inward, and the folding is the marking. The sign, his. The keeping, chosen. The marking, kept in the hand.)*
> *(If the keeping was chosen — the free's, the kept — then the marking is the day itself: she keeps it exactly — the chocolate, the book, the walk, the evening — and the keeping is the marking. The practice, his. The mornings, continued. The marking, kept in the hours.)*
> *(Whichever was chosen — the terrace, the gloves, or the keeping — the marking is done the same way: directly, in the open, where the years walk. Julian watches — the unguarded look, the understanding — and knows, because the free know these things, that the marking is a direction, not a decoration. The years, pointed.)*
> *(She writes it in the household book, in the margin: "The marking, set down." She looks at the line, and adds, because she is precise: "The years, pointed." She blots it.)*
> *(The marking is done. And the years — Julian's, the marked — receive it the way the garden receives the noon: completely, without announcement. The afternoon light dries the ink. The pointing holds.)*
> *(The afternoon goes on — the light on the page, the ink drying — and Julian comes up from the garden with the secateurs and the sun on him, and sees the book open, and the margin, and understands without being told.)*
> *"The marking," he says.*
> *"The marking. Set down."*
> *(He nods — the unguarded look, the receiving — and does not ask which; the marking is the given's, and the given is hers, and the receiving is his. He puts the secateurs down, and does the pat — the pocket, the gloves — and the afternoon holds them both.)*
> *(She looks at the two lines a moment — the marking, the years — and closes the book on them. The ink dries. The marking is done.)*
> *(The light goes gold on the page. The afternoon deepens. And the years — Julian's, the marked — go on, pointed, into the evening.)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian, the marking — the free man, the years'; the unguarded, the moved. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(The lane back from the village, and the hedgerows high, and the evening coming down in its blue order. Rose has the marking done — decided, set down, kept — and Julian walks beside her with the dog, unknowing, and she tells him the way the free tell everything: directly, walking.)*
> *"The years," she says. "Marked."*
> *(He stops walking. The dog stops. The hedgerows hold their evening.)*
> *"The marked," Julian says. "Is that like the landed, but cheaper?"*
> *"The marking is the given's. The given is the years'. The years —" she looks at him — "are yours."*
> *(The deflection dies — she watches it die, the old charm laying itself down — and what is left is the rarest thing: the man, moved. He stands in the lane with the evening round him, and does not manage his expression, and lets her see the whole of it.)*
> *"The marking," he says slowly, "is the given's. The given —" his look does not waver — "the given is yours, Rose. I am merely the marked. It is" — he searches — "a fair arrangement. The best I have ever made, and I have made them all."*
> *(His hand finds the gate — the field gate, the iron cold under his palm — and holds it, and the evening goes on around them: the hedgerows, the rooks, the dog sitting down to wait out the emotion with the patience of long practice.)*
> *"Moved," Rose says. "Is that the whole of the report?"*
> *"That is the report." He holds the gate, and her look. "In the lane. That is the receiving, and it is enough."*
> *(They walk on — the lane, the evening, the marking between them — and the dog goes ahead, converted and purposeful, and the hedgerows hold their blue.)*
> *"The receiving," Julian says, "is the harder part. The giving — you do the giving directly, without management. The receiving" — he looks at her — "the receiving has to be learned. I am still learning it. Ten years of the handle taught me to take nothing freely. The free man's education, completed late."*
> *(The gate swings shut behind them. The lane goes on. And Rose understands the marking's moving for what it is: a receiving, practiced like everything else — the terrace, the mornings, the kept.)*
> *"You are learning," she says.*
> *"I am learning," he agrees. "Adequately. The lane is my schoolroom. You are" — the unguarded look — "a demanding teacher."*
> *(They walk home as the dark comes down. The lane keeps its blue. The learning continues.)*

scenes.synopsis: Julian, the marked — the free man's, the years'; the kept, the forever. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(The harvest supper in the village, and the long tables in the barn, and the lanterns, and the smell of roast and straw and cider. Julian sits among the tenants — not at the head, not apart, among — with the marking worn like his coat: easily, unremarked.)*
> *(The toasts of the village go round — the harvest, the weather, the squire's health — and when they come to him, he rises with his cider and gives them the short one: "To debts, paid. To gloves, kept. To mornings, continued." The barn roars. The cider goes round again. The free man, marked, among his own.)*
> *(Rose watches from the table's end — the lanterns on his face, the laugh, the ease — and the marked's record keeps itself: the village does not know the story's shape; it knows the man's. That is enough. That was always enough.)*
> *(The fiddler starts. The benches are pushed back. Julian dances — badly, cheerfully, the whist strategy applied to reels — and the village laughs with him, not at him, which is the county's highest honor. The dog, under the table, sleeps through it all, converted and dreaming.)*
> *(Across the tables, through the lantern light and the cider steam, he raises his glass to her — the marked, unhidden, among his own.)*
> *(She raises hers back. The barn holds the harvest and the music and the marking, all of it, and the years — Julian's, the marked — go on deepening, unremarked, the way harvests do.)*
> *(The fiddler plays faster — the reels, the stamping, the barn's old boards — and Julian dances with the squire's wife, and then with the blacksmith's daughter, and then, breathless, with Rose, with the same cheerful incompetence and identical results.)*
> *(The cider goes round. The lanterns smoke. The village does its harvest arithmetic — the yield, the weather, the winter ahead — and the free man sits among it, marked, at home: the laugh, the ease, the glass raised.)*
> *"To the harvest," he says, when the toasts come round again. "To the barns. To the winter, when it comes." The barn roars. The marking, worn like his coat, needs no announcing.)*
> *(Rose watches from the bench — the lanterns, the dancing, the kept — and the village's knowing is the right kind: the man's shape, not the story's. The record needs no other keeping.)*
> *(They walk home under the stars, the fiddler's last tune following them up the lane, and the harvest supper holds its lanterns behind them. The marked, the kept, among his own — the record, lived.)*

scenes.synopsis: the free, the eternal — Julian's; the kept, the forever. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:

> *"The free life," Julian says.*
> *"The free life," Rose agrees. "Kept."*
> *(The sun reaches the top of the balustrade. The mist lifts. And the years — Julian's, the kept — go on ahead of them, the terrace, the daylight, the whole kept ground: the legacy, the freedom, the forever, lived.)*
> *(They walk the terrace's length again — slower now, the mist thinning — and the stone is warm underfoot where the sun has found it, and the morning does its ordinary business around them.)*
> *(The terrace takes the morning sun full in the face — stone, light, the two of them — and the legacy is there in the standing: the debts paid, the gloves kept by choice, the man beside her, public, in daylight, needing no one's permission.)*
> *(At the balustrade they stop again — the Park below, the mist gone, the day begun — and Julian does the pat, the pocket, the gloves, and Rose does not say anything at all.)*
> *(The blackbird begins its territorial audit of the morning. The mist lifts off the hollows. And the years go on ahead of them — the terrace, the daylight, the free life — and Rose understands, finally, that this is the whole of it. A life.)*
> *(They stand a while — the morning, the Park, the kept — and the legacy holds: the freedom, the charter, the forever, lived as a practice, continued, in the open.)*
> *(The mist lifts. The day begins. The free life, whole, goes on.)*

scenes.synopsis: Bell's free report — arch, precise; reward-only, never mystery. (Turns: 1 — the reading)
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning Gazette, read over chocolate. Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, in her own dry voice:)*
> *"The free man, then — free in the only sense that matters, which is to say free of the war and free to the keeping. The Gazette has watched men mistake freedom for escape for ten seasons, and finds this one satisfactory: he stayed. What is kept by choice is kept twice."*
> (T1 · stance) *Rose reads it twice — the amusement first, then the reckoning: the free life pronounced satisfactory in print, and Bell has made it permanent, which is Bell's way of making it forever. She files the sting under its lesson: in London, the freedom the Gazette watches is the freedom he chose — the staying, not the escape.* — remembered: *the lesson: the freedom the Gazette watches is the freedom he chose — the staying, not the escape.*
